title: Keep WebGPU selected and remove automatic Canvas fallbacks
description: Prevents automatic Canvas rendering when WebGPU is selected, ensuring that unsupported scenes display an error until GPU support is fixed or the user explicitly selects Canvas.
body:
Selecting WebGPU currently lets initialization failures, unsupported geometry, GPU device loss, or older X-Ray support silently mount the Canvas renderer. A board with unsupported breakout-point metadata can therefore enter the expensive Canvas path despite WebGPU being selected.

Keep WebGPU selected throughout these cases. Display the renderer failure and release its worker, or show an unsupported-X-Ray notice while retaining the GPU view. Canvas remains available through an explicit rendering-engine selection. Also use an event listener for worker message errors and prevent duplicate worker termination after failure.

Update the documentation and integration checks to assert that failures never mount Canvas, failed workers are released, manual Canvas selection still works, and unsupported X-Ray keeps the GPU canvas visible.

Validation:
- `bun run build` and `tsc --noEmit` pass.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Built-bundle browser checks via the in-app browser passed for unavailable WebGPU, unsupported geometry, worker errors, message errors, simulated device loss, startup timeout, unsupported X-Ray, and explicit Canvas selection after failure.
- The automated WebGPU runner was updated but not executed locally; its large-board performance and StrictMode checks remain unverified in this run.

This prevents automatic Canvas rendering; unsupported scenes now show an error until their GPU support is fixed or the user explicitly selects Canvas. It does not establish that every cause of the reported Chrome hang has been resolved.

title: Add source_runtime_error for circuit generation failures
description: Add source_runtime_error to represent an unexpected failure while generating or validating a circuit, allowing consumers to distinguish incomplete validation from a clean circuit.
body:
A DRC checker can throw before returning its design-rule diagnostics. Consumers currently cannot distinguish incomplete validation from a clean circuit by inspecting Circuit JSON.

Add `source_runtime_error` to represent an unexpected failure while generating or validating a circuit, with only required `message` and optional `phase_name` beyond the standard type, ID, and error_type fields. This is distinct from a design-rule violation. Export the schema/input/interface and register it in `any_circuit_element`.

Validation: all 397 tests pass; package build and TypeScript check pass. The new test verifies JSON round-trip through the union and required message and optional phase.

Core will use this to preserve a rendered circuit and successful DRC results while serializing failed check groups. This complements https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5018, which guards against unreported asynchronous failures.

title: Infer pin 1 orientation for numbered straight pad rows
description: Extends the existing analyzers two-pad convention to infer pin 1 orientation for longer straight pad rows with unique, consecutive pin numbers, resolving supplier placement preparation failures.
body:
`analyzePcbPin1Location` could infer a canonical orientation for a two-pad line, but returned null for longer straight rows. A routed JST PH J1 has pins 1–4 from -X to +X, while JLCPCB C131334 runs from +X to -X. The missing orientation caused supplier placement preparation to fail and let a permissive PnP export keep 90° instead of the needed 270°.

Extend the existing analyzer's two-pad convention to straight rows with unique, consecutive pin numbers in physical order. This lets the authored and supplier footprints compare consistently and reveals the 180° reversal. Ambiguous or nonmonotonic rows remain unresolved; other multi-row footprints keep the existing behavior. The fix uses plated-hole pad geometry, not CAD model rotation or a part-specific offset.

Tests cover the actual J1 and C131334 pad coordinates, all right-angle combinations, and ambiguous numbering. Validation: `bun test` (139 passing, 599 assertions, 4 snapshots), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, `bun run format:check`, and `git diff --check` pass. All GitHub checks pass. The package manifest has one formatting-only change because the repository-wide format check rejected its existing array layout.

This shared analyzer change supersedes the closed [PnP PR #22](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-pnp-csv/pull/22). After release, the PnP package needs to update its utility dependency and retain a J1 regression. The CLI export path also needs to prepare supplier orientation metadata for prebuilt Circuit JSON.

title: Add dogbone autorouter preset
description: Add dogbone as a recognized autorouter preset in the props types and schemas, enabling support for local pad-to-via escapes without boundary routing.
body:
`dogbone` is not currently a recognized autorouter preset in the closed props types and schemas. Add it to `AutorouterPreset`, `AutorouterConfig.preset`, and both Zod schemas so `<fanout autorouter="dogbone" />` and `{ preset: "dogbone" }` are supported by the shared props API.

Document local pad-to-via intent and regenerate the required docs. The existing fanout default remains unchanged. This provides the props prerequisite for core's dogbone implementation; routing support is tracked in https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4232.

Validation: all 573 tests pass; typecheck and build pass; all four required documentation generators ran; changed TypeScript files pass Biome formatting and the staged diff passes whitespace checks. The new test covers the closed preset/config schemas, shared autorouter parser, breakout/fanout and autorouting-phase schemas, and unchanged default.

title: Add model string props to assembly elements
description: Add model to assembly.device, assembly.screen, assembly.subassembly, and assembly.cadassembly so authors can supply a modelprinterfootprinter string directly, such as modelsoic8 or modelflexscreen_w26.7mm_h19.26mm_sitsflat.
body:
Add `model` to assembly.device, assembly.screen, assembly.subassembly, and assembly.cadassembly so authors can supply a modelprinter/footprinter string directly, such as `model="soic8"` or `model="flexscreen_w26.7mm_h19.26mm_sitsflat"`.

The optional string is trimmed and rejects empty/non-string values. It conflicts with modelUrl and, where supported, cadModel (including null). A screen with model does not require dimensions; existing paired positive dimension validation is preserved. No model defaults or URL expansion are added to the props schema. Existing modelUrl and cadModel behavior is unchanged.

Validation: all 572 tests pass, typecheck/build/format check pass, and all four required generation scripts were run. Core rendering is a dependent PR.

title: Add modelUrl props to assembly elements
description: Add optional modelUrl to assembly.device, assembly.screen, assembly.subassembly, and its assembly.cadassembly alias, allowing direct import of models without supplying dimensions or a modelprinter string.
body:
Add optional `modelUrl` to `assembly.device`, `assembly.screen`, `assembly.subassembly`, and its `assembly.cadassembly` alias. Authors can import a model directly with `<assembly.screen name="display" connectsTo=".B1 .J1" modelUrl="/display.glb" />` without supplying dimensions or a modelprinter string.

URLs use the existing asset URL parser, including imported asset defaults, and reject blank values. On screens and subassemblies, `modelUrl` conflicts with `cadModel` (including null) instead of choosing one silently. Existing dimension pairing/positivity checks and model-less containers remain unchanged. Core rendering support is a separate dependent change.

Validation: all 570 tests pass; typecheck, package build and format check pass. Ran all four required generation scripts and included generated changes.

title: Add schSize to diode and LED props
description: Adds schSize to diode and LED props using the existing SchematicSymbolSize API, enabling typed JSX for compact symbols.
body:
Adds `schSize` to diode and LED props using the existing `SchematicSymbolSize` API. This enables typed JSX such as `<diode schSize="sm" />`, `<diode zener schSize="xs" />`, and `<led schSize="sm" />` for the compact symbols introduced in tscircuit/schematic-symbols#483.

The prop is optional, with no new default or aliases. It accepts `sm`, `xs`, `default`, `md`, and existing distance inputs. Named sizes are preserved; distance inputs normalize to millimeters. Also checks named sizes before distance parsing and rejects nonfinite results, preventing the shared schema from turning `sm` into NaN with older circuit-json versions.

Generated component types and documentation are updated. Validation: all 568 tests, package build, TypeScript, and formatting pass. Core symbol selection is implemented in the dependent draft https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4216.

title: Skip slow AM62L orbit tests and balance CI shards by runtime
description: Skip the three AM62L LPDDR4 northsouthwest orbit routing regressions, which each take roughly 34 minutes. Keep their fixtures and snapshots for re-enabling. The AM62L direct-decoupling regression and other orbit tests continue to run. Balance every discovered test file longest-first across ten shards using measured CI runtimes. Refresh the baseline from the last successful full run and give the three skipped files zero weights so their former cost no longer reserves runners. Estimated shard runtimes are approximately 112s each. In the updated successful CI run, actual test steps ranged from 84157s, down from 122216s before skipping the orbit tests (27 faster at the slowest shard). Add per-shard slow-test summaries, timing-log artifacts for every attempt, and a baseline refresh command. Preserve native crash retries and propagate ordinary test failures through tee with explicit Bash pipefail. Document slow outliers and timing maintenance in .githubtest-timings.md. Validation: plannerparser regression tests pass; targeted run confirms exactly three skipped orbit tests; all 1,483 discovered files are still assigned exactly once. Updated full CI passed all ten shards, timing reports, typecheck, dependency checks, and distribution smoke test: https:github.comtscircuitcoreactionsruns36668064842
body:
Skip the three AM62L LPDDR4 north/south/west orbit routing regressions, which each take roughly 3–4 minutes. Keep their fixtures and snapshots for re-enabling. The AM62L direct-decoupling regression and other orbit tests continue to run.

Balance every discovered test file longest-first across ten shards using measured CI runtimes. Refresh the baseline from the last successful full run and give the three skipped files zero weights so their former cost no longer reserves runners. Estimated shard runtimes are approximately 112s each. In the updated successful CI run, actual test steps ranged from **84–157s**, down from **122–216s** before skipping the orbit tests (27% faster at the slowest shard).

Add per-shard slow-test summaries, timing-log artifacts for every attempt, and a baseline refresh command. Preserve native crash retries and propagate ordinary test failures through `tee` with explicit Bash pipefail. Document slow outliers and timing maintenance in `.github/test-timings.md`.

title: Support modelUrl on assembly elements
description: Add modelUrl rendering to assembly.device, assembly.screen, assembly.subassembly, and assembly.cadassembly, allowing direct import of housing or display models with connector-relative placement.
body:
Add `modelUrl` rendering to `assembly.device`, `assembly.screen`, `assembly.subassembly`, and `assembly.cadassembly`. Authors can import a housing or display directly on the assembly element; screen URL models retain connector-relative placement and replace the generated FlexScreen.

Reuse one URL resolver for the new props and assembly CAD children, preserving existing extension detection, query strings, `#ext` hints, relative assets and STL fallback. Device models render at the world origin with a CAD source identity; devices without a model remain transparent. Subassemblies keep their grouping and children behavior.

Uses the released `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.670` in both the dev dependency and override, following the merged https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/872. Validation uses the npm package, with no local props replacement.

Validation:
- 18 targeted assembly, namespaced-element, and enclosure-container tests pass, including existing 3D snapshots.
- New tests verify emitted model formats, URLs, child coexistence, unnamed devices, CAD-only behavior, disabled CAD rendering, and bottom-layer screen placement.
- Core typecheck and package build (ESM and declarations) pass with the published `@tscircuit/props@0.0.670` package.
- All five complete documentation examples render using the updated core.

title: Reproduce USB-C shell pad ambiguity with snapshots
description: Reproduces a bug where duplicate USB-C shell pins lose their PCB connections despite being wired to a ground header in the schematic.
body:
### Motivation
- Show duplicate USB-C shell pins losing their PCB connections despite being wired to a ground header in the schematic.

### Before
- The snapshots had no external ground header or enabled routing, making the missing copper connection difficult to see.

### After
- Use self-contained TSX with four shell slots, explicit wires and local routing. No JSON fixture is needed. The schematic shows the ground connection while the PCB snapshot has no routed traces.
- Verified the failure before the fix and two routed traces with the fix. The diagnostic test is skipped after generating the failure snapshots so the stacked code-only fix can inherit the same repro files.

title: fix: preserve rotated plated-hole obstacles in SRJ
description: Fixes incorrect dimensions of rotated rectangular plated-hole obstacles in SRJ by ensuring proper rotation is applied during obstacle generation.
body:
## Summary

- route `circular_hole_with_rect_pad` through Core's existing rotation-aware rectangular plated-hole obstacle conversion
- preserve correct SRJ dimensions for quarter-turn pads and rotation for non-axis-aligned pads
- add a TSX repro using the exact PMP23595 T500-T503 pad geometry at 90° and 270°

## Root cause

Circuit JSON correctly retained `rect_ccw_rotation`, but `getObstaclesFromCircuitJson` handled circular holes with rectangular pads in a separate branch that copied `rect_pad_width` and `rect_pad_height` without applying that rotation. On PMP23595, this changed each `12.7 × 17.272 mm` board-space pad obstacle into `17.272 × 12.7 mm`, making the two real routing gaps appear overlapped in SRJ.

The fix removes that unrotated special case and reuses the same established rotated-rectangle path as the other rectangular plated-hole variants.

![PMP23595 rotated rectangular plated-hole repro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/fix/rotated-rect-plated-hole-obstacles/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-pmp23595-rotated-rect-pad-srj-obstacles-pcb.snap.svg)

## Verification

- PMP23595 repro asserts `12.7 × 17.272 mm` SRJ obstacles at both 90° and 270°
- repro asserts the original `4.4196 mm` and `3.6068 mm` gaps
- related rotated SMT-pad, plated-slot, copper-pour, and plated-hole tests pass
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: Refresh cached supplier pin 1 orientation for straight-row connectors
description: Updates the cached supplier pin 1 orientation for straight-row connectors by advancing the cache key and updating the dependency to ensure correct orientation is computed.
body:
Core already calls `analyzePcbPin1Location`, but its installed `circuit-json-util` version predates the four-pin straight-row fix. A prior build may also have cached JLC C131334's orientation as `null`, so updating the dependency alone would leave J1 unresolved.

Update Core to `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util@^0.0.117` and advance the supplier orientation cache key from v3 to v4. This makes Core recompute the JST PH pin-1 locations: the authored footprint has pin 1 on the left, while JLC's C131334 footprint has pin 1 on the right. The renderer's geometry and the analyzer implementation stay in their existing packages.

Validation: focused orientation tests (5 pass), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, and Biome checks pass. A new PCB snapshot test seeds the stale v3 `null` result and verifies that a second render reuses the v4 result.

title: Require checks 0.0.230 with copper-pour precision fix
description: Raises cores minimum tscircuitchecks version from 0.0.228 to 0.0.230 to ensure the inclusion of a geometry converter fix for tiny trace segments near via drills, preventing copper-pour DRC boundary-conflict exceptions.
body:
Raise core's minimum `@tscircuit/checks` version from `^0.0.228` to `^0.0.230`. Version 0.0.230 bundles the released geometry converter fix for tiny trace segments near via drills, preventing the copper-pour DRC boundary-conflict exception.

The earlier range permits the fixed release but also permits older installations without it. This bump explicitly requires the fix. It replaces closed, unmerged dependency PR #4234, which targeted 0.0.229.

Validation: installed checks 0.0.230; 29 DRC/fabricator tests and TypeScript check pass. Its published `checkCopperPourShorts` also completes on the original smart-ring Circuit JSON without a runtime exception.

Upstream: https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/365.

title: Support modelprinter strings on assembly elements
description: Support model... on all assembly elements, accepting direct HTTP(S) model URLs and resolving modelprinterfootprinter strings to modelcdn GLB URLs.
body:
Support `model="..."` on all assembly elements, accepting direct HTTP(S) model URLs and resolving modelprinter/footprinter strings to modelcdn GLB URLs. For example, `<assembly.device model="soic8" />` emits `https://modelcdn.tscircuit.com/jscad_models/soic8.glb`, while `assembly.screen` retains its connector-relative frame.

Direct URLs use the existing `modelUrl` resolver for file formats, query strings, and `#ext` hints. For modelprinter/footprinter strings, a shared resolver encodes the complete model string as one URL path segment, preventing colors, spaces, slashes, and query characters from changing URL semantics. Rendering does not fetch geometry or mutate props. Model-less containers, existing modelUrl imports, cadModel strings, and screen dimension defaults keep their behavior.

Uses published `@tscircuit/props@0.0.672`, including the merged model prop schemas from https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/873. Both the dev dependency and override require this release. Validation uses the npm package.

Validation:
- 22 targeted assembly, namespaced-element, and enclosure tests pass.
- Covers all four elements, whitespace normalization, encoded model strings, direct HTTP(S) URLs, CAD-only behavior, children, disabled CAD, and bottom-layer screen placement.
- Added and visually checked a 3D snapshot of a modelcdn-generated FlexScreen attached to its PCB connector.
- Core typecheck and package build (ESM and declarations) pass with published `@tscircuit/props@0.0.672`.

title: chore: update circuit-json-to-connectivity-map to 0.0.32
description: Updates the circuit-json-to-connectivity-map dependency to version 0.0.32, fixing routing issues by allowing traces to connect directly to their via ports and updating related tests accordingly.
body:
Update the development dependency from ^0.0.30 to ^0.0.32 to include explicit via-port membership in the full connectivity map (tscircuit/circuit-json-to-connectivity-map#51). Peer dependencies remain unchanged.

Refresh two existing PCB snapshots: traces now route directly to their own via ports instead of detouring around them. Also update the two breakout/fanout tests that expected a false overlap error for a partially connected trace: the library now resolves the connected endpoint, while the legitimate disconnected/dangling endpoint errors remain.

Validation: 14 focused via/connectivity/copper-pour tests and both affected breakout/fanout tests pass; typecheck, build, and git diff --check pass.

title: Serialize DRC execution failures in circuit JSON
description: Serializes DRC execution failures in Circuit JSON, ensuring that diagnostics from successful checks are preserved and failures are logged without disrupting the rendering of the circuit.
body:
When a DRC check rejects, the renderer currently logs the exception and settles without a Circuit JSON error. `Promise.all` also discards diagnostics from successful check groups. A copper-pour boundary-operation exception in the smart-ring benchmark therefore produced a successful CLI build with incomplete DRC.

Group Board, its interface, and its helpers under `normal-components/Board/` and update all import paths. Move DRC scheduling and execution into `Board/Board_updatePcbDesignRuleChecks.ts`, following the existing Board helper pattern. `Board.updatePcbDesignRuleChecks()` delegates to that helper.

Catch execution failures per check group and insert a `source_runtime_error` containing `phase_name` and `message`. The message includes the check identity and exception text. Defer check invocation so synchronous throws are handled too. Successful groups still contribute diagnostics, the rendered circuit remains available, and repeated settling does not duplicate failures or rerun the checks.

Uses published `circuit-json@0.0.507`, including the merged source_runtime_error schema from https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/844. Updates both the dev dependency and override; this repository does not track a dependency lockfile.

Validation against the published package:
- 31 DRC, fabricator, and Board lifecycle tests pass, including both runtime-failure regressions.
- TypeScript check passes.
- The regression tests verify serialization, preserved PCB components and successful diagnostics, synchronous and asynchronous failures, non-Error rejections, and no duplicate errors after settling twice.

Failures are isolated at the check-group API boundary. If `runAllRoutingChecks` aborts before returning, results internal to that failed group cannot be recovered here. This does not fix the underlying copper-pour geometry exception.

Related CLI safeguard: https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5018. Handled DRC failures now appear in Circuit JSON for normal build diagnostics; the safeguard still covers other unhandled asynchronous render failures.

title: fix: integrate courtyard keepout placement DRC
description: Integrates courtyard keepout placement DRC into the core, ensuring that component courtyards entering keepouts produce placement DRC errors, including specific cases for battery connectors and mounting holes.
body:
Component courtyards entering keepouts now produce placement DRC in core, including the battery-connector/mounting-hole case fixed in https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/361. Previously the copper pads could remain clear while the connector envelope overlapped without an error.

Core already invokes the aggregate placement runner and serializes the required keepout permissions. The latest main supplies `@tscircuit/checks ^0.0.227`, which includes the courtyard rule; this PR adds end-to-end integration coverage. Peer dependencies remain unchanged (`*`).

Add two JSX-to-DRC integration tests with visually inspected PCB snapshots:
- Six BT1-style courtyard-only overlaps compare default rejection, `excludeRefs`, `allowPlacements`, `allowTraces`, `warningOnly`, and layer filtering. All copper pads remain outside the keepouts.
- A generated antenna automatically excludes its own courtyard while an unrelated component's courtyard still produces an error. Removing the inferred exclusions exposes the antenna's own overlaps, proving the exemption is exercised.

Validation:
- The permission regression fails against checks 0.0.225 (zero errors instead of two).
- 41 keepout, antenna, and DRC tests pass; both new snapshot tests also pass after the final visual adjustment.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, formatting of changed tests, and `git diff --check` pass.

title: fix: convert outline keepouts to SRJ obstacles
description: Fixes the issue where outline keepouts were not being converted to SRJ obstacles in the circuit JSON model, ensuring proper rendering and obstacle generation.
body:
Stacked on #4207.

## Root fix

Circuit JSON models a stroked keepout path as `pcb_keepout` with `shape: "outline"`, but `getObstaclesFromCircuitJson` only consumed circle and rectangle keepouts. This adds the missing shape conversion at that contract boundary.

Outline keepouts are rendered with round caps and joins. The conversion therefore decomposes the stroke using the existing obstacle approximation utilities:

- `generateApproximatingRects` approximates each rotated segment body
- `fillCircleWithRects` approximates the round join/cap at each unique vertex

The resulting obstacles are axis-aligned SRJ rectangles, preserve the source layers, have no electrical connectivity, and use stable keepout/segment/join-derived IDs.

There is no board-specific circle detection, expanded segment length, custom rectangle approximation, renderer compensation, custom SRJ shape, or connectivity inference.

## Real-board result

The real TI TMDS62LEVM crop now passes. Its 2.17779854 mm rounded keepout is visibly larger than the enclosed 1.00000054 mm pad obstacle and the SRJ approximation preserves the source shape.

The 48 segment bodies produce 96 rectangles through `generateApproximatingRects`. The 48 unique round joins produce 192 rectangles through `fillCircleWithRects`. The right panel contains only the resulting SRJ rectangles; it has no synthetic circle or source overlay.

![TMDS62LEVM real-board outline keepout SRJ obstacles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/9b68021466b7f6d1589eaa64a0536b22b0fc1888/tests/repros/__snapshots__/ti-tmds62levm-outline-keepout-obstacle.snap.svg)

## Validation

- focused real-board repro passes with 7 assertions
- TypeScript passes
- Biome passes on changed source and test files
- `git diff --check` passes

title: fix: collapse circular keepouts to one SRJ rect
description: Emit one rectangular SRJ obstacle for circular keepouts and recognize complete circular outlines, reducing the number of obstacles significantly.
body:
## Summary

- emit one rectangular SRJ obstacle for `<keepout shape="circle">`
- recognize complete circular outline keepouts and emit one circumscribed rectangle
- retain the existing segment/join approximation for partial and irregular outlines
- replace the raw-Circuit-JSON repro with a routed TSX repro using the default autorouter

Rectangular keepouts already emit one rectangular obstacle and are unchanged.

## Root cause

The direct circular keepout branch already calculated the correct square envelope from `radius * 2`, but labeled the obstacle with the unsupported `type: "oval"`.

PMP22650's layer-specific Altium circle keepouts correctly remain stroked outlines in Circuit JSON. Core then sent each outline through the generic path approximation, expanding every segment and rounded join. Its 154 closed circles and five open arcs became 45,782 obstacles.

Complete circular outlines are now identified from an explicit repeated endpoint, equal radius, complete angular coverage, and ordered traversal. Their full stroked bounds become one square; open and non-circular outlines continue through the existing implementation.

## Sample 24 result

- connections: 409 before and after
- closed circular keepouts: 154 → 154 obstacles
- open arcs: 5 → 1,430 segment/join obstacles
- obstacles for all 159 outlines: 45,782 → 1,584

## TSX repro

![A default-routed TSX trace detouring around the circular keepout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/fix/circle-keepouts-as-single-rects/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-circle-keepout-single-srj-rect-pcb.snap.svg)

The TSX repro asserts that a 2 mm-radius circular keepout produces one 4×4 mm rectangular SRJ obstacle. Focused utility tests cover PMP22650's imported circular outline and confirm that a 270° partial outline and densely sampled 345°, 350°, and 355° open arcs still use the generic approximation.

## Validation

- focused keepout, PMP22650, open-outline, and via tests: 7 passed

title: repro: duplicate autorouter connections from TSX net paths
description: Reproduces a bug where the autorouter submits duplicate connections for the same electrical nets in a TSX board, highlighting the issue through a comprehensive test.
body:
## User-facing TSX reproduction

This PR reproduces the issue through the public API a Core user uses: a real TSX board rendered and routed by Core's default autorouter. It does not import a Circuit JSON fixture, call `getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson` directly, or replace routing with a capture stub.

The circuit mirrors the PMP23653 planar-transformer connector topology:

- `J5` and `J7`: 12 physical terminals on `net.SECONDARY`
- `J3`: 6 physical terminals on `net.PRIMARY`
- two multi-terminal `<trace path={...}>` elements, each attached to its named net

The circuit has two electrical nets and two source traces. Current Core submits four routing jobs: one trace-owned and one net-owned connection for each identical endpoint group.

## What the default router proves

```text
SECONDARY source trace + SECONDARY source net -> 2 input jobs for the same 12 pads
PRIMARY   source trace + PRIMARY   source net -> 2 input jobs for the same  6 pads
```

The default solver merges the identical endpoint groups and emits 16 physical route segments, so the final PCB view alone hides the redundant input. The autorouting phase snapshot exposes the real defect: **4 submitted connections for 2 electrical nets**. Its routed output is associated with the two trace-owned jobs.

Trace hints are intentionally absent because they are not the cause of this reproduction.

## SVG reproduction

### Default-autorouter phase I/O

![Default autorouter receives four jobs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/553d13ed4701ed51a2994943091cceb547b5e6ee/tests/repros/ti-srj/__snapshots__/pmp23653-default-autorouter-duplicate-routing.snap.svg)

## Assertions

- physical topology: 2 source nets and 18 PCB ports
- default-autorouter input: 4 connections containing 36 endpoint occurrences
- default-autorouter output: 16 routed segments

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repros/ti-srj/pmp23653-duplicate-connections-repro.test.tsx`
- one focused commit on current `main`
- no production-code changes

title: fix: detect component courtyards overlapping placement keepouts
description: Fixes detection of component courtyards overlapping placement keepouts, ensuring DRC is triggered even when copper remains clear.
body:
A component's courtyard could overlap a placement keepout without producing DRC when its copper remained clear. In [ESP32-E-Reader 1.0.22](https://tscircuit.com/rushabhcodes/ESP32-E-Reader#pcb), BT1's courtyard intrudes about 1.60 mm into the top-left mounting-hole keepout while its nearest copper pad stays about 1.81 mm clear.

Add `checkPcbCourtyardOverKeepout` to the public API and placement check runner. It handles circular, rectangular (including rotated), outline, and polygon courtyards using the existing clearance geometry. It respects keepout layers, `allow_placements`, component exclusions, warning-only keepouts, and do-not-place components, and reports once per component/keepout pair. The shared courtyard conversion helper is extracted without changing the existing plated-hole overlap behavior.

Validation:
- 562 tests pass, including 22 new cases and a reduced fixture from the published board.
- The BT1 regression includes a close-up SVG snapshot with the actual connector silkscreen, courtyard, copper pads, mounting hole, keepout, and DRC message. Rendered and visually inspected; the 22-case suite and type checking pass after adding the snapshot.
- Running the new check on the complete published Circuit JSON produces exactly the expected BT1 placement error.
- Type checking and build pass.
- Format check and `git diff --check` pass; Biome reports existing oversized fixtures that it skips.

title: fix: enforce via-in-pad restrictions using hole overlap for all nets
description: Fixes via placement errors by enforcing restrictions on same-net vias whose drilled holes enter a pad when via-in-pad is disallowed, ensuring proper error reporting for overlapping vias.
body:
A same-net via whose drilled hole enters a pad must report a placement error when `is_via_in_pad_allowed` is false or omitted. Explicit `true` continues to allow it. Copper-ring contact alone no longer counts as via-in-pad.

The check measures the circular drill against the pad outline on shared layers. Full enclosure and partial drill intrusion report an error; external drill tangency and copper-only contact do not. Different-net copper overlap remains a violation in `checkViaPadClearance`, including when via-in-pad is enabled.

Builds on the reproduction merged in #358. Both branches retain separate allowed/disallowed TSX tests and SVG snapshots. The disallowed test changes from the incorrect empty result to the actual placement error; the allowed control remains unchanged. An additional TSX/SVG fixture shows eight positions across the pad edge, and unit tests cover the boundary and curved, rotated, and polygon pads. The Game Boy fixture retains all 11 copper-clearance errors but no longer misclassifies its five copper-only overlaps as via-in-pad.

[JLCPCB's guide](https://jlcpcb.com/blog/via-in-pad-in-pcb) describes vias inside component soldering pads and recommends full encapsulation by metal-defined pads. Its [BGA guidance](https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/bga-design-guidelines---pcb-layout-recommendations-for-bga-packages) distinguishes drill-to-pad spacing from copper-to-pad spacing. These sources do not specify an exact partial-overlap classification algorithm: counting partial drill intrusion is a conservative DRC choice, not a claim to reproduce JLCPCB's internal DFM.

![Same-net vias across a pad edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/checks/4e51fda554c8235f548bc53241159d4a6726d421/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-same-net-via-at-pad-edge.snap.svg)

Validation: 557 tests and 17 snapshots pass; type checking, formatting, build, and dependency checks pass. Updated SVGs were rendered and visually inspected.

Reproduction #358 has been merged. This PR targets `main` and will run the full GitHub Actions checks before merging.

The test fails with published 0.0.2 and passes with published 0.0.3; this does not suppress geometry failures or real shorts.

Circuit JSON is preserved and the CLI correctly exits 1 for those remaining design errors. A fully published-package verification can follow this checks release.

title: Fix Node imports by bundling calculate-elbow with placement analysis
description: Fixes Node import issues by bundling calculate-elbow with schematic placement analysis to resolve ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT errors and ensure successful builds and imports in Node environments.
body:
`@tscircuit/checks` can build successfully but fail to import in Node with `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT`. Its bundled schematic-placement analysis imports `calculate-elbow/lib`, and tsup leaves that transitive import external. This caused the SVG service to return 500 even on `/health` after a dependency upgrade.

Include calculate-elbow in `noExternal` alongside the embedded analysis package. The existing source is compiled into the published JavaScript, so no private directory import escapes the bundle and consumers do not need to rewrite node_modules. This keeps the pinned analysis revision and rendering behavior unchanged.

Add a Node import/execution smoke check after the CI build (Node 22) and before publishing (Node 24). It imports the built public API and exercises `checkSchematicPlacement([])`.

Validation: the unmodified build reproduces `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT`; the fixed production bundle builds and imports/runs successfully under Node 22 and Node 26. Formatting and diff checks pass (Biome reports existing oversized fixture warnings). The local Bun test preload is blocked by the existing missing sharp native binary; All PR CI checks passed on `4e13239`: build including the Node import smoke check, normal Bun tests, type checking, dependency check, and formatting.

Unblocks removal of the checks postinstall workaround in https://github.com/tscircuit/svg.tscircuit.com/pull/2399. Once merged and published, that draft should consume the new checks release.

The test uses the board's real oval slot dimensions (0.5999988 mm × 0.999998 mm) beside a round NPTH control on a four-layer board.

title: fix: include via port membership in full connectivity map
description: Fixes a bug where the full connectivity map ignores PCB via port IDs, leading to disconnections in the connectivity map for traces without source trace IDs.
body:
`getFullConnectivityMapFromCircuitJson` ignores `pcb_via.pcb_port_ids`, leaving a bottom-layer trace disconnected from its GND vias when the trace has endpoint port IDs but no `source_trace_id`. This is the upstream bug behind the custom connectivity-map reconstruction in https://github.com/tscircuit/check-shorts/pull/63.

Include each via's explicit port IDs alongside its existing source-net/source-trace/PCB-trace connections. The existing network builder now connects both sides of the via, including vias with only port membership. Geometry does not assign connectivity.

Adds a minimal regression reproducing the bottom-port route and checks for port-only vias, unidentified overlapping traces, and overlapping different-net vias. Updates the development `circuit-json` dependency to 0.0.504 for the canonical `pcb_port_ids` type.

body:
The shared straight-row pin analyzer was fixed in [circuit-json-util PR #200](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/pull/200) and published in v0.0.117. This updates `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` to that version and tests the real routed JST PH J1 against its JLCPCB C131334 footprint. Supplier preparation now detects that the pin row is reversed and emits J1 at 270° instead of the unverified 90°, without changing board coordinates or CAD geometry.

The fixtures preserve J1's routed plated holes and the supplier pad positions. The regression asserts the strict JLCPCB CSV row and verifies the input Circuit JSON is unchanged. `bun test` passes (52 tests, 329 assertions); type checking, build, targeted Biome check, and `git diff --check` pass. The README is unchanged.

This fixes the PnP package when callers run `populatePartOrientationMetadata` with a parts engine before converting. The CLI's prebuilt-JSON Gerber export currently bypasses preparation; that call path requires a separate integration change. Previously closed PR #22 contained a duplicate analyzer that this PR does not include.

title: Fix false SVG outages from cold-render timeouts
description: Fixes false SVG outages by increasing the timeout for cold-render requests to 15 seconds and improving SVG content validation.
body:
The SVG monitor marks healthy cold renders as outages because it allows only five seconds. Actual PCB/schematic requests from GitHub Actions returned valid images in 6.3–7.6 seconds; the previous Node deployment also exceeded the threshold (5.4–6.2 seconds). Warm current-production requests completed in 1.1–1.3 seconds.

Allow 15 seconds for each complete image response, disable redundant ky retries (the runner already retries), and verify SVG content and successful-render headers. Include the failing view, elapsed time, and error in status failures. Add unit coverage and a PR workflow that requests actual production PCB/schematic images.

Validation: four unit tests and TypeScript checks pass locally. [Cold production reproduction](https://github.com/tscircuit/status/actions/runs/36673566378), [comparison with previous Node deployment](https://github.com/tscircuit/status/actions/runs/36673666365). Temporary diagnostic scripts/workflows were removed from the final diff. No dependency patches or runtime rollback.

title: fix: update checker dependencies for via-connected routes
description: Fixes false shorts reporting in tsci check shorts when same-net routes contact through-vias without a source_trace_id by updating checker dependencies.
body:
`tsci check shorts` can report false shorts when a same-net route contacts through-vias but has no `source_trace_id`. Update the packaged checker to `0.0.26` to include https://github.com/tscircuit/check-shorts/pull/65, and raise `circuit-json-to-connectivity-map` to `^0.0.32` for via-port connectivity. Only `package.json` and `bun.lock` change.

Validation:
- Built both this branch and unchanged main (`87d5e617`) and ran their packaged checkers against the same unmodified Trellis circuit JSON in a temporary consumer project with `tscircuit@0.0.2680`. With `TSCI_TEST_MODE=true` to bypass the CDN and `--mode gerber --layer all`, main reports two bottom-layer GND shorts; this branch reports zero shorts across all four layers.
- `bun run build`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, and `bun scripts/check-for-dependencies.ts` pass. Formatting passes with Biome's Git-ignore support enabled; the default format command also scans existing ignored cache JSON.
- `bun test tests/cli/check` reports 5 pass, 15 fail, and 1 error on both this branch and a clean frozen-lockfile install of unchanged main. The existing `assemblySubassemblyProps` export mismatch prevents the shorts test file from loading. No assertions or snapshots were changed to hide these failures.

title: Restore signal names in EasyEDA imports
description: Restores meaningful signal names for pins in EasyEDA imports, allowing for better schematic representation and connectivity.
body:
EasyEDA imports now preserve signal names for C3188679 (LM5146RGYR) and C3662807 (TPS259474ARPWR). Pins previously shown only as `pin1`, `pin3`, and other numeric labels now have meaningful schematic labels and can be connected by their signal names.

LM5146 retains `EN`/`UVLO` on pin 1 and `SS`/`TRK` on pin 3. The eFuse retains its enable, overvoltage, power-good, and power-good threshold names. Nine connection tests confirm that these names reach the intended source pins and physical PCB pads.

**PR 2 of 2; depends on #5036.**

### Schematic snapshots

| Part | Reproduction | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C3188679 | ![LM5146 before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/cli/65917b10453989178ff91c02316b282d5df2c7b3/tests/lib/import/__snapshots__/C3188679-schematic.snap.svg) | ![LM5146 after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/cli/8778dfdd2657060334690d80e1e1900b9e305d76/tests/lib/import/__snapshots__/C3188679-schematic.snap.svg) |

Both schematic SVGs change and were visually inspected. PCB SVGs remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Schematics display the primary alias; all restored aliases remain available for connections.

- New offline regression tests: 11 passed, including all nine alias-to-pad checks.

description: Summary add checksum-derived Circuit JSON fixtures for DRV8307EVM, LM5155EVM-FLY, LM251772EVM-PD, and LMG342X-BB-EVM inline-snapshot the generated tscircuit TSX for each board evaluate every generated board with the repositorys existing runTscircuitCode path snapshot source Circuit JSON and evaluated TSX renders side by side for both PCB and schematic views  What the repro shows board outline, pads, holes, silkscreen, and rough footprint placement survive routed copper and copper pours do not survive the conversion the electrical schematic is not reconstructed; the evaluated board renders a generic multi-pin chip symbol outline keepouts are currently reported as unsupported on three fixtures This PR intentionally records the current output as a visual baseline. body:
## Summary

- add checksum-derived Circuit JSON fixtures for DRV8307EVM, LM5155EVM-FLY, LM251772EVM-PD, and LMG342X-BB-EVM
- inline-snapshot the generated tscircuit TSX for each board
- evaluate every generated board with the repository's existing `runTscircuitCode` path
- snapshot source Circuit JSON and evaluated TSX renders side by side for both PCB and schematic views

## What the repro shows

- board outline, pads, holes, silkscreen, and rough footprint placement survive
- routed copper and copper pours do not survive the conversion
- the electrical schematic is not reconstructed; the evaluated board renders a generic multi-pin chip symbol
- outline keepouts are currently reported as unsupported on three fixtures

This PR intentionally records the current output as a visual baseline. It does not claim equivalent round-trip fidelity.

## Test plan

- `bun test`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`

title: Update rendering dependencies with upstream checks fix and compatibility holds
description: Updates the rendering stack using tscircuitchecks0.0.229, which includes the upstream Node compatibility fix from tscircuitchecks362, and refreshes affected libraries while maintaining compatibility with existing versions to prevent breaking changes.
body:
Updates the rendering stack using `@tscircuit/checks@0.0.229`, which includes the upstream Node compatibility fix from tscircuit/checks#362. The published checks bundle no longer leaks the `calculate-elbow/lib` directory import that caused production requests to fail despite successful builds. No checks postinstall patch or direct calculate-elbow workaround is used; the existing OCCT/fanout patch script is unchanged.

Updates core/eval/props/tscircuit, circuit-to-svg, common, ngspice, snippet URLs, 3D PNG rendering, React, and supporting libraries. Reviews and refreshes the affected 2D snapshots and adds an endpoint regression test for automatic PCB teardrops and disabling one end. Existing 3D snapshots and the exact JLCPCB SVG hash assertion remain unchanged.

Three compatibility holds keep this update safe:
- `biscuitboard@1.0.10`: newer releases remove `Clad40x40`, breaking existing board code.
- `@tscircuit/fanout-solver@0.0.46`: newer 0.0.78 fails Vercel type checking in `complete-original-endpoints.ts` (`string | undefined` returned as `string`).
- `circuit-json-to-gltf@0.0.118`: newer conversion loses visible lead detail in the vectorized JLCPCB preview. Retaining this version restores the exact original SVG hash.

Next.js, TypeScript, Biome, and vectorizer major/minor migrations remain separate work. This PR does not update every dependency to latest.

Validation:
- Local production build, production Node smoke test, formatting, and full suite: **59 passed, 0 failed**.
- Production smoke coverage inherited from #2398 exercises cold health, code evaluation/routing, PCB/schematic/assembly SVG and PNG, 3D PNG, repeat rendering, and the legacy Biscuit Board fixture.
- Linux CI: build, formatting, Node 22 production smoke, and full test job all pass on `7adfdad2bf6150d50f8dc081d5990a31f34cfb63`.
- Vercel deployment succeeds and every production smoke check passes against the [immutable preview](https://svg-tscircuit-jsgy70iac-tscircuit.vercel.app), including 3D PNG and the legacy Biscuit Board fixture.
- Ready for review; auto-merge is not enabled.

title: Use Bun on Vercel and align rendering dependencies with tscircuit
description: Moves Vercel functions to Bun using bunVersion: 1.x and upgrades the rendering stack to current tscircuit versions, ensuring compatibility and improved performance.
body:
Moves Vercel functions to Bun using `bunVersion: "1.x"` and upgrades the rendering stack to current tscircuit versions. Builds and CI use Bun 1.3.14, frozen installs, Next.js 16.3.7, and Biome 2.5.14. The uncached health response exposes `X-Runtime` so deployed smoke tests verify that requests actually execute on Bun. Node fallback smoke coverage remains in the required test job.

Dependency alignment:
- `tscircuit@0.0.2679`, `@tscircuit/core@0.0.2016`, and `@tscircuit/eval@0.0.1491` match the current upstream release.
- Updates fanout-solver from 0.0.46 to upstream's 0.0.78, GLTF from 0.0.118 to 0.0.134, and vectorizer from 0.0.5 to 0.1.0. Retains the published checks fix at 0.0.229.
- Updates Biscuit Board to 1.0.28 and removes obsolete `Clad40x40` compatibility checks. TypeScript remains 5.9.3 to match tscircuit's 5.x peer requirement.
- Overrides poppygl to 0.0.29, matching tscircuit and the latest published release. This removes the renderer-local 0.0.24 copy allowed by circuit-json-to-3d-png's dependency range. A regression test verifies the version resolved from inside the renderer matches both the override and tscircuit.

The updated GLTF renderer changes the board and trace colors. The previous vectorization noise filter also discarded fine-pitch IC leads; lowering its filtering preserves those details without dependency patches. Reviewed and refreshed the 3D snapshots and exact JLCPCB SVG hash; test thresholds are unchanged. The existing OCCT/fanout postinstall patches are unchanged, with no new patches introduced.

Next.js configuration moves file tracing out of `experimental`, keeps webpack for the existing build, and includes the generated TypeScript updates. Biome's configuration is migrated and excludes generated `next-env.d.ts` from formatting.

Vercel installs into a clean `node_modules` directory before its frozen install: restoring the previous deployment cache otherwise retained an obsolete renderer-local poppygl copy. Every build runs the renderer-resolution regression test before compiling, so stale copies fail the build.

Validation on `3e5a092f5dd979d48d23131060bd333e0af7ef98`:
- All required GitHub checks pass: build, formatting, Bun and Node production smoke, and the full test suite.
- Local full suite: **60 tests / 0 failures**, snapshot updating disabled.
- The [immutable Vercel preview](https://svg-tscircuit-vcz2t2vgy-tscircuit.vercel.app) reports `X-Runtime: bun` and passes cold health, code evaluation/routing, PCB/schematic/assembly SVG and PNG, 3D PNG and SVG, and repeat rendering.
- The deployed JLCPCB fine-pitch chip SVG matches the reviewed poppygl 0.0.29 output's exact SHA-256 hash (`3161a299152768b84688e2879f17780f5e5faac56a89fcddb5c4b738052d3302`).
- Updated 3D snapshots were visually reviewed with component geometry and fine-pitch leads preserved. Test thresholds are unchanged.

Vercel manages the runtime version within its [Bun 1.x line](https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/bun), currently 1.3.14. Bun 1.4 is not selected. Ready for review; auto-merge is not enabled.

The live code-to-PCB endpoint ignores `pcbTeardrops` because its core and props dependencies predate the feature. Validation: production build, format check, and six focused endpoint tests pass. Visually inspected the teardrop snapshot. All 48 test files also pass when run individually in separate processes to limit memory use, including the 3D suite. Both simulation tests now use the service endpoint and its shared ngspice engine instead of initializing a separate engine through tscircuit. This resolves the order-dependent Linux CI failure without weakening assertions. The full Linux test suite passed after that fix. The PoppyGL update passes the targeted 3D tests locally and the full Linux test suite. Build, formatting, and Vercel deployment also pass on the latest commit. Local snapshot testing used a temporary native sharp installation; it does not change package dependencies or the lockfile.

Unblocks the teardrop CircuitPreview in https://github.com/tscircuit/docs/pull/895 after deployment.

title: Improve Pipeline 9 clearance repair for straight trace spans
description: Long, straight trace spans can remain too close to copper because the clearance projector only moves existing vertices and their endpoints are locked. Add bounded subdivisions to constant-width spans on routes implicated in DRC errors, then run a refinement pass after the existing independent wire repairs. This gives the solver nearby vertices to bend while retaining terminals, junctions, widths, and via sites.
body: Long, straight trace spans can remain too close to copper because the clearance projector only moves existing vertices and their endpoints are locked. Add bounded subdivisions to constant-width spans on routes implicated in DRC errors, then run a refinement pass after the existing independent wire repairs. This gives the solver nearby vertices to bend while retaining terminals, junctions, widths, and via sites. The change is in Pipeline 9's clearance-repair logic and applies to any eligible input. It contains no fixture-specific conditions, error filtering, changed DRC thresholds, or solver-failure suppression. Existing changed-segment collision checks, fixed-obstacle/via guards, and reference DRC validation still gate publication. Rejected and protected routes retain their original vertices. A 1e-9 mm tolerance applies only when comparing residual clearances; splitting unchanged segments produced approximately 1e-15 mm round-off differences. New errors and meaningful clearance regressions remain rejected. Segment lengths use the scaled `getVectorLength` calculation suggested in [the review](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2769#discussion_r4135330518), following [high-density-repair01#24](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair01/pull/24). This replaces `Math.hypot`, whose platform-dependent rounding can change `Math.ceil(length / 0.5)` and therefore the number of inserted vertices. Scaling protects the calculation from overflow and underflow. The 0.5 mm subdivision spacing and 32-subdivision cap bound the refinement resolution and work; existing DRC clearance requirements remain unchanged. ### Visual example: opening a via-to-trace clearance gap These are close-ups of the actual `bugreport107-board-1726` solver outputs before and after the fix (macOS run), with the **same location, layer, and scale**. Blue shows bottom-layer copper. The red circle marks the central via's outer copper radius plus the required **0.1 mm clearance**; the neighboring trace's copper edge must stay outside it. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | The trace just below and to the right of the central via enters the required clearance area. | The trace bends outward, opening the gap while the via stays in exactly the same place. | The solver inserts initially collinear points into eligible long spans, giving the existing repair solver places to bend locally. The candidate is accepted only after the collision and reference DRC checks described above. The dashed trace styling identifies the bottom layer; it does not represent physical breaks in the copper. This crop illustrates **one repaired gap**; the **97 → 89** reduction below is the total across the entire board. For `bugreport107-board-1726`, using the unchanged relaxed DRC preset: | Error category | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Via-to-trace clearance | 43 | 36 | | Pad-to-trace clearance | 23 | 22 | | Trace overlap / clearance | 22 | 22 | | Via spacing | 9 | 9 | | **Total** | **97** | **89** | With the board's declared 0.25 mm via-hole clearance and board-edge checks, the final count improves from 132 to 124. The comparison found no new error identities, identical geometry for all 758 emitted vias, and unchanged IDs and endpoints for all 763 traces. There are still 89 relaxed DRC errors; this PR addresses the small clearance gaps that can be repaired without moving vias or terminals. Validation: - `tests/bugs/bugreport107-board-1726.test.ts` explicitly requires at most 89 final DRC errors, in addition to its existing stage-improvement and snapshot assertions. - 23 focused tests pass (288 assertions), including clearance projection, independent nudges, bounded regional repair, and vector-length precision at zero, the 0.5 mm subdivision boundary, and extreme magnitudes. The new synthetic straight-span regression demonstrates the failure without subdivision and successful repair with it, independently of bugreport107. - Junction-preservation coverage runs with subdivision both disabled and enabled; reference-validation coverage accepts floating-point round-off and rejects a 1e-7 mm regression. - Full macOS bugreport107 regression passes with the explicit 89-error ceiling (7 assertions). Full Linux x64 CI regression with Bun 1.3.8 passes the same numeric ceiling and the corrected snapshot, which comes from its inspected received SVG and reports 89 errors. Linux ARM runs with Bun 1.3.8 and 1.3.14 also produce 89 errors and identical geometry to one another, but a different route variant from x64. - All nine CI test shards pass on commit `984e694cd`, along with formatting, type checking, build, Vercel build, and the string-ID check. [Passing test run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36569946508). - `bun run build` passes, including TypeScript declarations. - `git diff --check` passes.

title: Reduce bugreport107 DRC errors to 82 with finer clearance bends
description: Reduces DRC errors in bugreport107 by adjusting clearance segment lengths to improve pad-to-trace clearance without altering existing copper or connections.
body:
Bugreport107 still has a pad-to-trace clearance violation after the safe-bend selection in #2776. Pipeline 9 only adds a movable bend to an error-bearing trace when a straight segment is longer than 0.5 mm. A shorter segment can therefore couple movement near a pad to more distant copper. This PR reduces the subdivision spacing to 0.25 mm, giving the clearance projection another local degree of freedom without changing the original copper, electrical connections, via positions, or DRC rules.

The captured joint repair stage improves from **123 to 122 errors**. The removed error is the clearance between `pcb_smtpad_838` and `source_trace_64__source_net_64_mst167_0` (previously 0.071 mm versus a 0.1 mm minimum). The complete macOS bugreport107 solve improves from **83 to 82 relaxed DRC errors**. Comparing the final emitted boards found exactly that one removed error, no new error pairs, and no worsened remaining measured clearances. All 758 vias and all 763 trace endpoint pairs are unchanged. The regression assertion is tightened to 82, and the macOS and Linux snapshots are updated.

The existing clearance publication guards still require a lower DRC count with no new error identities or worsened remaining measured clearances. This branch is based on #2776 while that PR is open.

Validation: full macOS bugreport107 test, focused projection and safe-bend tests, TypeScript type checking, and build pass. [Final-commit Linux CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36625527700) passes all nine test shards, including bugreport107 with the 82-error assertion and refreshed Linux snapshot.

title: Reduce bugreport107 DRC errors to 58 on macOS and 59 on Linux
description: Reduces DRC errors for bugreport107 to 58 on macOS and 59 on Linux by improving clearance and routing logic in the autorouter.
body:
Bugreport107 now routes with **58 relaxed DRC errors on macOS and 59 on Linux**, down from the current `main` snapshots of 87 and 80. The regression ceiling is tightened to 59, and both platform snapshots are updated.

The branch contains three general clearance-repair improvements:

- A blocked bend no longer discards safe movements elsewhere in the same contiguous proposal. Restored neighbors are rechecked against the actual selected geometry until the remaining moves are safe.
- Short straight spans can gain a local bend at 0.25 mm spacing, letting a trace clear a nearby pad without dragging more distant copper with it.
- After the wire-only passes improve the layout, a final coupled projection lets wires and vias move together. It uses the same 0.01 mm clearance headroom as the wire-only passes. The DRC rule is unchanged: the coupled result is retained only if the complete-board error count falls, with no new or worsened fixed-obstacle violation and no new via-to-pad violation.

These changes affect solver logic rather than recognizing this report or editing its routes. The final coupled pass can trade one error identity for another; the complete-board DRC check decides whether the result is an overall improvement.

| Platform | Current `main` | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| macOS | 87 | **58** |
| Linux | 80 | **59** |

title: Reduce bugreport107 DRC errors to 63 on macOS and 65 on Linux
description: Reduces DRC errors in bugreport107 from 82 to 63 on macOS and 65 on Linux by implementing a final whole-board clearance projection that moves wire bends and vias together.
body:
## Problem and fix

On bugreport107, the existing bounded repair reaches 82 DRC errors in the emitted board. It runs two partial clearance projections after regional search, but those passes deliberately keep vias fixed. The wire bends they improve can open room for a via to move, yet the solver stops before trying that coupled motion again.

Run one final whole-board clearance projection on the retained wire geometry, with the same 0.01 mm precision margin already used by the partial projections. This pass moves wire bends and vias together. It uses the existing fixed-obstacle and via-to-pad physical guards and is published only when the complete reference DRC has fewer errors. The via-to-pad guard compares the proposal with the immediately preceding routes: subdivision may add bend vertices, while the two wire-only passes keep every drill fixed. The bug-report assertion and both platform snapshots now reflect the resulting route.

On macOS, the full bugreport107 solve improves from **82 to 63 relaxed DRC errors** (19 fewer); Linux CI reports **65**. The macOS bounded-repair stage improves from 122 to 86. All 763 trace endpoint pairs remain fixed.

| DRC category (macOS) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Accidental copper-contact shorts (subset of trace errors) | 16 | 3 |
| All trace errors | 19 | 8 |
| Pad-to-trace clearance | 20 | 0 |
| Via-to-via clearance | 9 | 3 |
| Via-to-trace clearance | 34 | 52 |
| **Total** | **82** | **63** |

The via-to-trace category rises by 18 as the coupled solver relocates copper; the other categories fall by 37 combined. The complete-board DRC guard checks the net result, so this is a measured improvement, not a claim that every individual clearance improves.

## Before and after snapshots

These are the actual bugreport107 test snapshots, embedded here for review only; no documentation images are added to the repository.

| Before: 82 errors | After: 63 errors |
| --- | --- |
| ![Bugreport107 before coupled repair](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/ce90512f431ca7da1e68a70701d1efee040fce7b/tests/bugs/__snapshots__/bugreport107-board-1726.snap.svg) | ![Bugreport107 after coupled repair](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/3d530e025/tests/bugs/__snapshots__/bugreport107-board-1726.snap.svg) |

[Open the macOS before SVG](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/blob/ce90512f431ca7da1e68a70701d1efee040fce7b/tests/bugs/__snapshots__/bugreport107-board-1726.snap.svg) · [Open the macOS after SVG](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/blob/3d530e025/tests/bugs/__snapshots__/bugreport107-board-1726.snap.svg) · [Open the Linux before SVG](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/blob/ce90512f431ca7da1e68a70701d1efee040fce7b/tests/bugs/__snapshots__/bugreport107-board-1726-linux.snap.svg) · [Open the Linux after SVG](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/blob/3d530e025/tests/bugs/__snapshots__/bugreport107-board-1726-linux.snap.svg)

## Validation

- Linux CI passes the tightened DRC assertion (65 errors); its received SVG is committed as the updated Linux snapshot.
- 27 focused projection/regional-repair tests: passed (323 assertions).
- TypeScript check and library build: passed.
- A stricter independent check including board edge and declared via-hole spacing: 117 to 82 errors.

body:
## Why this matters

The checked-in **Suneater Labs Joule Thief** board has five circular `Edge.Cuts` openings in its battery footprints. Importing them as `pcb_hole` elements turns them into five standalone drilled-pad footprints on KiCad export. That changes the board's editable geometry and the appearance of the openings.

## Change

Import those circles as `pcb_cutout` elements. The existing Joule Thief Circuit JSON, SVG, and PNG snapshots are updated in this PR.

Existing Joule Thief snapshot: [before the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/kicad-to-circuit-json/c68c091/tests/repros/repro01-joule-thief/__snapshots__/repro01-joule-thief-pcb.snap.png) · [after the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/kicad-to-circuit-json/93b1aa0/tests/repros/repro01-joule-thief/__snapshots__/repro01-joule-thief-pcb.snap.png). Without the change, the five circles remain `pcb_hole` elements and become drilled-pad footprints.

title: test: reproduce skipped four-pin crystal load network
description: Motivation The crystal placement analyzer only evaluates crystals with exactly two source ports. Four-pin crystals also have two grounded case pins, so their load-capacitor placement is skipped even when the signal network should be analyzed.  What this PR does Adds a focused Circuit JSON reproduction derived from a real USB hub board. Models Y2 as a simple_crystal with pin_variant: four_pin and renders the built-in four-pin crystal symbol. Preserves the 24 MHz frequency, 12 pF load capacitance, two signal pins, and two grounded case pins. Keeps only U13, Y2, R33, C31, and C32 so unrelated analyzer findings do not obscure the target behavior. Records the current bug: CrystalLoadCapacitorPlacementSolver reports zero CrystalNotCenteredOverLoadCapacitors issues. This PR only adds the reproduction; it does not change the solver.  References Renesas 8V41NS0412 Evaluation Board User Guide, Figure 5 on page 10(https:www.renesas.comendocumentmah8v41ns0412-evaluation-board-user-guide) shows a four-pin crystal with pins 1 and 3 used for the oscillator signals, pins 2 and 4 grounded, and a load capacitor from each signal to ground. Microchip USB2244 Hardware Design Checklist, section 6(https:ww1.microchip.comdownloadsaemDocumentsdocumentsUNGProductDocumentsDesignChecklistUSB2244-HW-Design-Checklist-00004319.pdfpage8) documents the USB hub oscillator and load-capacitor network. !Focused real-board four-pin crystal reproduction(https:raw.githubusercontent.comGokulPandi-Mcircuit-json-schematic-placement-analysisrepro-four-pin-crystal-load-networktestscases__snapshots__usb-hub-four-pin-crystal-repro-focused.snap.svg)  Validation 120 tests pass Type-checking passes Formatting passes
body:
## Motivation

The crystal placement analyzer only evaluates crystals with exactly two source ports. Four-pin crystals also have two grounded case pins, so their load-capacitor placement is skipped even when the signal network should be analyzed.

## What this PR does

- Adds a focused Circuit JSON reproduction derived from a real USB hub board.
- Models Y2 as a `simple_crystal` with `pin_variant: "four_pin"` and renders the built-in four-pin crystal symbol.
- Preserves the 24 MHz frequency, 12 pF load capacitance, two signal pins, and two grounded case pins.
- Keeps only U13, Y2, R33, C31, and C32 so unrelated analyzer findings do not obscure the target behavior.
- Records the current bug: `CrystalLoadCapacitorPlacementSolver` reports zero `CrystalNotCenteredOverLoadCapacitors` issues.

This PR only adds the reproduction; it does not change the solver.

## References

- [Renesas 8V41NS0412 Evaluation Board User Guide, Figure 5 on page 10](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/mah/8v41ns0412-evaluation-board-user-guide) shows a four-pin crystal with pins 1 and 3 used for the oscillator signals, pins 2 and 4 grounded, and a load capacitor from each signal to ground.
- [Microchip USB2244 Hardware Design Checklist, section 6](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/UNG/ProductDocuments/DesignChecklist/USB2244-HW-Design-Checklist-00004319.pdf#page=8) documents the USB hub oscillator and load-capacitor network.

![Focused real-board four-pin crystal reproduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/repro-four-pin-crystal-load-network/tests/cases/__snapshots__/usb-hub-four-pin-crystal-repro-focused.snap.svg)

## Validation

- 120 tests pass
- Type-checking passes
- Formatting passes

title: feat: detect flyback diodes separated from relay coils
description: Adds RelayFlybackDiodePlacementSolver, reporting FlybackDiodeSeparatedFromRelayCoil when a local, label-connected protection diode is placed away from its relay coil.
body:
Stacked on #126.

Adds `RelayFlybackDiodePlacementSolver`, reporting `FlybackDiodeSeparatedFromRelayCoil` when a local, label-connected protection diode is placed away from its relay coil. The real controller reports two findings: K1/D1 and K2/D2. Existing trace simplification does not report either pair.

Recognition requires named coil/contact pins, a diode across both coil nets, and a grounded-emitter transistor driver with the diode's anode at its collector. Nearby or directly wired loops, separate blocks, reversed polarity, shared coil pairs, and ambiguous placements are excluded. The advisory preserves polarity and pin assignments; it does not prescribe exact coordinates.

The existing full-sheet repro snapshot now highlights both members of each pair, with matching numbered badges beside the diagnostics. Two small TSX snapshots cover separated and grouped placement.

[Toshiba's mechanical relay driver, page 12](https://toshiba-semicon-storage.com/info/docget.jsp?did=156465#page=12), draws the protection diode beside and across the coil. The comparison concerns that branch; the complete circuits differ.

title: Reproduce 0.08 mm terminal neckdown from fragmented pad obstacles
description: Reproduces a bug where the terminal width calculation incorrectly reduces a valid trace width due to fragmented pad representation, without changing solver behavior.
body:
## Motivation

A single physical pad can be represented in SRJ as multiple adjacent rectangles sharing the same pad ID. The power trace expander currently calculates the terminal width using only one rectangle instead of the complete connected pad. This can unnecessarily reduce a valid `0.15 mm` trace to `0.08 mm`, creating a manufacturing-rule violation. This PR provides a minimal reproduction of that behavior.

## Issue

`PowerTraceClearanceRepairSolver` can create a terminal segment below `minTraceWidth` when one physical pad is represented by adjacent rectangular SRJ obstacles.

The endpoint-width calculation currently measures only the rectangle containing the terminal. In this reproduction, that rectangle is 0.10 mm tall and the terminal is 0.01 mm off its centerline, so the calculated limit is:

`2 × (0.05 - 0.01) = 0.08 mm`

`repairConnectedPadNeck` then applies that limit to a 0.30 mm-long terminal segment even though the configured minimum is 0.15 mm and the complete pad union has enough copper for it.

This is a general fragmented-pad problem, not a condition tied to one board or component. It can affect polygon, curved, annular, or other custom pads represented by multiple connected rectangles.

## Why this SRJ is valid

Core converts a non-axis-aligned polygon `pcb_smtpad` into 0.10 mm-tall rectangles with `fillPolygonWithRects`. Every generated rectangle retains the original `pcb_smtpad_id` in `connectedTo`: [Core obstacle conversion](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/main/lib/utils/obstacles/getObstaclesFromCircuitJson.ts#L197-L226).

The reduced fixture follows that contract directly:

- three adjacent 0.60 × 0.10 mm rectangles;
- every fragment shares `pcb_smtpad_fragmented` and the same `POWER` connection;
- their physical union is 0.60 × 0.30 mm;
- the terminal is at `(0, 0.01)`, so a 0.15 mm terminal spans `x = [-0.075, 0.075]` and `y = [-0.065, 0.085]`, entirely inside the union.

This keeps the reproduction at the power-trace-expander SRJ boundary. It does not depend on the acoustic-tuner TSX, its imported footprint, or the full autorouter pipeline. It is the reduced follow-up to the SRJ-origin concern raised on [tscircuit-autorouter#2638](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2638).

## Reproduced result

- Input minimum-width segment: `0.1500 mm`
- Output terminal segment: `0.0800 mm`
- Material below-minimum length: `0.299999 mm`
- `repairedPadNeckSegmentCount`: `1`
- Solver result: complete, not failed

The three labeled gray rows are adjacent SRJ rectangles that represent one physical pad. Both panels show the same terminal and the same local pad geometry. The left panel shows the expected 0.15 mm segment fitting across the complete pad, while the right panel shows the expander's 0.08 mm output in red.

![Fragmented pad terminal neckdown reproduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/power-trace-expander/3760cc2/tests/__snapshots__/fragmented-connected-pad-neckdown.snap.svg)

## Expected

Terminal-width calculation should consider the complete connected physical pad, rather than one rectangular fragment, before reducing a segment below `minTraceWidth`. A genuinely narrow pad may still require an explicit terminal neckdown; this case is different because the full same-pad union supports 0.15 mm.

This PR is reproduction-only and does not change solver behavior.

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 9999999` — 86 pass, 0 fail, 2,885 assertions
- focused reproduction and fixture-catalog tests — 2 pass, 0 fail, 33 assertions
- `bun run typecheck` — pass
- `bun run build` — pass
- Biome formatting for every changed TypeScript/TSX file — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass
- generated SVG rendered and visually inspected

The repository-wide `bun run format:check` still reports pre-existing formatting differences in `tests/alias-cache-lifetime.test.ts`, `tests/disallow-new-vias.test.ts`, `tests/grid-route-cost-pruning.test.ts`, and `tests/shared-alias-cache.test.ts`. None is changed here.

The PR targets `fix/enforce-connectivity-monotonicity`, the active power-expander line pinned by the autorouter, rather than the older default branch.

title: Resolve selected schematic variant parameters
description: Resolves schematic parameters based on the selected project variant, ensuring that variant-specific parameters are correctly prioritized and rendered without leaking values from other variants.
body:
## Summary

- keep base project parameters and each project variant in separate cached scopes
- add explicit `variantName` selection to schematic parameter resolution and SVG rendering
- resolve indexed Altium sections such as `Parameter2_1` only for their owning variant
- apply Altium precedence: project, then document, then selected variant
- preserve the lower-priority value when a higher-priority scope uses Altium's `*` inheritance marker
- resolve the built-in `=VariantName` string from the explicit selection

## Root cause

The original change treated every `Parameter<number>_<number>` section as a project-global parameter. Those sections are variant-owned: Altium reserves parameter owner 1 for the base project, so `ProjectVariant1` owns `Parameter2_*`, `ProjectVariant2` owns `Parameter3_*`, and so on. Loading all of them into one map leaked the last variant into renders that had not selected any variant.

The official TI LMX2694 project demonstrates both scopes: variant `001` resolves `EVM_Orderable` to `LMX2694EPEVM`, while variant `002` resolves it to `LMX2694SEPEVM`.

Altium documents variant parameters as higher priority than schematic-document and project parameters, and documents `*` as explicitly inheriting the next lower-priority value: https://www.altium.com/documentation/knowledge-base/altium-designer/reduce-repetitive-documentation-tasks-with-parameterized-project-template

## Regression coverage

- no selected variant does not import variant-owned parameters
- two selected variants resolve their own values without leaking
- selected variant parameters override document and project parameters
- `*` in the selected variant inherits the document value
- `*` in the document inherits the project value
- SVG rendering forwards the selected variant
- `=VariantName` resolves from the explicit selection

## Verification

- `bun test` — 346 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- verified against the real TI LMX2694 two-variant project
