title: Support independent and nested flex PCB folds
description: Enables independent and nested folding of flex PCBs, resolving placement errors and ensuring correct rendering of both flat and folded states.
body:
Flex boards with finite bends on different arms currently report a placement error and remain flat. Adopt the shared finite-region fold implementation so independent nonparallel arms fold successfully. Nested regions fold the child before carrying it with the parent. The original two-arm example with both `bendSide="left"` values also folds correctly: its vertical chord moves the body, while the right tip stays flat.

Add numeric CAD regressions and actual PCB/GLB snapshots for both arrangements, with explanatory PCB notes and optional finite bend lines. PCB placements remain flat, repeated rendering leaves Circuit JSON unchanged, and inverse CAD transforms recover the flat positions and orientations. Replace the obsolete all-nonparallel fallback fixture with crossing bend regions on a rectangle; that case retains the flat board, CAD, and schematic and shows its canonical placement error through published PoppyGL's existing labels.

The bend examples already declare `material="flex"`. Adopt the exporter material fix so their 3D surfaces and edges use the default polyimide palette, with dark markings for contrast. Refresh six existing default-color flex PNGs without adding explicit color overrides. Existing explicit colors and all PCB/schematic snapshots remain unchanged.

[Flex-utils #7](https://github.com/tscircuit/flex-utils/pull/7), [GLTF #232](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/232), and [GLTF #233](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/233) are merged. Core uses published flex-utils `0.0.8` for its bundled fold implementation and published GLTF `0.0.141` for its 3D snapshot exporter. Both preview pins are replaced, with no remaining dependency prerequisite. PoppyGL remains published `0.0.29`. Addresses [tscircuit #5277](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277), item 2.

Validation:

- 25 flex, CAD, and affected schematic regressions pass across 22 files with 338 assertions, including the existing finite-tail, bend-zone, stiffener, and unexpected-error cases. Numeric checks cover emitted orientations, restored CAD basis directions, and complete unchanged fallback poses.
- Three new PCB snapshots and the six refreshed real GLB-to-PNG snapshots were visually inspected. Both independent and nested success regressions fail against published flex-utils `0.0.7`.
- Installation with scripts disabled succeeds. The actual installed GLTF `0.0.141` package has all five distribution files byte-identical to the tested preview. All 15 flex snapshots remain byte-for-byte unchanged when replacing that preview with the published release. The material refresh changes exactly six default-color PNGs; existing explicit colors and all PCB/schematic snapshots stay unchanged.
- TypeScript, build, formatting, and diff checks pass. Full CI passes on source [`3e11388`](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/commit/3e1138851cb5f0652be8238e4362bd1908f39750): all ten test shards, TypeScript, formatting, distribution smoke tests, package preview, and Vercel deployment.

title: fix: preserve flex rendering with shared fold diagnostics
description: Fixes rendering issues for nonparallel PCB bends and CAD mounts in bend zones, ensuring that errors are reported while preserving flat placements for PCB, schematic, and 3D outputs.
body:
Nonparallel PCB bends and CAD mounts inside bend zones currently abort `renderUntilSettled()` or 3D export. Emit `pcb_placement_error` records and preserve flat placements for these declared folding limitations so PCB, schematic, and 3D output remain available.

Board construction uses flex-utils' explicit folding result. CAD placement handles only `PcbFoldError`; unexpected failures propagate. An unsupported board keeps its CAD flat, while an invalid rigid mount stays flat and other valid mounts still fold. The shared helper covers footprint models, bounding boxes, and child `<cadmodel>` elements. Surface deformation, rigid meshes, and stiffener fallback remain in the shared exporter.

The standard `toMatch3dSnapshot`/PoppyGL regressions enable the exporter's `showErrors` option. GLTF stores full Circuit JSON messages in renderer-neutral scene metadata. The snapshot matcher forwards the exporter's adapter options to published `poppygl@0.0.29`, which draws the messages through its existing `debugPoints` labels. The adapter uses the current camera to place readable rows on screen, including errors without coordinates. Circuit geometry, camera and bounds are preserved. The PCB snapshot enables `showBendLines` and shows both finite bend segments with 0.5 mm BEND LINE labels. The underside close-up still checks the flat stiffener directly.

Uses published `@tscircuit/flex-utils@0.0.7`, `poppygl@0.0.29`, `circuit-json-to-gltf@0.0.139`, and `circuit-to-svg@0.0.437`. [GLTF #231](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/231) and [SVG #803](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/803) are merged and released. Both rendering options default to false.

Addresses items 2 and the rendering exception in item 3 of [tscircuit#5277](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277). Bend-zone DRC is covered separately by [checks #370](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/370); independent nonparallel physical folds remain unsupported.

The released SVG renderer also includes upstream [SVG #795](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/795) and [SVG #796](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/796). Three existing schematic snapshots are refreshed with the already-reviewed paint order and selected-sheet framing; symbol positions and geometry are unchanged. The final published-version update adds only the bend labels to the PCB baseline; the 3D and schematic baselines are unchanged from the tested previews.

Validation: all 10 PCB-flex tests, 10 adjacent CAD tests across seven files, and all three affected schematic regressions pass (23 tests, 230 assertions). TypeScript, build, formatting, and installation with scripts disabled pass. Repeated settled renders preserve Circuit JSON and do not duplicate diagnostics. New PCB and 3D snapshots were visually inspected. The unexpected-error regression verifies that ordinary failures propagate. Actual GLB messages are rendered through the published PoppyGL API.

Full CI passes on the published renderer versions and refreshed PCB snapshot: all ten test shards, TypeScript, formatting, dist smoke tests, package preview, continuous releases, and Vercel.

title: Reproduce arbitrary silkscreen rectangle rotation
description: Fixes rendering issue where silkscreen rectangles with specific rotations (30 and 45) render horizontally instead of following the requested rotation.
body:
A 6 × 2 mm `<silkscreenrect>` with `pcbRotation={30}` or `pcbRotation={45}` renders horizontally instead of following its requested rotation.

Adds a passing snapshot reproduction with explicit, labelled examples for 30°, 45°, 0°, 90° and 180°. Every rectangle has its props directly on the JSX component. The snapshot records the current output: the two incorrect arbitrary rotations alongside three working controls. There are no expected-failure tests or rotation assertions; the implementation fix can update the snapshot.

The current props types omit `pcbRotation`, so each requested rotation has a narrow `@ts-expect-error` comment. These comments can be removed when props support lands.

Requested in [the review of props #884](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/884#pullrequestreview-5381266812). This PR changes only the reproduction test and its snapshot. Proposed implementation: #4265. Converter mapping: tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit#119.

Validation: the reproduction and existing rectangle/rotation tests pass (4 tests), along with the targeted TypeScript check and Biome formatting. The existing snapshot passes unchanged.

title: Preserve supplied fanout autorouter options
description: Preserves user-supplied options in the autorouter configuration when using the fanout preset, ensuring that custom algorithms can be invoked correctly without losing configuration details.
body:
The `fanout` preset discards options supplied in an autorouter configuration object. For example, `autorouter={{ preset: "fanout", allowViaInPad: true }}` loses `allowViaInPad` in the effective routing input, and a supplied `algorithmFn` is never called.

Preserve the supplied configuration before applying the fanout preset defaults. Custom algorithms return their own final traces, so they no longer inherit the built-in fanout solver's follow-up stage, which requires a transformed routing problem.

Keep the AM62L/LPDDR4 full-board benchmark on the native fanout pipeline that generated its original snapshot. Its test name now identifies that router explicitly. The shared fixture, four-layer board, and PCB snapshot are unchanged from the base branch.

A separate focused regression runs the actual `FixedTargetBgaFanoutSolver` callback through core and verifies its completed top-pad → dogbone via → bottom-pad route. It checks callback invocation, emitted traces and vias, and routing errors. The configuration regression covers explicit and omitted via-in-pad settings and callback identity. Report the BGA solver's underlying error when solving fails.

Validation with Bun 1.4.0:
- Eight targeted tests pass, including the full AM62L benchmark, custom BGA callback, option preservation, native/sequential/single-layer fanout, production AM62L routing, and dogbone handoff.
- The custom callback regression fails when the follow-up-stage fix is removed.
- `tsc --noEmit`, Biome formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The full-board snapshot matches the base SVG byte for byte; both snapshots were rendered and visually inspected.

title: fix: use finite bend regions for outlined flex boards

With the U-shaped flex board in tscircuit/tscircuit#5277, a bend across the left tail also folds the right resistor because core does not provide an outline to flex-utils. Adopt `@tscircuit/flex-utils` 0.0.6 and pass the emitted board outline after subtracting the final board center. RL folds 90°, while RR's CAD position and rotation stay flat. PCB records remain unchanged.

Also adopt released `circuit-json-to-gltf` 0.0.137, which includes finite board-mesh folding from https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/229. The regression uses core's existing `toMatch3dSnapshot` path: emitted Circuit JSON → GLB export → PoppyGL. The snapshots show actual board textures and resistor models, and the exporter selects the pose from core's emitted CAD fold flags.

The exact issue fixture is tested at the origin and with a translated board against the same flat/folded snapshots. Numeric checks cover CAD position/rotation, unchanged PCB records, and folded-to-flat restoration. Explicit RL/RR silkscreen labels make the expected behavior visible.

Validation: all 6 PCB-flex tests pass, `bunx tsc --noEmit` passes, and `bun run build` passes against the released packages. Existing flex snapshots still match. Temporarily restoring exporter 0.0.133 fails the new folded snapshot; 0.0.137 passes it.

title: fix: bundle schematic trace solver runtime and types
description: Bundles the schematic trace solvers JavaScript and public types inside Core to eliminate the need for consumers to supply it separately, addressing Bun 1.3s duplicate-tarball resolution bug.
body:
Core currently emits runtime and declaration imports of `@tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver`, although the solver is a JSCDN-only build dependency at the version Core uses. Consumers must supply it separately, exposing overlapping dependency graphs to Bun 1.3's duplicate-tarball resolution bug.

This bundles the solver's JavaScript and public types inside Core, following the existing `flex-utils` configuration. The dist smoke check now rejects external solver imports in either artifact, including subpath imports. That check runs in the existing Smoke Test Dist workflow.

Validation:
- Build, repository typecheck, dist smoke tests, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Five existing schematic solver/routing tests passed (25 assertions).
- The new artifact check rejects a build using the original configuration and passes with this change.
- Packed Core installed in separate projects with fresh caches on Bun 1.3.0, 1.3.14 and 1.4.2. After removing the unrelated transitive solver 0.0.208 installed by a peer's dependencies, all three projects routed a two-resistor schematic with Bun auto-install disabled and passed a TypeScript consumer check using `SOLVERS.SchematicTracePipelineSolver`. These consumer checks used exact peer versions and `skipLibCheck: true`; the dist guard separately verifies that emitted declarations have no external solver import.

Bundling adds about 0.8 MB of unminified JavaScript and 59 KB of declarations. A Core release and downstream manifest updates are still needed before tscircuit can remove its redundant solver tarball dependency. This PR does not change solver versions, routing behavior, CI Bun versions or snapshots. The full suite is left to PR CI.

Related installer diagnosis: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/35426 and https://github.com/tscircuit/eval/pull/4907.

title: Preserve PCB dimension offset vectors
description: Adds functionality to ensure PCB note and fabrication note dimensions emit native offset distance and direction, preventing duplicate renderer geometry and maintaining transform integrity.
body:
PCB note and fabrication note dimensions must emit native `offset_distance` plus `offset_direction`; pre-shifting endpoints or authoring extra extension paths duplicates renderer geometry. Explicit footprint-local directions rotate/reflect with the PCB transform without receiving translation. Scalar-only offsets use the perpendicular to board-space endpoints, and coincident endpoints avoid division by zero.

Adds emitted-geometry assertions and visual regressions, including a short 0.25 mm oblique PCB-note offset that exposes duplicate extension lines. Existing fabrication transform coverage remains intact.

Uses released `@tscircuit/props@0.0.674` from https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/886. The temporary development patch has been removed.

The printed-coil repro snapshot was regenerated because it contains a scalar-offset fabrication dimension: the dimension now renders at its authored offset instead of directly on the measured line.

Validation: focused PCB/fabrication dimension regressions (49 assertions), the printed-coil repro, TypeScript typecheck, and format checks pass against the published props package.

Converter mappings: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/pull/130 and https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/pull/132.

body:
Adds NEMA8, NEMA17, and NEMA23 JSCAD models and moves the existing hex socket bolt and sheet-metal generators out of modelprinter. Model strings, schemas, dimensions, defaults, and validation come from [modelprinter PR #7](https://github.com/tscircuit/modelprinter/pull/7); this repository owns the models and visual tests.

The motors have accurately positioned mounting bores, blind-hole floors or through-flange holes, pilots, and configurable round/D shafts. Tests probe the rendered solids at the mounting centers and shaft flats, including custom dimensions and rotated flats. Motor defaults and coordinate conventions are documented in modelprinter.

`HexSocketBolt` and `SheetMetal` components and JSCAD solid factories wrap the migrated indexed surfaces without changing their geometry. Existing mesh factories and types are exported from jscad-electronics. `Footprinter3d` and vanilla helpers route these mechanical strings and return no PCB pads. Geometry topology checks and four-view poppygl snapshots move here; the migrated PNGs were reviewed with this repository's renderer versions. Node ESM tests cover the built vanilla models.

The dependency is pinned to the modelprinter spec PR commit so CI uses the real contract without duplicate defaults or parsers. **Release order:** publish the updated modelprinter package first, then replace the Git pin with that published version before releasing jscad-electronics.

Sets Node 24 for Vercel; its previous Node 20 project default was discontinued.

Validation: all 294 tests pass; typecheck, format check, library build, and Cosmos site build pass. A fresh consumer install verifies Git preparation and Node loading. GitHub Actions and Vercel are green on the final PR commit (`cbcbf48`).

title: Add optional finite PCB bend line overlays
description: Adds the ability to render optional finite PCB bend line overlays in SVG outputs, improving the inspection of flex layouts intended folds.
body:
PCB SVG renders currently omit `pcb_bend` centerlines, which makes it difficult to inspect a flex layout's intended folds. Add `convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg(circuitJson, { showBendLines: true })` to draw yellow dashed overlays between each bend's finite endpoints. The option defaults to false, works on either PCB face, and is independent of PCB note visibility.

Each segment has a small `BEND LINE` label running parallel beside it. Labels use the embedded font, are capped at 0.5 mm, and shrink to fit short finite segments with endpoint margins. Reversing endpoints keeps the label upright.

Endpoints use the canonical board-local millimeter frame and translate once by the referenced board center before the existing SVG transform. Finite bends stay confined to their declared segment, including a bend crossing only one tail of a U-shaped board. Each line carries the bend/board IDs and a title with its name, signed angle, and radius.

Declare the renderer's existing runtime imports (`circuit-json`, `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util`, `circuit-json-to-connectivity-map`, and `schematic-symbols`) as required runtime peers, with development versions matching the existing installed packages. This follows the project's internal-library dependency policy. Previously a standalone production-only install could not import the built renderer because these packages were supplied indirectly by development dependencies. Renderer behavior is unchanged.

Validation: 419 tests pass, with one existing Resvg TODO; typecheck, format check, and package build pass. Seven focused tests verify unchanged default output, exact translated finite endpoints, separate board ownership, top/bottom visibility, hidden PCB notes, absent board references, and unchanged input JSON. Label checks compare the emitted text baseline against horizontal, vertical, and diagonal segments, verify readable orientation after reversing endpoints, and check the 0.5 mm cap and short-segment sizing. Three standard `toMatchSvgSnapshot` fixtures were rendered to PNG and visually inspected.

The packaging correction was verified by packing the built library and installing it with `npm install --omit=dev --ignore-scripts` into a fresh directory outside the checkout. Required peers install automatically; import, top/bottom bend-line rendering, default-hidden bend output, and schematic export pass without companion packages. The previous built preview fails this same cold import because `circuit-json` is missing. Focused tests, typecheck, format check, dependency policy check, and build were rerun after the dependency correction; generated JavaScript differs only in its embedded package metadata.

The preview now selects Node.js 24 through `engines.node`, overriding Vercel's discontinued Node.js 20 project setting. This matches the release workflow's existing Node.js 24 version. The Cosmos preview export passes on Node.js 24.21.0, and installation with the frozen Bun lockfile passes without dependency changes. All CI is green on `42881562cd7dcaf602a9dd65adf020736bc84ded`, including tests, typecheck, both format checks, bundle/install size checks, and the Vercel preview deployment.

![Small labels along finite bends on translated boards](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/4220615e3cc5cef94092ebfad1158811f264a275/tests/pcb/__snapshots__/pcb-bend-lines-top.snap.svg)

Related to https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277.

title: Export PCB stiffener outline Gerber layers
description: Adds support for exporting PCB stiffener outlines in Gerber format, including handling of rotated rectangles and polygons, while preserving existing layer functionalities.
body:
`pcb_stiffener` records are currently omitted from Gerber exports. Add a closed outline drawing per attachment face and material, such as `B_Stiffener_polyimide.gbr`, preserving material, thickness, and optional adhesive thickness in Gerber comments.

Handle rotated rectangles and polygon outlines in the owning board's coordinates, including boards away from the origin and optional Y flipping. Existing copper, mask, paste, silkscreen, and edge-cut layers remain unchanged. The CLI already archives the returned file map dynamically, so the new drawings are included in its export ZIP.

One enlarged, labeled 1400 × 450 SVG snapshot renders a realistic six-contact flex jumper from the actual files returned by `convertCircuitJsonToGerberFiles`. It compares the top copper with the same copper plus separate bottom polyimide and FR4 stiffener drawings. Contact fingers and solder pads are supported at the two ends, while the narrow neck stays flexible. The actual exported `.gbr` strings go directly to the independent Tracespace `gerber-to-svg@4.2.8` parser/plotter. Complete renderer-produced SVGs keep their native geometry, definitions, and transforms; the comparison only positions and resizes them using renderer-reported bounds. The example uses an off-origin board to check registration. Fatal rendering errors and geometry warnings fail the test; only precisely identified unsupported X2 metadata warnings are allowed. Existing numeric regressions retain coverage of both faces, all materials, rotated rectangles, polygons, board ownership, translations, and Y flipping. All 142 existing SVG snapshots are unchanged. There are no README changes.

Addresses item 4 of https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277.

Validation:
- Full suite: 183 tests pass across 89 files (1,791 assertions).
- Twelve focused regressions cover grouping, both faces, rotation, translated boards, board ownership, Y flipping, polygon closure, unchanged nonempty electrical layers, and the exported visual snapshot.
- The new comparison snapshot was rendered at its full pixel dimensions and visually inspected. A deliberately corrupted exported aperture was rejected with the renderer diagnostic `tool 99 is not defined`.
- KiCad 10.0.3 GerbView independently opened the original export ZIP, recognized both stiffener files as `Other, Stiffener`, and showed the rectangle/chamfered outlines registered with the end tabs and copper.
- TypeScript, build, formatting, and diff checks pass.

Manufacturer upload check:
- JLCPCB accepted the original ZIP as a 40 × 12 mm, two-layer flex board. A filename-only comparison using its documented `pib_0.2.gbr` and `fr4b_0.4.gbr` names was also accepted; Gerber contents were identical between uploads.
- With EDA software set to Other, JLCPCB says stiffeners cannot be automatically detected and require manual review. Renaming alone did not change this. The quote can be manually configured for 0.12 mm flex, 0.20 mm polyimide, and 0.4 mm FR4. This is upload/quote validation, not confirmation of production acceptance.
- Gerber Viewer redirects to sign-in. The manufacturer’s 3D stiffener preview remains unverified pending an authenticated check.
- Naming reference: https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/fpc-stiffener-emi-guide.

title: fix: update Bun to 1.4.2 and sync Core 0.0.2035 packages
description: Updates Bun to version 1.4.2 and synchronizes Core package versions to resolve installation issues and ensure compatibility.
body:
## Summary

- Pin both Bun Test jobs to Bun 1.4.2 (previously 1.3.14).
- Update @tscircuit/core to ^0.0.2035, the latest published release verified when preparing this PR.
- Synchronize the matching Core package versions: capacity-autorouter ^0.0.951, checks ^0.0.232, and bus-lanes-solver 0.0.6.
- No application code, board inputs, assertions, snapshots, timeouts, retry policies, or lockfile policy changes.

## Why

The package-only update in #4906 is blocked during installation on Bun 1.3.14, before tests run. Duplicate direct/transitive Git or tarball dependencies can be queued after their extraction task has completed and remain unresolved even though the archive downloaded successfully. The upstream fix is https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/35426 and is included in Bun 1.4.2.

A controlled local reproduction with identical two-package manifests, archive bytes, and clean caches passed on Bun 1.3.14 when the duplicate was discovered before extraction completed and failed when it was discovered afterwards. Bun 1.4.2 handled the failing order successfully. The exact eval update manifest also installed successfully on Bun 1.4.2. This is an installer fix, not a new Core runtime requirement.

## Validation

- Dependency installation with isolated Bun 1.4.2 passed locally with lifecycle scripts disabled; resolved Core 0.0.2035 and autorouter 0.0.951.
- Test-matrix validation passed: all seven test directories remain covered.
- git diff --check passed.
- Full GitHub CI passed at commit 03ee35ff77f9e2a8c3b19141418aa6a979a0196d: all 13 checks are green.
  - [Bun Test](https://github.com/tscircuit/eval/actions/runs/36911492372): all seven test groups plus matrix validation passed. Each Linux job installed Bun 1.4.2, Core 0.0.2035, autorouter 0.0.951, checks 0.0.232, and bus-lanes-solver 0.0.6.
  - [Playwright/browser build and tests](https://github.com/tscircuit/eval/actions/runs/36911492930) passed.
  - [Type Check](https://github.com/tscircuit/eval/actions/runs/36911492597), [Format Check](https://github.com/tscircuit/eval/actions/runs/36911492360), [Webworker Imports](https://github.com/tscircuit/eval/actions/runs/36911492387), and [Packaged Fabricator Engine](https://github.com/tscircuit/eval/actions/runs/36911492356) passed.
- No CI jobs were rerun. No full routing or browser suite was run locally.

This PR combines the package updates from #4906 with the narrowly scoped CI fix. It does not enable auto-merge.

title: Keep exact import footprints when compact pin aliases collide
description: Prevents attribute merging between pins when compact pin aliases collide by maintaining original generated TSX and providing a CLI explanation for exact pin conflicts.
body:
A footprint can match the supplier's copper geometry above 98% while numbering its pads differently. Importing MCIMX6D6AVT08AD exposed this: adding `pin4` as an alias of `pin3` lets Core apply attributes from both physical pins, mixing neighboring input, ground, and power requirements.

Before compacting, check the complete pin map for a nonidentity alias that already names another target physical pin. Return `exact-pin-conflict` and keep the original generated TSX unchanged, with a CLI explanation. Identity maps and noncolliding aliases such as `thermalpad` to `pin57` still compact normally. No dependencies change.

Validation: all 25 tests in `bun test tests/lib/import` pass. The new swapped-numbering regression checks unchanged TSX, rendered pad geometry, and isolated receive/ground/power attributes; safe identity and thermal-pad mappings are also covered. Full `tsc --noEmit`, Biome formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

title: Fix clipped TI EVM schematic comparison snapshots
description: Fixes clipping issue in TI EVM schematic comparison snapshots by disabling normalization in the comparison helper, ensuring full canvas is preserved and preventing overlap of panels.
body:
The TI EVM schematic comparisons shrink each 1200×600 SVG canvas to 800×400 while leaving its drawing coordinates unscaled. Because the schematic SVGs have no `viewBox`, the bottom of the drawing is clipped and the two panels overlap.

Disable normalization in the comparison helper to preserve the renderer's full canvas. Update all four EVM schematic snapshots and add a regression snapshot with markers at the bottom-right of both panels, so clipping either drawing is detected.

The underlying dependency bug is tracked in https://github.com/tscircuit/stack-svgs/pull/2. This fixes the comparisons with the currently installed dependency.

Validation: `bun test` (66 pass, 0 fail), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, and `bun run format:check`. The new corner-marker regression fails with the previous normalization settings and passes with this change.

title: Repair the PCB goal board to zero DRC with incremental regional search
description: Board 1726 currently leaves about 55 relaxed DRC errors after Pipeline 9 routing. This change clears the goal repro to zero relaxed and declared-clearance errors, including after final power-trace expansion. Regional repair uses one effort-scaled policy for every board. It starts with a small allowance and earns additional bounded search only when a physically valid candidate reduces the whole-board reference DRC count. The previous route-count threshold is removed. Required-clearance projection runs before precision-margin refinement so exact-fit channels can be repaired without first asking for infeasible extra slack. All added repair work uses persistent Pipeline subsolvers. Exact, B01, regional search, clearance projection, reported-via merging, and repair04 path searches expose their active child and advance it once per parent step. No added nested solve(), synchronous child-step drains, or generators. The incremental repair04 classes are proposed upstream in repair04 fix PR 26(https:github.comtscircuitrepair04pull26), which targets main and includes the visual fixtures captured in repro PR 27(https:github.comtscircuitrepair04pull27). The repro PR captures 13 real PCB close-ups; the fix updates eight SVG snapshots with the same input panels, viewports, colors, and computed measurements. Both upstream PRs have green CI. This PR pins the immutable 422b7546 source commit and has no Bun patch or patchedDependencies. Existing synchronous APIs remain intact; the new classes use bounded preparation, search, and sweep batches. When a via pair needs more separation while touching fixed pads, projection removes the inward movement and retains feasible motion along the pad boundary. This applies only to via-to-via constraints; pad and wire constraints retain their existing movement behavior. Conservative rounding correction and uniform ray shortening handle rotated pads and board limits while preserving the exact physical guards, locked endpoints, displacement limits, and solver budgets. Validation (benchmark production 15783c90; 5dfa8557 changes only the inspected T113 expected snapshot; current head b0d74d07 replaces the patch with semantically identical upstream repair04 source): Final goal output: relaxed DRC 0, declared DRC with board clearance 0 after power expansion. Independent regional-output checks also report fixed-obstacle, newly worsened fixed-obstacle, and new via-pad violations 0. Saved production-stage replays: goal 0 in 273.9s (8 regions attempted, 6 accepted, 3,584 calls, 4,841,277 nodes); sample 14 0 in 64.9s, with every physical guard clear. These are stage replays, not cold full-pipeline benchmark times. Fresh installation of the upstream commit matches all 27 repair04 library files exactly. Nine focused consumer tests pass (1,257 assertions), along with full TypeScript checking and build. The upstream repair04 fix passes all 163 tests (30,491 assertions), typecheck, formatting, and its current PR CI(https:github.comtscircuitrepair04actionsruns36982046969). The upstream PR adds repro tests and snapshots while keeping all 27 library files byte-identical to the pinned source. Source review confirms the transfer preserves the tested patchs behavior. Reviewed and updated observed failing Linux goal, T113, and via-inner2 snapshots. Full goal CI on the patch-free head(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouteractionsruns36975615842job110738689115) passed all eight assertions in 827.5s, including both zero-DRC checks and the final snapshot. Controlled sample-14 pair(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouteractionsruns36970688436): main and PR both complete with DRC 0; 316.57s  293.51s (7.28). Joint repair takes 118.04s  99.71s. Vias 281  294 (4.63); odd-angle segments 726  709 (2.34). Configured detector reports no regressions. Full paired dataset 18(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouteractionsruns36970678706): main 1516 complete and DRC-clean, PR 1416. Sample 14 times out on both sides; sample 15 completes on main at 357.72s and hits the unchanged 360s limit on PR during length matching, after joint repair completed (86.33s  86.54s). The configured detector flags the completionDRC-rate loss. On the 14 mutually completed samples, mean vias rise 0.81 and odd-angle segments fall 4.68. Controlled sample-15 pair(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouteractionsruns36972258221): main and PR both complete with DRC 0; 261.51s  264.31s (1.07). HD iterations are identical (302,999); joint repair takes 66.58s  69.88s. Vias 349  356 (2.01); odd-angle segments 1,012  1,197 (18.28). The configured detector reports no regressions, but does not check odd angles. The full-run timeout and this style tradeoff remain recorded. Patch-free-head CI(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouteractionsruns36975615842) is green: all nine test shards, build, typecheck, format, code checks, and Vercel pass. Fullcontrolled-14 benchmarks used 15783c90; controlled-15 used 5dfa8557, with identical production source.
body:
Board 1726 currently leaves about 55 relaxed DRC errors after Pipeline 9 routing. This change clears the goal repro to **zero relaxed and declared-clearance errors**, including after final power-trace expansion.

Regional repair uses one effort-scaled policy for every board. It starts with a small allowance and earns additional bounded search only when a physically valid candidate reduces the whole-board reference DRC count. The previous route-count threshold is removed. Required-clearance projection runs before precision-margin refinement so exact-fit channels can be repaired without first asking for infeasible extra slack.

All added repair work uses persistent Pipeline subsolvers. Exact, B01, regional search, clearance projection, reported-via merging, and repair04 path searches expose their active child and advance it once per parent step. No added nested `solve()`, synchronous child-step drains, or generators. The incremental repair04 classes are proposed upstream in [repair04 fix PR #26](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/pull/26), which targets `main` and includes the visual fixtures captured in [repro PR #27](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/pull/27). The repro PR captures 13 real PCB close-ups; the fix updates eight SVG snapshots with the same input panels, viewports, colors, and computed measurements. Both upstream PRs have green CI. This PR pins the immutable `422b7546` source commit and has no Bun patch or `patchedDependencies`. Existing synchronous APIs remain intact; the new classes use bounded preparation, search, and sweep batches.

When a via pair needs more separation while touching fixed pads, projection removes the inward movement and retains feasible motion along the pad boundary. This applies only to via-to-via constraints; pad and wire constraints retain their existing movement behavior. Conservative rounding correction and uniform ray shortening handle rotated pads and board limits while preserving the exact physical guards, locked endpoints, displacement limits, and solver budgets.

Validation (benchmark production `15783c90`; `5dfa8557` changes only the inspected T113 expected snapshot; current head `b0d74d07` replaces the patch with semantically identical upstream repair04 source):

- Final goal output: relaxed DRC **0**, declared DRC with board clearance **0** after power expansion. Independent regional-output checks also report fixed-obstacle, newly worsened fixed-obstacle, and new via-pad violations **0**.
- Saved production-stage replays: goal **0** in 273.9s (8 regions attempted, 6 accepted, 3,584 calls, 4,841,277 nodes); sample 14 **0** in 64.9s, with every physical guard clear. These are stage replays, not cold full-pipeline benchmark times.
- Fresh installation of the upstream commit matches all 27 repair04 library files exactly. Nine focused consumer tests pass (1,257 assertions), along with full TypeScript checking and build. The upstream repair04 fix passes all 163 tests (30,491 assertions), typecheck, formatting, and its [current PR CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/actions/runs/36982046969). The upstream PR adds repro tests and snapshots while keeping all 27 library files byte-identical to the pinned source. Source review confirms the transfer preserves the tested patch's behavior.
- Reviewed and updated observed failing Linux goal, T113, and via-inner2 snapshots.
- [Full goal CI on the patch-free head](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36975615842/job/110738689115) passed all eight assertions in 827.5s, including both zero-DRC checks and the final snapshot.
- [Controlled sample-14 pair](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36970688436): main and PR both complete with DRC **0**; 316.57s → 293.51s (**−7.28%**). Joint repair takes 118.04s → 99.71s. Vias 281 → 294 (+4.63%); odd-angle segments 726 → 709 (−2.34%). Configured detector reports **no regressions**.
- [Full paired dataset 18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36970678706): main **15/16** complete and DRC-clean, PR **14/16**. Sample 14 times out on both sides; sample 15 completes on main at 357.72s and hits the unchanged 360s limit on PR during length matching, after joint repair completed (86.33s → 86.54s). The configured detector flags the completion/DRC-rate loss. On the 14 mutually completed samples, mean vias rise 0.81% and odd-angle segments fall 4.68%.
- [Controlled sample-15 pair](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36972258221): main and PR both complete with DRC **0**; 261.51s → 264.31s (+1.07%). HD iterations are identical (302,999); joint repair takes 66.58s → 69.88s. Vias 349 → 356 (+2.01%); odd-angle segments 1,012 → 1,197 (**+18.28%**). The configured detector reports no regressions, but does not check odd angles. The full-run timeout and this style tradeoff remain recorded.
- Patch-free-head [CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36975615842) is **green**: all nine test shards, build, typecheck, format, code checks, and Vercel pass. Full/controlled-14 benchmarks used `15783c90`; controlled-15 used `5dfa8557`, with identical production source.

title: prevent grid iteration limits from dropping schematic dividers
description: Fixes the issue where grid iteration limits prevent the generation of schematic dividers in the cm4 calculation.
body:
**motivation**
restore the missing cm4 schematic dividers reproduced in #45. this fix is stacked on that repro branch.

**before**
28 section bounds generate 186,634 segments, but the grid solver stops at its fixed 100,000-step limit and the public calculation returns no dividers.

**after**
size the grid budget for every input segment plus the phase transition and grid-construction steps. both regressions fail on the original code and pass with the six-line fix. refresh the same grid-stage snapshot to show all 28 completed section containers. all 35 tests, typecheck, touched-file formatting, and the library build pass. the full cm4 calculation produces 22 divider segments but still takes about 6½ minutes in existing downstream stages.

title: reproduce missing cm4 section dividers at the grid iteration limit

title: Display Circuit JSON errors with existing PoppyGL labels
description: Adds opt-in metadata to display Circuit JSON errors in 3D exports using PoppyGLs debug labels, preserving existing geometry and materials.
body:
Circuit JSON errors currently disappear from 3D exports, including unlocated placement errors when invalid flex boards fall back to flat geometry. Add opt-in `showErrors` metadata and a browser-safe adapter that displays it using released PoppyGL 0.0.29's existing debug labels.

`Scene3D.errorMessages` carries full original messages, and glTF/GLB stores them on the selected scene in `extras.tscircuit.errorMessages`. All Circuit JSON records with `error_type` and `message` are included, even before board geometry exists. Geometry, materials, binary buffers, bounds, and cameras remain unchanged; omitted/false options preserve existing output.

`getPoppyglErrorOverlayOptions(gltf, camera, options)` wraps the messages into stock PoppyGL debug labels at the top left. It uses the supplied camera to unproject screen layout anchors into world points, rather than claiming physical error locations. Recompute it after camera changes and forward its result to the renderer:

```ts
const errors = getPoppyglErrorOverlayOptions(gltf, camera, {
  width: renderOptions.width,
  height: renderOptions.height,
  supersampling: renderOptions.supersampling,
  debugFontSize: 20,
})
const { bitmap } = renderSceneFromGLTF(scene, {
  ...renderOptions,
  ...errors,
})
```

Supersampling keeps the requested final font size. Display-only ASCII fallbacks keep unsupported punctuation readable; unsupported Unicode uses visible codepoint text. Narrow viewports show a count for omitted rows while retaining all original messages in the metadata. Both browser entry points export the adapter and support source-only error scenes.

Validation: 167 tests pass (76,212 assertions across 113 files), TypeScript, build, and formatting pass, and all four Playwright browser tests pass. New tests verify metadata-only glTF/GLB changes, byte-identical geometry buffers, input/camera immutability, selected-scene metadata, translated cameras and camera orbits, supersampling 1/2/3, long tokens, Unicode, narrow overflow, both browser exports, disabled/no-error output, and actual stock rendering before geometry exists. Snapshot tests load actual exported GLBs through released PoppyGL's public loader and renderer; the snapshots were visually reviewed. The immutable built package was also rendered with stock PoppyGL 0.0.29.

![Translated and flex boards with existing PoppyGL error labels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/e374a02812e1db62d9846d58aa8676e45d8a1ae3/tests/snapshot/__snapshots__/show-errors.snap.png)

Supports the flex diagnostics in [tscircuit/tscircuit#5277](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277) and [core#4279](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4279).

title: fix: preserve flex exports for declared folding limitations
description: Fixes GLTFGLB export failures for unsupported PCB bends and rigid objects crossing a bend zone by retaining existing flat geometry for declared limitations while allowing unexpected errors to propagate.
body:
Unsupported PCB bends and rigid objects crossing a bend zone currently abort GLTF/GLB export, including Circuit JSON that core can render with placement errors. Use the explicit folding results from [flex-utils #6](https://github.com/tscircuit/flex-utils/pull/6) to retain the existing flat geometry for those declared limitations while allowing unexpected errors to propagate.

- Activate the board fold only after construction and surface deformation both succeed. Unsupported boards keep their CAD and stiffeners flat, including legacy boards whose incomplete bend spans are discovered during deformation.
- Carry CAD and debug bounding boxes through shared rigid-mesh folding. Validate the PCB mount independently of model extents so an offset model cannot hide an invalid mount.
- Construct each stiffener's flat mesh once and use the shared stiffener folding result, preserving its existing outline anchor. An invalid rigid object stays flat while the board and valid objects still fold.
- Keep pre-folded CAD normalization strict: its flat pose requires a valid fold and flat PCB mount reference. Circuit JSON remains unchanged, and existing model/layer rotations, winding, normals, UVs, and material metadata are preserved.

Addresses the export paths for items 2 and 3 of [tscircuit#5277](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277), alongside [core #4279](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4279). Independent nonparallel physical folds remain unsupported.

Uses the published `@tscircuit/flex-utils@0.0.7` release from merged flex-utils #6. Its runtime and declarations match the tested preview byte for byte.

Validation: all 154 tests pass (76,017 assertions), including actual emitted GLB geometry checks, pre-folded/mixed inputs, offset mounts, off-axis rotations on both layers, and PoppyGL/toMatchPngSnapshot coverage. Existing snapshots are unchanged and visually checked. The new unexpected-error regression confirms failures propagate through both GLTF frame adapters. Five original fallback regressions fail on the original converter, and the offset-CAD regression fails without mount validation. After adopting the published release, dependency installation with scripts disabled, all 14 focused tests (75,453 assertions), TypeScript, build, and formatting pass with unchanged snapshots.

The visual test uses `convertCircuitJsonToGltf` → PoppyGL → the existing `toMatchPngSnapshot` matcher, with RL/RR labels in the exported board texture. title: Make A03 path scores deterministic across platforms
description: Fixes inconsistency in A03 path scoring between macOS and Linux by standardizing vector length calculations, ensuring reproducible routing decisions across platforms.
body:
A03 scores grid candidates using `Math.hypot`. For bugreport107's `cmn_21` input, that distance differs by one ULP between macOS and Linux for some candidate vectors. The heap compares the resulting scores exactly, so the platforms choose different turns and the downstream DRC totals diverge.

Use one scaled vector-length helper for both A03 movement cost and its pathfinding heuristic. Export that helper for the autorouter's clearance subdivision; [tscircuit-autorouter#2789](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2789) imports it and removes the local copy. This changes the distance implementation, not clearance requirements or route-specific conditions.

The production A03 input is captured as a focused regression. The route now takes the same grid turn on macOS and Linux. The affected A03 snapshot is updated. On the full board, the linked autorouter PR produces 38 relaxed DRC errors on both platforms (previously 32 on macOS and 38 on Linux). This is a reproducibility fix, not a DRC-count improvement.

Validation: `bun run build`; `BUN_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bun test` (108 pass, 2 existing skips); focused vector-length and bugreport107 A03 tests pass on both macOS and Linux arm64. CI format, test, and type checks pass.

A last-bit distance difference can change which candidate the priority queue expands first, producing a different turn. This PR uses the same calculation for both movement costs and the remaining-distance heuristic so that routing decisions are reproducible across platforms. It does not relax clearance rules or promise a lower DRC count.

These are the existing **sample002 test snapshots**, not full-board bugreport107 images. The separate captured bugreport107 regression checks the affected grid turn directly. Both images are linked from existing commits; no visualization files are added by this description update.

title: feat: detect capacitors separated from connected chip pins
description: Adds a new solver to detect capacitors that are placed far from their connected chip pins, ensuring they are readable beside those pins for better schematic clarity.
body:
Stacked on #158.

Adds `ChipPinPairCapacitorPlacementSolver` / `CapacitorSeparatedFromChipPins`. A capacitor whose terminals each connect exclusively to a different pin of the same chip should be readable beside those pins. The rule flags a distant capacitor wholly across the chip from both connected pins, following their actual sides.

Recognition uses component types and connectivity. Power/ground exclusions use structured pin attributes and net flags; pin names, net names, reference designators, and part numbers are not used for detection. The rule does not classify the capacitor's electrical function. Shared nets, different chips, separate blocks, and unpopulated parts are excluded. Compact, mirrored, and rotated layouts are accepted.

The complete TSX NEMA23 repro reports one finding for `C_CP`, with numbered highlights in its existing full-sheet snapshot. Below: [TI DRV8462 Figure 8-1](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/drv8462.pdf#page=101), the TSX repro, and the same TSX with only the capacitor moved/rotated. Connectivity is preserved and the finding clears; traces are regenerated.

![TI reference, TSX repro, and placement correction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/e50872c60691059ec12b06eb02ea2eb09737f0d9/reference-tsx-before-after.png)

title: docs: forbid name checks for semantic meaning
description: Adds a directive to AGENTS.md forbidding the use of string checks on names or labels to establish semantic meaning or infer electrical roles, requiring explicit typed metadata and connectivitytopology instead.
body:
The [review on #159](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/pull/159#pullrequestreview-5384494003) points out that matching a pin name does not establish a capacitor's electrical role. Add one directive to `AGENTS.md` forbidding name/label string checks for semantic meaning or electrical roles, requiring explicit typed metadata and connectivity/topology, and skipping cases with insufficient evidence.

## Existing rules using this antipattern

Audited `lib/solvers` and their shared utilities on `main` at `b7238b0`. These existing rules still derive semantic decisions from names or `port_hints`, even where they also check component types or topology:

| Rule | Existing name-based semantic check |
| --- | --- |
| [ResetNetworkGroupingSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/ResetNetworkGroupingSolver/ResetNetworkGroupingSolver.ts#L247) | Matches `RESET`/`RST` variants in pin names or hints to declare a reset network. |
| [UsbSeriesResistorPlacementSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/UsbSeriesResistorPlacementSolver/UsbSeriesResistorPlacementSolver.ts#L198) | Matches `DP`, `D+`, `DM`, `DN`, `D-`, and related aliases to declare USB positive/negative roles. |
| [RegulatorInputOutputCapacitorPlacementSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/RegulatorInputOutputCapacitorPlacementSolver/RegulatorInputOutputCapacitorPlacementSolver.ts#L188) | Matches `VIN`/`IN`/`INPUT`, `VOUT`/`OUT`/`OUTPUT`, ground names, and control names to classify a chip as a regulator. |
| [CurrentSenseShuntPlacementSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/CurrentSenseShuntPlacementSolver/CurrentSenseShuntPlacementSolver.ts#L47) | Requires named positive/negative inputs, output, supply, and ground pins to identify a current-sense amplifier (`inputRole`/`hasHint`). |
| [RelayFlybackDiodePlacementSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/RelayFlybackDiodePlacementSolver/RelayFlybackDiodePlacementSolver.ts#L178) | Uses named coil/contact pairs to identify relays; also matches anode/cathode and base/collector/emitter aliases to infer diode polarity and driver terminal roles. |
| [MosfetGateNetworkPlacementSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/MosfetGateNetworkPlacementSolver/MosfetGateNetworkPlacementSolver.ts#L118) | Matches `G`/`GATE`, `S`/`SOURCE`, and `D`/`DRAIN` aliases to infer terminal roles, including for generic `simple_chip` components. |
| [FeedbackNetworkPlacementSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/FeedbackNetworkPlacementSolver/FeedbackNetworkPlacementSolver.ts#L38) | Uses `namedPort("output")` and `namedPort("inverting_input")` to establish feedback terminal roles. |
| [LowSideTransistorPlacementSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/LowSideTransistorPlacementSolver/LowSideTransistorPlacementSolver.ts#L48) | Uses `namedPort` for `base`/`collector`/`emitter` and, at lines 113–114, `anode`/`cathode` to establish terminal roles and clamp polarity. |
| [CapacitorOrientationSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/CapacitorOrientationSolver/CapacitorOrientationSolver.ts#L76) | Exempts feedback capacitors through `PlacementNetworkIndex.isDirectOpAmpFeedback`, which identifies `output`, `inverting_input`, and `non_inverting_input` by name. |
| [TraceSimplificationSolver](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/solvers/TraceSimplificationSolver/TraceSimplificationSolver.ts#L101) | Uses reference-designator prefixes `U` and `C`/`R` to infer IC versus passive components when generating and prioritizing move candidates. |

The shared [`PlacementNetworkIndex.namedPort`](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/utils/placement-network-index.ts#L78) compares `port.name` and `port_hints` to literal strings; [`isDirectOpAmpFeedback`](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/b7238b0f421af6e12f4bb00fa2247311489e743a/lib/utils/placement-network-index.ts#L98) uses it for feedback classification. That is the dependency behind the feedback, low-side transistor, and capacitor-orientation entries above.

The proposed [`ChargePumpCapacitorPlacementSolver` in #159](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/330e41bcdc91b15d9431ab59ee0314dcdb8f96e4/lib/solvers/ChargePumpCapacitorPlacementSolver/ChargePumpCapacitorPlacementSolver.ts#L43) likewise matches `CPH`/`CPL` in pin names/hints to infer a charge-pump capacitor. It is open and is not part of the audited `main` snapshot.

This PR adds only the directive. The listed implementations remain follow-up work. Display text, label-to-port lookup for geometry, and explicit schema fields such as `ftype` and power/ground flags are distinct from inferring electrical meaning from a name.

- Verified the diff adds exactly one directive to `AGENTS.md`.
- Manually checked the linked name-based decisions and shared-helper callers.
- Runtime tests were not run for this documentation-only change.

title: Publish modelprinter to npm using trusted publishing
description: Changes the publishing workflow of the modelprinter package to publish to the public npm registry instead of GitHub Packages, enabling dependency updates for jscad-electronics.
body:
Merging modelprinter did not publish its new specifications to npm: both the workflow and package `publishConfig` targeted GitHub Packages, the workflow only ran for releases/manual dispatch, and its GitHub token was not npm authentication. npmjs.com still only offers 0.0.2, blocking jscad-electronics' dependency update.

Switch `.github/workflows/publish.yml` to the same npm OIDC/pver release pattern already working in jscad-electronics: publish on pushes to `main` or manual dispatch, grant `id-token: write`, use Node 24 on a GitHub-hosted runner, increment/publish the version with `pver release`, and commit the version update. Package publishing now explicitly targets the public npm registry. Tests, typecheck, formatting, build, and package inspection run before release.

**Before merging:** configure an npm trusted publisher for `@tscircuit/modelprinter` with GitHub owner `tscircuit`, repository `modelprinter`, workflow filename `publish.yml`, no environment, and permission for direct `npm publish`. The package settings require maintainer login/2FA; no npm token or interactive login is needed in CI. Exact instructions are in `docs/publishing.md`.

With the repository at 0.0.3, pver's next release will be 0.0.4. After publication, [jscad-electronics PR #399](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/399) must target the actual released version and regenerate its lockfile.

Validation: all 6 parameter tests pass; typecheck, format check, and build pass. npm publish dry-run confirms `https://registry.npmjs.org/` and public access. Live OIDC publishing is untested until the npm trusted publisher is configured and this workflow runs from main. No package was published while preparing this PR.

title: Project coupled clearance and respect rounded pad geometry
description: Dense routing can trap an individual trace behind neighboring tracks that also need to move. Add negotiateTraceClearance, a bounded regional operation that keeps pads, collars, locked via transitions and immutable copper fixed while negotiating space between movable spans. Its congestion cost estimates the geometric work of rerouting a blocking span. Searches share the callers node and call budgets; returned candidates require atomic DRC and physical validation. An explicit drill diameter reserves hole clearance even when two vias connect disjoint layers. Export relaxTraceClearance as a complementary bounded operation that preserves fixed contacts, shared junctions, widths, vertices and via transition indices. It uses the configured clearance without an extra fixed margin, handles wire vertices inside pads, and permits an existing via-pad contact to improve only when unchanged route topology proves via correspondence. New contacts, altered spans, changed diameters and ambiguous correspondence are rejected. Regional repair directs indexed contacts to their owning routes. Existing via-pad contacts receive direct position candidates under the existing permissions and work budget. A uses conservative pad envelopes consistent with the DRC scorer; final physical guards retain actual rotated and rounded pad geometry. Immutable through-obstacle spans are preserved across repair collars. The nested DRC dependency includes current pad rotations with immutable geometry, static-query and dynamic-query reuse (dependency PR 108(https:github.comtscircuithigh-density-repair03pull108)). Fixed anchors include the endpoints of movable spans. Separate branch endpoints can share an immutable electrical attachment only when they lie inside the same physical pad on a supported layer and declare the same net. Circular plated-hole copper retains its circular planning outline; SMT pad envelopes remain conservative. Feasible incumbent spans preserve their existing vertices and consume no A nodes. Incumbent validation and search expansion both enforce mechanical drill spacing within the same route, using the callers actual hole diameter. Consecutive layer transitions at exactly the same XY location share one physical hole. Invalid hole dimensions and non-colocated via transitions are rejected. Validation: all 122 tests pass (13,075 assertions) and full typechecking passes. All three CI jobs pass at dde0b003ccd0194421112bdaa8015f08cf27634b: Bun Test, Type Check and Format Check. New regressions cover coupled pad escapes, rerouting cost, locked vias, boundary preservation, exhausted searches, drill spacing across disjoint layers, fixed junction sites, plated-hole corners and shared physical pad attachments. Existing regressions cover measured clearance, exact-fit corridors, conservative oval corners, interior pad contacts and correspondence-verified via movement. CI-reported layout changes were applied directly and checked for equivalent emitted JavaScript. Verified native Joint replays of the current update reach zero reference DRC on samples 6, 12, 13 and 15, with no new fixed-geometry or via-pad violations. Compared with the published shared-pad baseline, samples 13 and 15 use 36 and 11 fewer search nodes respectively. Sample 2 still has two residual pad contacts at the existing work limit; its remaining region can be repaired within 69,429 additional nodes, which is not counted as a completed production pass. These targeted runs are not a completed same-machine dataset benchmark. The autorouter integration and full benchmark remain in progress in autorouter PR 2447(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterpull2447). The caller performs full reference validation before accepting candidates; partial routes are never labeled clean.
body:
Dense routing can trap an individual trace behind neighboring tracks that also need to move. Add `negotiateTraceClearance`, a bounded regional operation that keeps pads, collars, locked via transitions and immutable copper fixed while negotiating space between movable spans. Its congestion cost estimates the geometric work of rerouting a blocking span. Searches share the caller's node and call budgets; returned candidates require atomic DRC and physical validation. An explicit drill diameter reserves hole clearance even when two vias connect disjoint layers.

Export `relaxTraceClearance` as a complementary bounded operation that preserves fixed contacts, shared junctions, widths, vertices and via transition indices. It uses the configured clearance without an extra fixed margin, handles wire vertices inside pads, and permits an existing via-pad contact to improve only when unchanged route topology proves via correspondence. New contacts, altered spans, changed diameters and ambiguous correspondence are rejected.

Regional repair directs indexed contacts to their owning routes. Existing via-pad contacts receive direct position candidates under the existing permissions and work budget. A* uses conservative pad envelopes consistent with the DRC scorer; final physical guards retain actual rotated and rounded pad geometry. Immutable through-obstacle spans are preserved across repair collars. The nested DRC dependency includes current pad rotations with immutable geometry, static-query and dynamic-query reuse ([dependency PR #108](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/108)).

Fixed anchors include the endpoints of movable spans. Separate branch endpoints can share an immutable electrical attachment only when they lie inside the same physical pad on a supported layer and declare the same net. Circular plated-hole copper retains its circular planning outline; SMT pad envelopes remain conservative.

Feasible incumbent spans preserve their existing vertices and consume no A* nodes. Incumbent validation and search expansion both enforce mechanical drill spacing within the same route, using the caller's actual hole diameter. Consecutive layer transitions at exactly the same XY location share one physical hole. Invalid hole dimensions and non-colocated via transitions are rejected.

Validation: all 122 tests pass (13,075 assertions) and full typechecking passes. All three CI jobs pass at dde0b003ccd0194421112bdaa8015f08cf27634b: Bun Test, Type Check and Format Check. New regressions cover coupled pad escapes, rerouting cost, locked vias, boundary preservation, exhausted searches, drill spacing across disjoint layers, fixed junction sites, plated-hole corners and shared physical pad attachments. Existing regressions cover measured clearance, exact-fit corridors, conservative oval corners, interior pad contacts and correspondence-verified via movement. CI-reported layout changes were applied directly and checked for equivalent emitted JavaScript.

Verified native Joint replays of the current update reach zero reference DRC on samples 6, 12, 13 and 15, with no new fixed-geometry or via-pad violations. Compared with the published shared-pad baseline, samples 13 and 15 use 36% and 11% fewer search nodes respectively. Sample 2 still has two residual pad contacts at the existing work limit; its remaining region can be repaired within 69,429 additional nodes, which is not counted as a completed production pass. These targeted runs are not a completed same-machine dataset benchmark. The autorouter integration and full benchmark remain in progress in [autorouter PR #2447](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2447). The caller performs full reference validation before accepting candidates; partial routes are never labeled clean.

title: Cache bounded repair checks and expose deterministic work limits
description: Dense bounded repairs repeatedly convert unchanged copper and query the same obstacles. This change reuses that immutable geometry and exposes deterministic work limits so Pipeline9 can bound unsuccessful searches. Reuse converted traces, fixed-obstacle results, physical-via geometry, static pad contacts and prepared A obstacles within each solver. Preserve route indices, alias ownership, validation order and independent returned errors. Pin repair03 PR 100 at bbc6ea4b9a1ef11e6e6c827bdad514b37727d0df. The engine receives solver-owned immutable context and trace objects. Dynamic buckets, route order and global via ownership are rebuilt for each evaluation; the dependency flags remain disabled by default. Add optional maxCandidateAttempts and maxPathSearchNodes. Attempts include yielded proposals rejected by permissions; nodes count actual heap pops across searches and accepted states. Budget completion retains validated progress and reports remaining DRC. Invalid geometry and solver failures still surface. Repair operates on the supplied bounded region. body:
Dense bounded repairs repeatedly convert unchanged copper and query the same obstacles. This change reuses that immutable geometry and exposes deterministic work limits so Pipeline9 can bound unsuccessful searches.

- Reuse converted traces, fixed-obstacle results, physical-via geometry, static pad contacts and prepared A* obstacles within each solver. Preserve route indices, alias ownership, validation order and independent returned errors.
- Pin [repair03 PR #100](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/100) at `bbc6ea4b9a1ef11e6e6c827bdad514b37727d0df`. Enable its static obstacle-net membership cache, immutable trace geometry and ordered spatial-query reuse, and conservative rectangular-obstacle precheck. The engine receives solver-owned immutable context and trace objects. Dynamic buckets, route order and global via ownership are rebuilt for each evaluation; the dependency flags remain disabled by default.
- Reuse up to 128 exact duplicate proposal scores until an accepted route changes. Validate candidate copper and mandatory via-pad clearance before indexed scoring.
- Add optional `maxCandidateAttempts` and `maxPathSearchNodes`. Attempts include yielded proposals rejected by permissions; nodes count actual heap pops across searches and accepted states. Budget completion retains validated progress and reports remaining DRC. Invalid geometry and solver failures still surface.

Repair operates on the supplied bounded region. Endpoint and boundary-collar protection, fixed copper, via permissions, new via-pad rejection, candidate order and DRC acceptance rules are preserved. Default search budgets remain unchanged in this package; Pipeline9 selects its policy.

Each pair preserved exact routes, statistics and outcomes. title: Fix incremental clearance repair with real-region visual repros
description: Real PCB via pairs can remain too close when fixed pads block their normal separation direction. This adds incremental clearance subsolvers and preserves feasible tangent motion for via-to-via separation, with conservative rounding and board-limit handling. Existing synchronous APIs remain unchanged.
body:
Real PCB via pairs can remain too close when fixed pads block their normal separation direction. This adds incremental clearance subsolvers and preserves feasible tangent motion for via-to-via separation, with conservative rounding and board-limit handling. Existing synchronous APIs remain unchanged.

**Targets `main`.** [Visual repro PR #27](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/pull/27) records 13 baseline SVG snapshots from eight Board1726 regions and five SRJ18 sample14 views. This PR runs the same fixtures through the stepped projection solver and updates eight expected SVGs; five remain byte-identical. Fixed viewports, net colors, physical widths/drills, and target markers make the image diff reflect the geometry and computed measurements.

| Real region | Synchronous candidate → incremental candidate |
| --- | --- |
| Board1726 connector pads | Focus DRC **9 → 5**; distinct via-pair contacts **3 → 0** |
| Board1726 left pad P_B12 | Focus DRC **5 → 2**; selected net34/net20 copper gap **0.067 → 0.103 mm** |
| Board1726 power via/trace | Focus DRC **6 → 5**, using the native checker's existing clearance tolerance |
| Sample14 via60/trace59 | Focus DRC **22 → 21**; targeted gap **0.079 → 0.189 mm** |

The images label projection candidates and retain remaining real errors. They do not claim every individual crop is a fully repaired board. The connector's existing outside-view fixed contact is retained. Complete routing still requires the caller's physical validation and DRC-based candidate acceptance; the consumer [autorouter PR #2811](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2811) reaches zero public and declared DRC on Board1726.

`FindClearancePathSolver` preserves its frontier and bounds preparation/search (at most 128 heap pops per search step). `NegotiateTraceClearanceSolver` exposes its active child, advances it once per parent step, and reserves enough child iterations for preparation. `RelaxTraceClearanceSolver` batches pair/obstacle preparation and advances one sweep at a time. Tangent motion applies only to via-pair constraints; pad/wire constraints keep their existing movement behavior. No added generators, nested `solve()`, or synchronous child-step drains in production code.

Validation: all **163 tests / 30,491 assertions** pass, including parity/golden accounting, heap-pop limits, preloaded tiny-budget preparation, rotated-pad physical guards, and the 13 visual repros. TypeScript and formatting pass. The targeted sample14 gap and cleared connector pairs also have direct assertions. Baseline and fixed images were rendered and inspected; input primitives, viewports, and legends remain identical across all 13 comparisons. The [current fix CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/actions/runs/36982046969) and [repro CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/actions/runs/36981094015) are green.

All 27 library files are byte-identical to the upstream `422b7546` commit already installed by autorouter PR #2811 without a Bun patch. Its full CI is [green](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36975615842), including the [zero-DRC goal test](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36975615842/job/110738689115). The visual repros add tests and snapshots around that same library source. The earlier dataset18 timeout and sample15 routing-style tradeoff remain documented in the consumer PR. No PR has been merged.

body:
The wide tuning banks left large gaps between traces and pushed AM3352/RAM routes far from the chip-to-chip centerline. This packs rounded meanders into narrower banks, reducing overall copper bounding area by **31–39%**, signal-only bounds by **32–39%**, and total copper length by **12–15%** across all four placements.

Stacked on #12 (`solver/four-placements-complete`). No new JSX props or solver dependency changes.

### Implementation

- Try dense rounded cells in the existing corridor, then compact banks before wider fallbacks. Use available run length and minimum bend radius to choose cell counts; paired cells share the same centerline and preserve both rail radii.
- Try the unchanged corridor once before spending work on every small corner-trim variation. The full refinement search remains available as a fallback.
- Add overall/per-layer copper bounds and the maximum middle-region offset from the physical chip-center axis to the benchmark. Bounds include wire radii and via pads. Both overall bounds (including fixed power) and signal-only bounds are reported.

### Measured results

Fresh serial runs on the user’s macOS arm64 computer, Bun 1.3.2. Baseline is #12 at `d8f004d`; no saved signal geometry is replayed.

| Placement | Overall bounds area (mm²) | Reduction | Signal-only reduction | Middle offset (mm) | Routing | Total with validation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Control | 1104.2 → 725.1 | 34.3% | 34.3% | 13.60 → 9.20 | 15.326 s | 17.587 s |
| Right | 1174.3 → 804.2 | 31.5% | 32.2% | 17.00 → 12.50 | 19.055 s | 24.753 s |
| Left | 1615.0 → 1022.2 | 36.7% | 35.5% | 22.06 → 14.86 | 21.383 s | 27.463 s |
| Above | 1524.6 → 930.9 | 38.9% | 38.9% | 18.40 → 11.46 | 26.453 s | 31.397 s |

**All four pass 47/47 connectivity, native DRC, pad-to-pad matching, and zero exterior pair separation.** All 161 fixed power dogbones and their provenance remain unchanged. Every byte bus stays within 0.635 mm skew and every pair within 0.127 mm (numerical epsilon included). Ordinary/curved angle checks pass. Timing claims are for the measured computer; shared CI runners use the existing larger budget.

### Routed snapshots

Generated by a separate fresh run; all four must pass validation before the exporter writes any image. Each completed image was visually inspected.

### Validation

- `./benchmark.sh --timeout-seconds 30 --require-all-solved`: 4/4 pass.
- Packed single/pair tuning regressions check lower height, unchanged endpoints, DRC, self-clearance, skew, coupling, and conventional angles. The integrated matcher regression checks that packing is enabled automatically.
- Footprint tests cover wire/via radii, per-layer envelopes, and translated/rotated package centerlines.

title: Route all four powered AM3352 placements with coupled pairs under 30 seconds
description: The four AM3352RAM placements now compute all 47 signal routes, match their lengths, and keep differential pairs together outside native packagefanout regions. All four finish under 30 seconds on the measured machine, including final validation. The 161 supplied VCCGND dogbones remain immutable obstacles.
body:
The four AM3352/RAM placements now compute all 47 signal routes, match their lengths, and keep differential pairs together outside native package/fanout regions. All four finish under 30 seconds on the measured machine, including final validation. The 161 supplied VCC/GND dogbones remain immutable obstacles.

Stacked on #10 (`benchmark/am3352-ram-placements`). No saved signal geometry or board/net-name lookup is used.

### Routing changes

- Route pairs as shared corridors and shared smooth tuning curves; independently audit both rails outside physical package/fanout regions, including approaches and meanders.
- For backward-facing packages, repair an unfinished bus together with its newly generated signal dogbones. Supplied fanout handoffs are never dogboned again. Preserve existing internal compensation when extending pair coupling, then rematch without increasing the bus length target.
- Reuse request-local spatial/search data, bound child searches, and stabilize aligned corridors against floating-point coordinate noise. All searches remain cancellable.
- Validate native output shape, complete connectivity, continuous DRC, full pad-to-pad matching, exterior coupling, and ordinary/curved corner geometry. Export review images only after all four pass.

### Four-placement benchmark

`./benchmark.sh --timeout-seconds 30 --require-all-solved`

Fresh serial processes on macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.2. AM3352 stays at (0, 0); RAM moves without rotation. Routing time includes tuning; total includes fixture and native output validation.

| RAM placement (mm) | Routing | Total | Signals | Native DRC | Byte 0 / byte 1 skew | DQS0 / DQS1 / clock skew |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Control (0, -27) | 12.396 s | 14.187 s | 47/47 | Pass | 0.635 / 0.635 mm | 0.127 / 0.127 / 0.073 mm |
| Right (27, 0) | 16.635 s | 18.149 s | 47/47 | Pass | 0.635 / 0.635 mm | 0.127 / 0.127 / 0.103 mm |
| Left (-27, 0) | 17.949 s | 20.989 s | 47/47 | Pass | 0.635 / 0.635 mm | 0.029 / 0.127 / 0.105 mm |
| Above (0, 27) | 21.126 s | 23.322 s | 47/47 | Pass | 0.635 / 0.635 mm | 0.127 / 0.127 / 0.127 mm |

All four have **zero exterior pair separation**, acute corners, sharp curve corners, illegal ordinary corners, and non-octilinear ordinary segments. Tolerances include floating-point epsilon. Timings vary by machine; CI uses ordinary Ubuntu runners.

The checked-in benchmark JSON includes length, detour, turn, clearance, and coupling measurements. The four images were generated by a separate fresh solve and each was visually inspected. Only completed routes are included.

The [PR benchmark job](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/36991534669) completes all four with identical reported copper quality: control 28.361 s, right 33.882 s, left 38.278 s, above 43.260 s.
