title: Defer GPU device destruction to avoid Chrome worker shutdown hangs
description: Defers GPU device destruction until queued work settles to prevent Chrome from becoming unresponsive during WebGPU worker failure cleanup.
body:
Switching the F1C100S board to PCB can leave Chrome unresponsive during WebGPU worker failure cleanup. Defer `GPUDevice.destroy()` until queued work settles, including rejection/device loss, while keeping `dispose()` immediate and idempotent for callers. This preserves the existing diagnostic/failure path and avoids changing geometry behavior.

Adds two cleanup regression tests and a pinned full-site Chrome reproduction: run `python3 scripts/repro-chrome-page-hang.py`, open its baseline/patched URLs, then click PCB. Main-thread heartbeats are printed independently of browser automation. The script also isolates PostHog and Sentry. The existing library-only probe now exercises immediate shutdown and explicitly states that it has not reproduced the full-site freeze.

Validation: 66 unit tests pass; type checking, build, and formatting pass. Multiple unchanged Chrome controls stopped their heartbeat after entering PCB; two controls with this exact queued cleanup remained responsive for several minutes with both analytics SDKs enabled. Recorded evidence is in `tests/repro/chrome-page-hang-evidence.json`. Removing only PostHog also prevented the hang in the integration control; removing only Sentry did not. No SDK-internal or Chrome root cause has been established, and the standalone probe is not a confirmed freeze reproduction.

README files are unchanged; the existing AGENTS.md prohibition remains in place.

title: Fix F1C100S PCB preview failure from breakout routing points
description: Fixes PCB preview failure caused by unsupported breakout routing points in the F1C100S board rendering process.
body:
The PCB preview for [seveibar/f1c100s-linux-dev-board v1.9.2](https://tscircuit.com/seveibar/f1c100s-linux-dev-board#pcb) stops with `Unsupported WebGPU geometry: pcb_breakout_point`. Its published Circuit JSON contains 130 breakout points; the compiler reports each as unsupported and pcb-viewer's worker rejects the entire scene.

Treat `pcb_breakout_point` as routing metadata alongside PCB ports and trace hints. Keep its element ID in the scene without generating geometry or diagnostics. Add an unchanged four-element subset of the published board and two regression tests that verify metadata-only compilation, identical meshes, and preserved highlighting IDs. Regenerate the tracked distribution bundle. Add an AGENTS.md instruction prohibiting README edits. Include a manual worker reproduction that downloads the exact published board and compares the original distribution bundle with the patched source in Google Chrome.

Chrome reproduction:

1. Run `bun scripts/prepare-f1c100s-repro.ts`, then `bun run dev`.
2. Open `/tests/repro/f1c100s.html?baseline` in Google Chrome and click **Render published board**. The worker compiles the board, rejects its 130 diagnostics, disposes its drawer, and the UI removes the canvas and terminates the worker, matching pcb-viewer's error path.
3. Compare `/tests/repro/f1c100s.html?patched`: the board renders with zero diagnostics and the heartbeat continues.

On Google Chrome 154.0.8037.58 on this Mac, the production page became unresponsive after loading. The isolated baseline worker reproduction also became unresponsive to DOM inspection, while the patched worker and patched PCBViewer remained responsive. The original renderer can draw the same geometry without freezing when diagnostics are ignored. The patch removes the board-specific error that sends pcb-viewer into the failing teardown path; it does not change generic GPU-device disposal. Baseline freezes are intermittent: a subsequent isolated run completed cleanup with a continuing heartbeat. A separate full-viewer baseline run stopped sending its independent heartbeat after tick 10 and remained unresponsive to inspection. The patched runs remained responsive. This establishes a rendering-error fix and a candidate fix for the observed failure path, rather than a guarantee that every Chrome freeze has the same cause. The production deployment has not been modified.

Validation:

- Both new regression tests fail on the original compiler and pass with the fix.
- `bun run test`: 64 passed; type checking, build, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- `bun run test:visual` with SwiftShader: all 20 snapshots passed.
- `bun run test:snapshots` with SwiftShader: all 597 feature snapshots passed; no baselines changed.
- `bun run test:parity-layout`: all 597 pairs passed at desktop and narrow widths.
- The full published board renders with zero diagnostics instead of 130; its WebGPU PNG is byte-identical before and after the change.
- A test browser loading the live page with the locally compiled patched PCB worker renders successfully and redraws after resizing, without worker or page errors. The deployed site was not modified.

The snapshot harness separately reports 154 passing and 10 failing assertions in the untouched upstream Canvas reference suite, and 520 SVG/WebGPU parity mismatches. Snapshot regression success is not a claim of full renderer parity. The hardware-adapter visual run failed during repeated device creation on this machine; the SwiftShader run passed.


PostHog comparison on the deployed site in Google Chrome: opted out of capture before reloading and switched Files → PCB twice; both runs remained responsive. Restored the original preference and repeated three times, including one with DevTools closed; those also remained responsive. The unsupported breakout-point error appeared in both conditions. No session recorder was loaded in either condition. This does not establish PostHog as the cause of the intermittent freezes. Restored the browser preference and removed temporary diagnostics.

title: Support independent and nested PCB bend axes
description: Allows independent regions to fold about different axes and supports nested folds, enhancing the flexibility of PCB design.
body:
Finite bends on separate PCB arms are currently rejected whenever their moving directions differ. Allow independent regions to fold about different axes, and allow a nested fold to move with its parent's rigid distal region. This supports both the two outward arms and the original body-moving arrangement from [tscircuit#5277](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277).

Derive fold order from finite moving-region containment: fold children first, then carry them with their parents. A nested region must lie entirely beyond its parent's curved strip. Edge-aware polygon containment handles concave outlines. Partially overlapping regions, equal regions, and intersecting curved strips still return typed folding errors. Calls without a board outline retain the parallel, same-moving-direction requirement.

The existing point, direction, inverse CAD, surface, and rigid-mesh transforms are reused. Geometry does not depend on record order, endpoint direction, or outline winding. The original fixture's vertical `bend_side: "left"` deliberately moves the main body; its snapshot preserves that direction and shows the right tip staying fixed.

Validation: all 32 tests pass (2,029 assertions), including existing visual baselines, parallel serial folds, opposite moving directions, negative angles, rigid forward/inverse transforms, incompatible intersections, and concave containment. TypeScript, build, formatting, and diff checks pass. Three new PNG snapshots use the existing `toMatchPngSnapshot`/PoppyGL conventions and were visually inspected. No README changes.

Independent arms:

![Independent arms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/flex-utils/4d3fa839b3663308ee56b258c6cc5254026aaed8/tests/__snapshots__/nonparallel-independent-arms.snap.png)

Original body-moving arrangement:

![Nested body fold](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/flex-utils/4d3fa839b3663308ee56b258c6cc5254026aaed8/tests/__snapshots__/nonparallel-nested-body.snap.png)

Full GitHub CI passes for the source commit, including tests, typecheck, and build. Downstream consumer PRs use immutable built preview `dbe07e49220c40ec3f0109b7d566561ce5e58bc9` until this helper is merged and released.

title: Expose explicit results for unsupported PCB folds
description: Add explicit shared folding results for unsupported PCB folds to allow renderers to retain flat geometry for known limitations while rejecting unexpected failures.
body:
Unsupported PCB folds and rigid placements in bend zones are expected geometry limitations, but consumers currently have to catch arbitrary exceptions to keep a design renderable. Add explicit shared folding results so renderers can retain flat geometry only for known limitations while unexpected failures still reject.

- Add `PcbFoldIssue`, `PcbFoldError`, and `PcbFoldResult<T>`, with stable issue codes and optional bend IDs. Existing strict APIs preserve their error messages.
- Add `tryCreatePcbFold` and `tryFoldSurfaceMesh`, including legacy full-cross-section validation that occurs during surface deformation.
- Share rigid mesh deformation through `foldRigidMesh`/`tryFoldRigidMesh`. Validate an optional PCB mount separately from model extents, so CAD offsets cannot conceal an invalid mount.
- Reuse rigid mesh deformation for stiffeners and expose `tryFoldStiffenerMesh` for already-created flat meshes, preserving the original outline-average anchor without duplicate extrusion.
- Keep malformed board/polygon/stiffener data, missing CAD references, and unexpected transformation failures as exceptions. CAD pose normalization remains strict.

Supports the explicit fallback implementation in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/230 for https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277. Consumers can choose their rendering/reporting policy; flex-utils does not log or automatically select flat geometry.

Validation: `bun test` passes all 24 tests (1,329 assertions); typecheck and build pass. Tests cover structured diagnostics, unexpected-error propagation, legacy surface failures, separately validated offset CAD mounts, rigid positions/normals/metadata, unchanged input geometry, and stiffener reuse. The new common `toMatchPngSnapshot`/PoppyGL snapshot shows a valid board and blue CAD folded together while the invalid red bend-zone placement stays flat; the image was visually inspected. Existing snapshots remain unchanged.

title: Support finite PCB bend regions from board outlines
description: Adds support for finite PCB bend regions by allowing a board-local outline to define the connected region cut off by bends, improving the handling of flex-board tails during deformation.
body:
Bends on one flex-board tail currently deform every point beyond the bend's infinite line, including neighboring tails. Add an optional board-local outline to `createPcbFold` so a finite boundary-to-boundary chord selects the connected region it cuts off. Include widened distal tips and allow overlapping bend positions on disjoint tails.

CAD points/directions, inverse placement, rigid-mount checks, stiffeners, and surface meshes use the same selected region. `getCadFoldContext` automatically converts the Circuit JSON board outline from world coordinates to board-local coordinates. Existing two-argument calls retain their behavior.

Addresses the folding utility underlying item 1 of https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277. Core adoption is still required: update its flex-utils dependency and pass the emitted board outline minus `board.center` from `Board.doInitialPcbFlexRender`. Viewer/GLTF callers that construct folds directly need the same outline argument.

Scope remains parallel bends sharing a moving direction on simple outlines. Incomplete chords, branching within a bend zone, and moving regions wrapping behind the proximal tangent fail explicitly.

Validation:
- 17 tests pass, including six topology regressions with the issue's outline, independent tails, widened tips, winding/endpoint/order invariance, translated CAD, surface meshes, rigid stiffeners, and inverse placement.
- Typecheck, build, and diff checks pass. The PoppyGL PNG regression fails when infinite-line folding is restored.
- An isolated core adoption patch passes all six flex tests, including the exact two-tail issue fixture at the origin and at `(100, -70)`. The left resistor folds to z ≈ 5.2146 mm and x rotation 90° while the right resistor stays flat; PCB records remain unchanged and CAD round-trips. This consumer patch is not included here because it requires adopting the new dependency release.

Visual snapshots render the locally generated surface mesh with PoppyGL and use the standard `toMatchPngSnapshot` fixture. The camera is identical in both images. Red RL follows the left tail through its 90° bend; blue RR stays on the flat right tail.

| Flat reference | Finite left-tail fold |
| --- | --- |
| ![Flat two-tail board](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/flex-utils/8deadc4a6bba23243050bb1ecbe621ca89733c5e/tests/__snapshots__/finite-bend-flat-reference.snap.png) | ![Only the left tail folds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/flex-utils/8deadc4a6bba23243050bb1ecbe621ca89733c5e/tests/__snapshots__/finite-bend-left-tail-folded.snap.png) |

title: Polygon pads can carry validated solder-paste contours
description: Adds support for polygon SMT pads to carry validated solder paste contours in Circuit JSON, allowing for absolute board-space contours and optional inner openings.
body:
Polygon SMT pads cannot carry solder paste through Circuit JSON because the paste union accepts only centered primitive shapes. Add `PcbSolderPastePolygon` with absolute board-space contours, optional inner openings, and existing pad/component ownership fields. Contours use the shared polygon validation for finite coordinates, at least three vertices and nonzero area.

Validation: 420 tests pass, TypeScript and build pass, Zod lint and snake-case check pass. Regression covers top/bottom contours, inner openings, links and invalid boundaries. Enables the generation and export fixes accompanying tscircuit/core#4335.

title: Normalize source pin voltage attributes to numeric volts
description: Normalizes requires_voltage and provides_voltage attributes to numeric volts, allowing for direct comparison of electrical values without string interpretation.
body:
`requires_voltage` and `provides_voltage` currently preserve strings such as `"3.3V"` in parsed Circuit JSON. Normalize both fields to finite numeric volts, so consumers can compare electrical values without interpreting strings.

Accept numbers, numeric strings, and SI voltage inputs through the existing voltage unit parser. Validate a complete scalar before conversion, rejecting ranges, conditional prose, unrelated units, and non-finite values instead of truncating them into an invented voltage. Keep omitted attributes omitted and preserve caller input. `SourcePinAttributes` and `SourcePort` expose numeric output; `SourcePinAttributesInput` and the existing `SourcePortInput` allow string inputs. Update the documented output types.

Validation: the complete suite passes (421 tests); added coverage for normalization through pin attributes, source ports, and the generic Circuit JSON parser/JSON serialization, including zero, negative, scientific notation, and SI units; type checks assert numeric output. Type checking, Zod lint, snake-case checks, changed-file formatting, and package build pass. No dependency changes.

title: Allow missing manufacturer part number warnings for all source components
description: Allows source components to emit missing manufacturer part number warnings without requiring a connector standard, enhancing flexibility in warning generation.
body:
The missing-manufacturer-part-number warning currently requires a connector `standard`, preventing other parts from emitting a valid warning. Make `standard` optional so core can warn for any source component, while retaining existing connector records.

Validation: all 419 tests pass, TypeScript checking passes, and the package builds. Updated the generated warning documentation. Supports the core missing-MPN warning work and https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/895.

title: Support polygon solder paste in PCB placement transforms
description: Fixes the issue where polygon solder paste remains at its original position during PCB placement, ensuring that paste stays aligned with its pad by applying the existing point transform to copper outlines, paste outlines, and inner openings.
body:
Polygon paste remains at its original position during PCB placement, while polygon pads receive invalid NaN center fields. Apply the existing point transform to copper outlines, paste outlines and inner openings before the centered-shape branch so paste stays aligned with its pad.

Follows the existing solder-mask opening transform pattern in the same file and preserves in-place mutation, layer and ownership links. Removes the redundant polygon-pad branch and its type escapes; the source implementation has 17 added and 19 removed lines. Uses the released circuit-json 0.0.513 polygon-paste schema.

Validation: both new top/bottom regressions fail on unchanged main and pass with the fix. All 145 tests pass after a fresh install, along with type checking, formatting and build. Regression checks translation, rotation, reflection, inverse placement, matching copper/paste bounds, attachment IDs, schema validity and absence of center fields. Coordinates are verified directly; the existing SVG development dependency and snapshots are unchanged.

title: Add copper pour crosshatch pitch and width props
description: Adds optional crosshatchPitch and crosshatchWidth distances to copperpour , keeping crosshatch as the boolean switch.
body:
Adds optional `crosshatchPitch` and `crosshatchWidth` distances to `<copperpour />`, keeping `crosshatch` as the boolean switch. For example, `crosshatch crosshatchPitch="2mm" crosshatchWidth="0.4mm"` requests a coarser mesh.

Numbers are millimetres and unit strings parse to millimetres. Explicit dimensions must be finite and positive; enabled hatching requires width below pitch, including when one dimension uses its default. Omitted dimensions remain undefined for the solver to resolve to the existing 1mm pitch / 0.25mm width. Sizing alone does not enable hatching. No aliases or migration are needed.

Validation: all 600 tests, typecheck, build, format check, and the four required generation scripts passed. Includes generated documentation and distance/default/validation regression coverage.

title: Add crosshatch boolean to copper pours
description: Adds crosshatch boolean option to copper pours, allowing for 45-degree crosshatch fill with specified parameters while preserving solid copper around boundaries and connections.
body:
Adds `crosshatch?: boolean` to `<copperpour>` so authors can opt into crosshatched copper with `<copperpour crosshatch connectsTo="net.GND" layer="bottom" />`.

`true` requests a 45-degree mesh with 0.25 mm copper width and 1 mm pitch, preserving solid copper around boundaries and connections. `false` or omission retains solid fill. The parser accepts only booleans, preserves omission as `undefined`, and adds no aliases or conflicts. Existing circuits require no migration. Geometry generation is in https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/pull/109 and core forwarding is in https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4327; this PR defines the authoring contract.

title: Support mpn on components alongside manufacturerPartNumber and mfn
description: Components now accept mpn alongside manufacturerPartNumber and mfn, including mounted boards. Crystals existing mpn definition is inherited from the common component props.
body:
Components now accept `mpn` alongside `manufacturerPartNumber` and `mfn`, including mounted boards. Crystal's existing `mpn` definition is inherited from the common component props.

`resolveManufacturerPartNumber` provides a canonical, trimmed part number without mutating author props. Matching aliases are accepted, conflicting nonempty aliases throw, and missing or whitespace-only values resolve to `undefined`. Schemas retain the aliases to preserve Zod object composition and existing input compatibility.

title: feat: propose pcbbend tearReliefRadius for rounded tear reliefs
description: Adds an opt-in tearReliefRadius prop to pcbbend  for rounded tear-relief cutouts intended to reduce tearing at flex edges.
body:
Adds an opt-in `tearReliefRadius` prop to `<pcbbend />` for rounded tear-relief cutouts intended to reduce tearing at flex edges.

```tsx
<pcbbend
  x1={0} y1={-5}
  x2={0} y2={5}
  bendAngle={90}
  bendRadius="3mm"
  bendSide="right"
  tearReliefRadius="0.5mm"
/>
```

The proposed geometry is a circular material-removing cutout centered at each bend centerline endpoint, using the same radius at both ends. At straight board edges this produces semicircular relief notches in the flat fabrication outline. The relief radius is independent of the fold radius, angle, and moving side.

- Accepts a finite positive number in millimeters or a unit-aware distance string; parses to millimeters.
- Omitted or `undefined` leaves the outline unchanged. Zero, negative, nonfinite, and invalid values are rejected. No aliases, conflicting props, or migration are introduced.
- Includes the authoring contract, usage example, regenerated documentation, and tests for normalization, omission, invalid inputs, and independence from fold settings.

This PR proposes and validates the props API only. Core geometry, Circuit JSON propagation, rendering, fabrication exports, and board-level checks for relief overlap and clearances need downstream implementation.

Validation: `bun test` (595 pass), `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and all four generation scripts required by `AGENTS.md`.

title: Add assembly.motor and board mounting props
description: Add assembly.motor with motor standard, shaft direction, and board mounting target properties to simplify motor controller assembly without requiring modelcdn URLs or CAD offsets.
body:
Motor controller assemblies need a motor standard, shaft direction, and a board mounting target without authors constructing a modelcdn URL or calculating a CAD offset. Add `assembly.motor` with `standard="nema8" | "nema17" | "nema23"`, plus board `mountedTo` and unit-aware `mountGap` props for this usage:

```tsx
<assembly.device>
  <assembly.motor name="NEMA17" standard="nema17" />
  <Rp2040MotorController mountedTo="NEMA17.backface" mountGap="6mm" />
</assembly.device>
```

The motor requires a stable `name` and exactly one of `standard` or a custom modelprinter string via `model`. `shaftFacingDirection` accepts all six signed axes, including `"x+"` and `"z-"`, defaulting to the native `"z+"` shaft axis. Also support optional `displayName`.

Board mounting targets are trimmed nonblank strings; gaps accept nonnegative finite distances and parse to millimeters. Mounting props are unset by default, preserving existing boards and the board schema's ZodObject API. The docs show how the controller forwards its mounting props to `<board>` and explain the coordinate frame, defaults, conflicts, validation, and migration.

This PR defines props only; core rendering, shaft orientation, and board mounting support are follow-ups.

title: fix: add instance reference labels to imported custom symbols
description: Adds instance reference labels to imported custom symbols for better visibility and clarity in schematic representations.
body:
Imported custom symbols for C105188, C94934, C20917, and C15127 now display each instance's reference (U1/U2, D1/D2, or Q1/Q2). The converter adds a dynamic {NAME} label above the source bounds when there is no visible reference annotation, keeping it clear of the artwork and pins.

EasyEDA's P-marked reference annotations are retained as instance-dependent text instead of a static library prefix. The second field of a T record is a semantic mark (L=label, N=name, P=reference prefix); the separate text-anchor field contains start/middle/end. The parser calls this raw field textMark and preserves the existing normalized alignment output for compatibility. These roles are defined in the official format: https://docs.easyeda.com/en/DocumentFormat/2-EasyEDA-Schematic-File-Format/#annotations.

Existing reference placeholders are reused, hidden source references do not prevent a visible label, and ordinary annotations such as GND remain unchanged.

The core association reproduction https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4340 and its stacked fix https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4341 address the checker incorrectly reporting a visible label outside the symbol body as missing.

body:
Callers currently cannot supply reviewed datasheet pin attributes to EasyEDA conversion. This forces `tsci import` to merge attributes itself and use a separate TSX conversion path, where numeric datasheet keys can be lost.

Add optional caller-supplied `pinAttributes` to Circuit JSON conversion and both raw/parsed TSX entry points, using the existing props schema. Resolve attributes against actual footprint pad identifiers, including BGA balls, and write them onto `source_port` records before using the normal TSX generator. Physical rows take precedence over signal aliases; explicit empty rows, false values, zero quantities and serial capabilities survive. Existing symbol selection, component classification, footprint geometry and CAD handling are preserved.

The caller retains responsibility for fetching and validating datasheet metadata. There are no new runtime dependencies or datasheet API requests. Existing development versions of props, tscircuit and circuit-json-util are updated to support the current schemas; one pushbutton schematic snapshot is refreshed for the current native symbol position.

Validation:

- 12 focused tests / 233 assertions, including all 29 DRV8818 pads, BGA identifiers, repeated pads, alias conflicts, explicit uncertainty and a semantic TypeScript check for capability arrays.
- Normal EasyEDA conversion preserves all 2,729 attribute fields across 47 real stepper-driver imports / 1,167 physical contacts. Strict props and Circuit JSON validation pass; geometry, labels, symbols, classification and CAD metadata match the conversion without supplied attributes.
- TypeScript, Biome and Node/browser/CLI builds with declaration files pass.
- No-option generated TSX is byte-identical to the original generator for all ten component types.
- The full suite completed with 317 passing tests and eight snapshot failures. The pushbutton snapshot was reviewed, refreshed and its test passes. The remaining seven CAD snapshot failures reproduce with the original conversion code on the same development runtime; all 19 compared TSX/Circuit JSON outputs are byte-identical. A renderer OBJ request returning HTTP 403 HTML was observed for C2886621, resulting in an empty CAD mesh. Those seven reference images are intentionally retained.

This provides the upstream API needed to replace the CLI-owned merge and alternate conversion path discussed in tscircuit/cli#5129.

title: Preserve all mechanical-switch terminals and source drill dimensions
description: Preserves all terminals and drill dimensions for multi-terminal mechanical switches in the PCB mapping.
body:
Multi-terminal mechanical switches retain every numbered terminal and its PCB mapping in a chip box. C221539 now exposes pins 1, 2 and 3, and all three holes preserve the source's 0.9139936 × 1.499997 mm slots.

The reproduction in #585 is merged; this fix targets main. The existing [SPDT symbol](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-symbols/blob/main/symbols/spdt_switch_right.ts) assigns common to pin 1, whereas C221539 uses pin 2. Mechanical switches with more than two terminals and DIP switches therefore use numbered chip boxes without a custom symbol or inferred contact roles. Two-terminal switches retain their built-in symbol. Regressions also cover C2941005's six terminals, C136720's five terminals and C4681's eighteen terminals.

Drill dimensions follow the explicit EasyEDA length and centerline endpoints rather than the copper aspect ratio. Round drills remain round inside elongated copper. Tests cover rectangular and oval pads at cardinal and arbitrary rotations. Slots misaligned with the pad's local axes fail explicitly rather than receiving guessed geometry.

Validation after integrating main: 313 tests and 77 snapshots pass; TypeScript, formatting and build pass. GitHub CI runs against the final fix head.

The [EasyEDA PAD format](https://docs.easyeda.com/en/DocumentFormat/3-EasyEDA-PCB-File-Format/index.html#pad) defines the drill fields. The [manufacturer drawing](https://www.ckswitches.com/media/1429/1000.pdf) recommends a different PCB drill; source preservation does not establish fabrication suitability.

body:

title: Remove the fanout-solver dependency patch
description: Removes the fanout-solver dependency patch and reverts to strict TypeScript checking, ensuring the viewer operates without routing or rendering behavior changes.
body:
The viewer carries a type-only Bun patch for an empty array in fanout-solver. Its `noImplicitAny: false` override, combined with strict null checks, makes TypeScript infer that array as `never[]` when it follows core's declarations into the solver's exported source.

Remove the override and inherit strict mode's implicit-any checking. Add the types this exposes in the hole/via helpers, `@types/debug`, and the Troika Text API used by the viewer. Delete the solver patch and its patchedDependencies entry. No routing or rendering behavior changes, and the viewer works with the existing unmodified npm release.

Also proposed the explicit array annotation upstream in https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/pull/253, with a consumer compiler configuration check. This PR can land independently.

Validation: unpatched clean install, TypeScript check, format check, package build, Node bundle smoke test, and the five flex/mechanical CI tests pass. Full local suite: 153 pass, six failures; a clean main checkout with identical dependencies produces the same six failures. No snapshots were rebaselined.

body:
Use @tscircuit/modelprinter 0.0.4 from npm for parsing and schemas, and import the sheet-metal and bolt mesh generators from jscad-electronics. Update jscad-electronics to 0.0.182, enabling NEMA8/17/23 in the viewer as well.

title: Add named reference planes and geometry-only plan extraction
description: Adds named reference planes to survive JSCAD JSON round trips without becoming printable geometry, including metadata and a resolver for geometry-only plans.
body:
Named attachment planes need to survive a JSCAD JSON round trip without becoming printable geometry. This adds `name`/`reference` metadata to operation nodes and `resolveReferencePlanes(plan)`, which returns a geometry-only plan plus each reference's origin, outward normal, and in-plane X axis.

Reference rectangles use ordinary transform operations. The resolver also accepts the rectangular polygons emitted by jscad-fiber, composes nested affine transforms, and rejects duplicate names, singular/projective transforms, and ambiguous extrusion or subtraction-base references. `executeJscadOperations` strips references before evaluation. No changes to the JSCAD modeling kernel are required.

This is the foundation for mounting a printed spacer between a motor and board; assembly integration follows separately.

Validation: all 23 tests, TypeScript, and package build pass. Geometry tests cover a 4 mm plate with four M3 clearance holes, a 30 mm center opening, unchanged solids after reference removal, and transformed attachment frames. The existing CI now also runs tests and builds the package.

title: Support polygon solder paste on SMT pads
description: Adds support for generating solder paste on polygon SMT pads, ensuring proper paste emission for ground-pad polygons and maintaining existing copper and schematic integrity.
body:
Polygon SMT pads currently emit no solder paste. The ICS-43434 import therefore has paste on its five rectangular pads but none on the four ground-pad polygons. This PR emits nine apertures while preserving the imported copper and schematic.

Polygon paste follows the existing default 0.7 scale, explicit margin, layer, and solder-mask coverage rules. Clipper handles concave clipping and edge offsets, including split or fully eroded apertures. The existing PCB transform utility moves paste with copper; footprint inflation preserves supplied contours, inner openings, and intentionally absent paste.

Uses published circuit-json 0.0.513, circuit-json-util 0.0.119, and circuit-to-svg 0.0.440. Two existing through-hole assertions are narrowed to their intended paste shape for the new schema union.

All 18 GitHub checks pass, including all ten full-suite test shards, type checking, formatting, dependency checks, package preview, and distribution smoke tests. title: Enable voltage compatibility DRC and emit numeric pin voltages
description: Enables voltage compatibility checks for the F1C100S AVCC pin, ensuring correct voltage connections and updating related dependencies and tests.
body:

The currently released renderer supports the message overlay only.

title: Preserve supplier imports for strict legacy parts engines
description: Preserves supplier part numbers and fetch function when strict legacy parts engines reject the datasheet option, ensuring successful fallbacks and proper error handling.
body:
Strict custom parts engines can reject `includeDatasheetInformation` as an unknown request field. Core previously retried with the field set to `false`, so both attempts failed and an otherwise available supplier footprint could not load.

When both flagged requests throw, retry with the original request shape, preserving the supplier/manufacturer part numbers and platform fetch function. Keep the explicit `false` attempt for modern engines that enable enrichment by default. All successful fallbacks pass through the existing manufacturer identity check, and the legacy fallback emits one readable warning that pin attributes may not be populated. Genuine supplier failures still propagate.

Validation: reproduced the regression before the fix; added a PCB snapshot test using a strict legacy request schema, plus tests for rejecting a wrong-voltage regulator and propagating a supplier failure. Related parts-engine, import, pin-attribute, and decoupling tests pass, along with type checking, formatting, package build, and distribution smoke tests. No dependency changes.

title: Preserve datasheet pin attributes from parts-engine imports
description: Preserves electrical attributes from imported parts when converting Circuit JSON to footprint primitives, ensuring that essential specifications like voltage requirements are retained during the rendering process.
body:
Core drops electrical attributes when imported part Circuit JSON is converted into footprint primitives. For example, a source port enriched by parts-engine 0.0.36 with a 2.8V supply requirement loses that requirement when core renders its own ports.

Request `includeDatasheetInformation: true` on supplier-footprint and standard-connector imports, carrying the requested manufacturer identity for variant validation, and preserve the returned canonical SourcePinAttributes as derived component state. Match physical contacts first, then unique aliases/BGA hints; leave ambiguous or multi-component imports unapplied. Refresh existing source ports when async imports arrive, retaining IDs, labels and geometry. Apply explicit user pinAttributes last, including false/zero and explicitly empty capability selections, without changing user props or the imported array. Power/ground connection checks use the same resolved attributes. If enrichment fails, retry without it and emit one pinAttributes warning when the footprint is still available. The fallback never accepts a different known manufacturer identity/voltage variant.

Core receives an injected PartsEngine and has no direct parts-engine dependency to bump. This integrates the published 0.0.36 behavior without adding dependencies or changing the shared props interface. Older/custom engines can ignore the optional request flag. Aggregate missing-attribute warnings and voltage-compatibility DRC remain follow-ups.

Validation:
- 42 related tests pass, including new async-import/user-override/power-ground and BGA/ambiguity regressions, standard connector attribute preservation, timeout/failure fallback and wrong-voltage rejection, existing footprint and schematic snapshots, disabled-engine paths and decoupling behavior.
- Type checking, formatting and package/declaration build pass.
- Read-only end-to-end verification with the published parts-engine 0.0.36 and live supplier/API responses: all 140 contacts across the F1C board's nine ICs preserve the engine's canonical attributes exactly. Existing unspecified attributes stay unspecified.

title: feat: add rounded tear relief cutouts to pcbbend
description: Adds rounded tear relief cutouts to the pcbbend component, allowing for circular cutouts at bend endpoints when a tearReliefRadius prop is specified, enhancing the PCB design capabilities without altering existing behavior when the prop is omitted.
body:
Implements the merged [`tearReliefRadius` API](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/896). `<pcbbend tearReliefRadius="0.5mm" ... />` now emits a circular cutout at each bend endpoint, producing rounded edge notches in flat and folded boards. Omitting the prop preserves the existing behavior.

The cutouts are emitted during `PcbFlexRender`, after board sizing and panel placement and before routing. They use the existing `pcb_cutout` representation, so routing obstacles, 3D material subtraction, and Gerber outline clipping work without new Circuit JSON fields or renderer changes. Their centers are converted from board-relative bend coordinates to circuit-world coordinates, with explicit board/group/subcircuit ownership.

Also corrects the bend removal hook to `removePcbFlexRender`, which the render lifecycle actually dispatches, and cleans up its generated cutouts in that phase.

body:
Placed parts emit `source_missing_manufacturer_part_number_warning` only when they have neither a manufacturer part number nor a non-empty supplier part number after parts-engine resolution finishes. For example, a resistor whose engine lookup returns `{ jlcpcb: ["C123"] }` does not need an explicit MPN; an empty or failed lookup leaves the part unresolved and produces a warning. Explicit supplier part numbers also satisfy the check. Resistors, capacitors, and inductors follow the same resolution rule as other components, and `doNotPlace` remains exempt.

The new warning phase runs after `PartsEngineRender` and waits for its asynchronous effects plus footprint fetches. The parts-engine `findPart` API returns supplier IDs, so the check uses those matches without inventing or copying an MPN. It respects DRC disabling, emits one warning per source component with connector `standard` metadata, and removes stale warnings when a later update resolves a part.

All part renderers resolve `mpn`, `mfn`, and `manufacturerPartNumber` consistently into `manufacturer_part_number`. This also fixes previously ignored `mfn` aliases on chips, pinouts, jumpers, and solder jumpers, and uses the resolved number for schematic labels and connector parts-engine lookups.

Props prerequisite https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/895 is merged and released in `@tscircuit/props@0.0.680`. Core follows current main's `^0.0.681` dev dependency and override, which include the alias API. Peer dependencies retain `*` as required by the repository's internal-package policy. Validation uses the published props package.

The warning-schema prerequisite https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/856 is also merged and released in `circuit-json@0.0.511`. Core uses that minimum in its dev dependency and override. Validation uses the published packages, with no local prerequisite builds.

Validation: all CI checks pass on the latest commit, including all ten test shards, type checking, dependency policy, formatting, package preview, and distribution smoke tests. All 18 focused MPN/parts-engine tests also pass locally. The local component/base-component/root-circuit run with Bun 1.3.2 had 451 passing tests, 3 skips, and one pre-existing numeric snapshot formatting difference in `pin-header-pcbOrientation.test.tsx`; CI's Bun version passes it. Coverage checks aliases across 23 part types, pending lookups, successful automatic passive selection, empty/failed lookups, cache hits, disabled engines, standard connector selection, explicit/empty/blank supplier IDs, stale-warning removal, ownership/deduplication, DRC disabling, and `doNotPlace` exemptions.

EasyEDA imports already emit `manufacturerPartNumber`, which satisfies this check. Additional fallback/skip-path regression coverage: https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5122. No generator changes are required.

body:
Enables `<copperpour crosshatch connectsTo="net.GND" layer="top" />` by forwarding the boolean to the copper-pour solver. The solver emits the mesh as ordinary BRep holes, so consumers receive the physical copper geometry. Omission or `crosshatch={false}` retains solid fill.

The integration fixture renders a crosshatched top pour with thermal reliefs and a solid bottom pour. It checks the effective solver input, emitted holes, clipped boundary cells behind the 0.25 mm copper rim, and unchanged solid output. Its labeled PCB snapshot shows the partial edge openings.

Updates `@tscircuit/props` (including its override) to `^0.0.681` and `@tscircuit/copper-pour-solver` to `^0.0.66`, the published releases containing the merged companion changes:

- Props API: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/897
- Solver geometry: https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/pull/109

body:
Core now implements the motor and board-mount props added in tscircuit/props#893. Authors can assemble a controller and a NEMA motor without creating a model URL or manually calculating CAD offsets:

```tsx
<assembly.device>
  <assembly.motor name="NEMA17" standard="nema17" />
  <Rp2040MotorController
    mountedTo="NEMA17.backface"
    mountGap="6mm"
  />
</assembly.device>
```

The controller must forward these props to its `<board>`. `standard` supports NEMA8/17/23; `model` accepts a custom NEMA modelprinter string instead. The optional `shaftFacingDirection` defaults to `z+` and supports all six signed axes. Core parses modelprinter specs and resolves modelcdn GLBs; mesh generation remains in jscad-electronics.

Backface mounting uses the actual model body length and finalized PCB thickness to measure the requested gap from the nearest board surface. Boards keep their existing PCB coordinates; the motor follows the board center and in-plane rotation. Mount references resolve in the nearest assembly device, including forward references, with errors for missing/ambiguous targets and conflicting placements.

Board mounting currently supports `z+` and `z-`. Sideways motors render, but sideways board mounts report a clear error until Circuit JSON and the renderers support rotated PCB boards.

Validation: 32 assembly/namespace/container tests pass, including ten new motor tests with annotated PNG snapshots pairing TSX on the left with the render on the right. Shaft orientations, NEMA standards and backface mounting directions each have one combined comparison image per test file; the PCB-disabled case explicitly shows only R1 in the schematic. Geometry assertions measure exported GLB bounds for all standards, all six directions, custom dimensions, and the 6 mm surface gap. All ten CI test shards, typecheck, package build/preview, dist smoke tests and dependency checks pass.

The RP2040 controller placement build also succeeds with the new API: a 1.6 mm PCB and 6 mm rear clearance produce the NEMA17 origin at Z = -44.8 mm. All 1,901 emitted PCB records match an unmounted build under the same core. This integration check disables routing: the project's saved route plan from an older core rejects the current routing input and needs a separate migration. The unmodified controller build without an assembly also rejects the route plan under current core.

title: Preserve PCB connections for separated polygon contacts
description: Fixes autorouting failure by ensuring that separated polygon contacts for ground connections are correctly recognized and connected in the PCB layout.
body:
C5656610 / ICS-43434's four pin-3 ground polygons produce four internally connected PCB contacts, and default autorouting creates the GND connection without ambiguity or a missing-contact failure.

Before rendering, polygon bounds were centered on the pad origin, which need not be the center of its vertices. The separated shapes were grouped as overlapping, then rejected once their actual geometry rendered. SmtPad returns bounds from vertices transformed into board coordinates through the shared primitive bounds method. The port overlap helper delegates to that method, keeping shape geometry in the primitive that owns it.

Follows merged reproduction #4322. Both use the same plain board and ordinary trace with default autorouting. Removing the bounds fix makes the regression fail with the original missing-contact autorouting error. With the fix, it confirms four physical ground contacts, their internal connection, an active routing solver and a PCB trace associated with the source trace. There are no ambiguous-port, trace or missing-trace errors.

The PCB SVG shows the autorouted ground connection; the schematic SVG is unchanged. Translation, 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° rotation on both layers remain covered, with bounds checked against emitted geometry. The imported component, acoustic hole, copper geometry and pin mapping are unchanged.

Validation after alignment with current main: eight focused tests (206 assertions), TypeScript, formatting, package build and distribution smoke tests pass. The fix diff is byte-for-byte identical to the approved patch. All 18 CI checks pass on the latest commit, including all ten full-suite test shards. There are no unresolved review threads. The previous head passed all ten full-suite CI shards; local full-suite success is not claimed. The separate supplier acoustic-hole discrepancy remains unresolved.

title: Reproduce the missing ICS-43434 PCB ground connection
description: Reproduces the missing PCB ground connection for the ICS-43434 component, highlighting the failure in autorouting due to the absence of ground PCB contacts.
body:
C5656610 / ICS-43434 has four imported polygon copper shapes for pin 3 (GND). Connecting GND creates a source trace, but core emits source_ambiguous_port_reference and creates no ground PCB contact. With normal local autorouting enabled, route conversion fails while reading the missing contact and produces no PCB trace.

The reproduction uses a plain board and an ordinary trace with default autorouting, with neither routingDisabled nor pcbStraightLine. It preserves the official EasyEDA import and captures PCB and schematic SVG snapshots. Its assertions record the failure: four ground shapes, one logical port, zero ground PCB contacts and zero PCB traces. The PCB and schematic snapshots are unchanged because the failing circuit still produces no route.

Stacked fix: #4323 uses the same circuit and routing settings, then requires four internally connected ground contacts and a successful autorouted trace. The separate supplier 0.40 mm acoustic-opening discrepancy remains unchanged.

Validation: the reproduction records the failure and passes its expected-bug assertions; TypeScript and formatting pass locally. All 18 CI checks pass on the latest commit, including all ten full-suite test shards. There are no unresolved review threads.

title: Add TSX solder-mask openings for flex coverlay windows
description: Adds TSX solder-mask openings for flex coverlay windows to accommodate flex contact rows with a continuous coverlay window across multiple fingers.
body:
Flex contact rows need one coverlay window across multiple fingers, extending past their ends. Add `<pcbsoldermaskopening>` for a rectangle, circle, or polygon on the top/bottom face. It emits canonical `pcb_soldermask_opening` geometry independently of pads. Addresses item 5 of [tscircuit #5277](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277).

```tsx
<pcbsoldermaskopening
  name="CONTACT_WINDOW"
  shape="rect"
  layer="top"
  pcbX={0}
  pcbY={12}
  width={10}
  height={4}
/>
```

Placement, group rotation/translation, footprint side flips, and subsequent layout movement follow the pad transform. Rotated rectangles serialize as `rotated_rect`; polygon vertices include world placement. Cached subcircuits retain standalone and component-owned openings. Component inflation uses the canonical transform utility.

All coverlay dependencies are now merged, published, and adopted: props `^0.0.677`, Circuit JSON `^0.0.510`, utility `^0.0.118`, and SVG `^0.0.438`. The last SVG preview pin is removed. Core's existing independent/nested folds, error overlays, and polyimide rendering remain in place with flex-utils `0.0.8`, GLTF `^0.0.141`, and PoppyGL `0.0.29`.

Validation:

- Installed the actual published SVG `0.0.438` and utility `0.0.118` with scripts disabled.
- All four opening tests and 12 PCB-flex regressions pass (16 tests, 597 assertions). Geometry checks compare emitted openings to emitted pad markers through translation, group rotation, and footprint rotations on both faces.
- Six labeled opening snapshots cover the contact window, transformed geometry, and cache paths. All 1,250 snapshot-file hashes are unchanged after release adoption.
- TypeScript, distribution build, full formatting, and diff checks pass. No README changes.

title: Update Footprinter for BGA pin numbering

body:
Rendering an imported column-major BGA footprint requires Footprinter's new `pinnumbering(...)` conventions. An older Footprinter accepts the string without implementing that parameter, assigning the wrong numeric IDs; a live 624-ball i.MX6 render produced 625 source ports.

Update the existing development dependency to Footprinter 0.0.430 while preserving the repository’s wildcard peer-dependency policy. Through-hole pill pads now emit schema-valid paste that follows the pad's final rotation on both outer layers. The paste radius matches the smaller copper-pad dimension, so a 90° slot gets horizontal paste aligned with its copper pad.

body:
Through-hole pill pads emit solder paste without the radius required by circuit-json. A pad rotated 90° still gets unrotated paste on both outer layers, so the paste overlaps the wrong area.

This reproduction captures the existing PCB output and asserts schema validity, radius and rotation as an expected failure. Circular THT and SMD pads remain covered. The fix is stacked in #4316.

title: Render NEMA rear-face holes and socket-head screws
description: Adds rendering of rear socket-head screws and blind bores for NEMA8, NEMA17, and NEMA23 motors, with configurable parameters for pitch, diameter, and screw size.
body:
NEMA8, NEMA17 and NEMA23 now render four rear socket-head screws by default. Modelprinter's `_backfaceholes` exposes four blind bores, `_backfacescrews` installs the screws, and `_plainbackface` preserves the plain rear cap. React/vanilla props use `backFace`.

Rear pitch, bore diameter/depth and metric screw size are configurable. Heads face outward from Z=-bodyLength; smooth shanks occupy the bores, which retain solid floors. The rear cap supports NEMA23's corner fasteners. Front mounting holes and shaft geometry stay unchanged. Screw heads and hex recesses reuse the existing HexSocketBolt JSCAD generator; all mesh generation remains in this repository.

Uses the published modelprinter 0.0.5 schema from https://github.com/tscircuit/modelprinter/pull/9, with the registry dependency and lockfile updated together.

Validation from a clean frozen-lockfile install of the published dependency: build, typecheck, format check, and all 299 tests pass. New geometry tests probe every rear hole's opening and floor, screw shank/head/socket seating, custom rear pitch, and unchanged front mounting holes in both React and built vanilla paths. Rear comparison snapshots and all three default motor snapshots were visually reviewed.

title: Add headless JSX plans and named reference rectangles
description: Adds a new headless JSX component namespace and functionality for compiling synchronous JSX components into serializable operation JSON, including support for named reference rectangles.
body:
Printed parts need to author named mounting references beside their solid geometry. This adds `jscad-fiber/headless`, a lowercase `jscad` component namespace, and `renderToJscadPlan` for compiling synchronous JSX components into serializable operation JSON without the viewer, Three.js, or modeling kernel.

```tsx
<jscad.translate offset={[0, 0, height]}>
  <jscad.rectangle name="board" size={[42, 42]} reference />
</jscad.translate>
```

Reference rectangles are invisible in native rendering and retain their names and reference metadata in headless plans. They lower to ordinary polygon operations, so no JSCAD kernel extension is needed. Nested fragments and operation arrays are handled consistently; subtract, hull, extrusion, and color/transform plans now receive individual operation nodes.

The motor spacer example contains a 4 mm plate, four hollow posts on 31 mm centers, 3.2 mm M3 clearance holes, a 30 mm center opening, and named `motor`/`board` planes. The headless compiler supports pure synchronous components; hooks, async components, and raw Custom geometry are explicitly unsupported.

Use the reference extractor in https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-planner/pull/18 before passing reference-bearing plans to existing geometry consumers. This PR builds independently against published jscad-planner 0.0.14. `assembly.printedpart` integration follows separately.

Validation: all 15 tests (4 snapshots), TypeScript, formatting, frozen-lockfile install, and package build pass. Tests compare native and planned spacer geometry, probe all clearance openings, check JSON metadata and parameter changes, and verify the headless bundle excludes viewer/kernel imports. A local cross-package check with planner PR #18 also verifies both attachment frames at 10 mm and 18 mm spacer heights.

title: Render source port errors at schematic pins with shouldDrawErrors
description: Render source port errors at schematic pins with shouldDrawErrors, allowing for local message callouts and highlighting of referenced pins for various error types.
body:
`shouldDrawErrors` currently highlights only pins referenced by `source_component_misconfigured_error`, and its message needs the separate `showErrorsInTextOverlay` option. Single-pin DRC errors are not rendered at their schematic pins.

Resolve source error references to the visible schematic ports and draw a local message callout with a leader to the affected pin. Highlight every referenced pin but show one message per error. Support component configuration, must-be-connected, I2C configuration, and trace connection errors through their existing Circuit JSON fields. `shouldDrawErrors: true` alone shows the diagnostic; the global text overlay stays independent.

Reuse the existing schematic warning callout layout for wrapping, viewport limits, and callout spacing. Source error placement also accounts for component and label bounds so the F1C callout preserves its reference designator. References missing from the current sheet produce no guessed markers.

Update the F1C voltage regression to use only `shouldDrawErrors`, and cover single-port errors, the I2C and trace reference fields, missing/repeated references, sheet selection, and disabling local diagnostics.

Validation: all 430 tests pass (one existing TODO), TypeScript checking and package build pass. Existing warning snapshots are unchanged. Rendered and visually inspected the voltage and single-pin error snapshots. No dependency changes.

Follow-up to #805.

title: Support polygon solder paste in PCB and stencil previews
description: Adds support for rendering polygon solder paste elements in PCB and stencil previews, preventing crashes by implementing a polygon branch in the renderer and updating bounds calculations accordingly.
body:
Polygon solder-paste elements currently crash PCB and stencil previews because the renderer has no polygon branch. Render the supplied outline and openings with the existing `ringToPathD` helper and even-odd fill, and include polygon extents in the existing bounds calculations so previews work without a board.

The implementation adds 33 lines across three source files. It follows the existing copper-pour contour rendering, layer filtering, paste colors and bounds helpers. Uses the released `circuit-json` 0.0.513 polygon-paste schema.

Validation: the new regression fails on unchanged main; all 431 tests pass with the fix (one existing todo). Type checking, formatting and build pass. Tests cover top/bottom PCB and stencil previews, concavity, an inner opening, hidden/opposite-layer paste, and transformed polygons without openings. Four SVG snapshots are included and rendered for visual inspection.

title: Highlight pins referenced by source configuration errors in schematic SVGs
description: Adds support for highlighting pins referenced by source_component_misconfigured_error in schematic SVGs, including error messages as tooltips and labels.
body:
Source voltage DRCs currently appear only as text when `showErrorsInTextOverlay` is enabled; the schematic does not mark the pins identified by `source_component_misconfigured_error`.

Add schematic `shouldDrawErrors` support that draws red rings at the referenced ports, with the error message as a tooltip and accessible label. Use `showErrorsInTextOverlay: true` alongside it to display the message in the SVG. References resolve only against ports on the selected schematic sheet; missing references are skipped and repeated references do not produce duplicate markers.

Includes Circuit JSON emitted by core's F1C100S regression: the regulator provides 1.8 V while AVCC requires 2.8 V. Its snapshot displays the actual DRC message and highlights AVCC and VOUT. Also covers disabling highlights, missing/repeated references, and selected-sheet filtering. No dependency changes.

Validation: 428 tests passed (one existing TODO), TypeScript check and package build passed. Rendered and visually inspected the F1C snapshot.

Core integration: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4334 enables the error text overlay now. Its snapshot will receive pin highlights when this renderer change is released and core's existing circuit-to-svg dependency is updated.

title: Render explicit solder-mask openings over existing copper
description: Render explicit solder-mask openings on the selected face when showSolderMask is enabled, exposing substrate and clipping underlying copper, including covered traces and pours.
body:
Explicit `pcb_soldermask_opening` records currently disappear from PCB previews. Render circles, rectangles, rotated rectangles, and polygons on the selected face when `showSolderMask` is enabled. Each opening exposes substrate and clips the actual underlying copper into the aperture, including covered traces and pours, so a continuous coverlay window displays the existing gold-finger row.

Hidden openings and openings on the opposite face do not expand the viewport. Copper-pour mask and materialized-via lookups are shared within the render, including the exposed-copper pass. Default rendering remains unchanged.

This adapts [Anil Kumar's implementation in #765](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/765) onto current main, preserving its pixel assertions and three SVG snapshots. Addresses the preview portion of [tscircuit #5277](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277), item 5.

Uses published `circuit-json@^0.0.510` from merged [schema #854](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/854), replacing the schema preview in the development dependency and lockfile. The schema dependency gate is resolved.

The branch includes merged [SVG #803](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/803), including its required internal runtime peers and Node.js 24 configuration. The refreshed built preview is `github:tscircuit/circuit-to-svg#7f9f394b3643020eb223171b1ed16140acb0a803` for downstream validation.

Validation:
- Full suite: 424 tests pass, one existing TODO, zero failures across 279 files; three snapshots and 1,286 assertions.
- Four focused opening test files cover both faces, actual exposed copper, substrate, covered copper, disabled rendering, hidden viewport bounds, circles, and rotated geometry. All three coverlay snapshots contain actual Circuit JSON silkscreen explanations and were rendered and visually inspected. Top/bottom callouts identify the exposed trace, exposed pour, masked copper, and bare substrate; the shape snapshot identifies dimensions and rotation. The bottom snapshot is presented from underneath so its silkscreen is readable. Existing copper/substrate pixel assertions still pass.
- Fourteen focused tests, including existing mask rendering and merged bend-line regressions, pass with 109 assertions.
- TypeScript, build, formatting, and diff checks pass. Cosmos export succeeds using Node.js 24.
- A clean production-only npm install with scripts disabled succeeds without companion packages; the built preview imports and renders both coverlay faces using Node.js 24, with identical disabled-rendering output.
- All CI passes on the refreshed source, including tests, typecheck, formatting, dependency policy, bundle/install size, and the Vercel preview.

Release validation: installed npm `circuit-json@0.0.510`; all 424 tests pass (one existing TODO, 1,286 assertions), plus types, build, formatting, and frozen-lockfile installation. The three coverlay snapshots now include explanatory silkscreen; unrelated snapshots are unchanged. All seven CI checks pass on the silkscreen update (`adc914c`), including tests, types, formatting, dependency policy, bundle/install size, and Vercel. No README changes.

title: Detect incompatible voltages on connected source pins
description: Adds a check for incompatible voltage levels on source pins, ensuring that connected components meet their voltage requirements and reporting errors for mismatches.
body:
The F1C100S AVCC pin requires 2.8 V, but connecting it to a regulator that provides 1.8 V currently passes netlist checks even when both pins have voltage attributes.

Add and export `checkSourcePinVoltageCompatibility`, and run it through `runAllNetlistChecks` and `runAllChecks`. It compares explicit scalar `requires_voltage` and `provides_voltage` values across source traces, net IDs, and both forms of internal pin connections. Each incompatible supply/consumer pair emits a fatal `source_component_misconfigured_error` with both component and pin references and readable names. A compatible supply on the same net does not hide an incompatible one.

Reuse Circuit JSON's existing component-configuration error: it already represents conflicting component configurations and identifies all affected components and pins. No Circuit JSON schema change or dependency update is needed. The checks release workflow already triggers the core dependency update.

Only documented scalar voltages are compared. Missing attributes, non-finite values, and legacy ranges/prose are skipped. Numeric/SI-unit values, zero, and negative voltages work; only numerical roundoff is tolerated. The check does not infer a connection through arbitrary component terminals or invent operating ranges from nominal voltages.

Validation:
- All **606 tests pass**, including six new regression tests covering the F1C100S 1.8 V failure/2.8 V success, source-net and internal connections, separate same-named nets, scalar units, missing attributes, multiple supplies, and named/unnamed diagnostics.
- Checked the saved F1C board's actual net connections after applying the documented voltage to its regulator output: 2.8 V passes; changing only that output to 1.8 V reports `U1.AVCC requires 2.8 V ... U_2V8.OUT provides 1.8 V`.
- Type checking, repository formatting, package build, and Node imports of the built check and netlist runner pass.

title: Never expose Circuit JSON IDs in check messages
description: User-facing diagnostics currently expose Circuit JSON IDs directly or through readable-name helpers that fall back to IDs. Use readable elementcomponentpinnet names throughout the checks, with honest labels such as unnamed via and unnamed bend when names are unavailable. Diagnostic IDs and object-reference fields remain unchanged.
body:
User-facing diagnostics currently expose Circuit JSON IDs directly or through readable-name helpers that fall back to IDs. Use readable element/component/pin/net names throughout the checks, with honest labels such as `unnamed via` and `unnamed bend` when names are unavailable. Diagnostic IDs and object-reference fields remain unchanged.

This covers bend zones, clearance and copper-edge rules, pours, keepouts/cutouts, courtyard overlap, via boundaries, connectivity, and schematic diagnostics. Trace names use authored display names or connected port names; pads resolve their owning component/pin names. A shared helper prevents missing names and embedded utility ID fallbacks from leaking into messages. Add the explicit **NEVER use IDs in user-facing messages** rule to `AGENTS.md`; no README changes.

Validation:

- Full suite: 600 tests pass. Dedicated named/unnamed regressions exercise the public placement/routing runners, preserve diagnostic references, and reject raw IDs and arbitrary ID fallbacks.
- Types, build, full formatting, and diff checks pass; the full suite makes 6,081 assertions.
- Updated message expectations and 55 SVG snapshots. All path, line, circle, ellipse, polygon, and polyline primitives are identical before/after in all 55 snapshots. The changes are diagnostic wording; offending copper and geometry are unchanged.
- A populated PCB error snapshot was rendered and visually inspected to verify component/pin names remain visible.

Follows merged #370 and addresses diagnostic clarity in [tscircuit #5277](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277).

title: Add DRC checks for finite PCB bend zones
description: Add DRC checks for placement of vias, pads, stiffeners, and trace corners within finite PCB bend zones to ensure compliance with design rules.
body:
Vias, pads, stiffeners and trace corners can currently occupy a flex PCB bend zone without a DRC diagnostic. Add `checkPcbBendZonePlacement` and `checkPcbBendZoneTraces` to the placement/routing runners and public exports so `runAllChecks` reports these violations.

The checks use finite, centered bend rectangles with width `radius * abs(angle in radians)`, translate board-local bend/stiffener coordinates, and reuse the existing copper/polygon geometry helpers. They check SMT and plated pads, route-only or materialized vias, rectangular/rotated/polygon stiffeners, and non-perpendicular trace copper or corners. Straight perpendicular crossings remain valid. Trace routes include copper entering or leaving a through-pad on its matching face, and materialized vias suppress duplicate route-via diagnostics. Board ownership follows explicit component board links and nested subcircuit ancestry. Tapered trace overlap uses the maximum outgoing width conservatively.

Addresses the bend-zone checks portion of https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277 (item 3).

Validation:
- `bun test`: 599 passed across 195 files, 0 failed; 17 snapshots and 6,039 assertions.
- 13 focused bend-zone regression files cover the issue reproduction, finite ends/copper extents, translated/diagonal bends, rotated and polygon geometry, nested/foreign board ownership, perpendicular crossings, corners/reversals, layer changes, through-pad segments, route-only via deduplication, tapers, and inactive zones.
- `bun run build`, `bunx --no-install tsc --noEmit --pretty false`, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Combined integration with the accompanying core/rendering and Gerber changes rendered the exact item 3 TSX plus a resistor without an exception, detected five bend-zone violations (two SMT pads, via, stiffener and trace), and completed Gerber generation.


Two labeled visual regressions compare the same finite bend before and after correction. These use the repository's actual PCB renderer and Circuit JSON silkscreen annotations; the counts come from the actual placement/trace checks and are asserted by the tests. No README changes.

- **Failing:** the via, pad, and bottom backing overlap the bend zone (three placement errors); the signal trace turns inside the zone (one trace error).
- **Passing:** those parts move outside the zone and the signal crosses straight, perpendicular to the bend (zero errors).
- A via beyond the finite bend end passes in both layouts. The dashed outline is the 1.57 mm × 12 mm bend zone for a 1 mm radius and 90° fold. The solid yellow rectangle annotates the bottom stiffener footprint in this top view; it is not copper.
- These tests exercise bend-zone rules specifically. General pad/trace connectivity and unrelated DRC rules are separate.

![Failing bend-zone layout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/checks/784ea0089f2e03943ec9fd2362214d1f081b54e4/tests/lib/__snapshots__/check-pcb-bend-zones-failing-visual.snap.svg)

![Passing bend-zone layout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/checks/784ea0089f2e03943ec9fd2362214d1f081b54e4/tests/lib/__snapshots__/check-pcb-bend-zones-passing-visual.snap.svg)

Both snapshots were rendered to PNG and visually inspected. All 13 focused bend tests pass (43 assertions), the full suite passes, and types/build/full formatting pass. CI is running for this visual update.

title: Export explicit solder-mask and coverlay opening regions
description: Exports explicit solder-mask and coverlay opening regions to Gerber output, allowing for precise control over mask pad openings and ensuring accurate representation of coverlay windows.
body:
Explicit coverlay windows are currently dropped from Gerber output, so an FPC contact row can only open the mask pad by pad. Export canonical `pcb_soldermask_opening` records to `F_Mask.gbr` or `B_Mask.gbr`: circles use exact circular flashes, while rectangles, rotated rectangles, and polygons use closed filled regions. Coordinates stay in the world PCB frame, with rotation applied before the optional Gerber Y reflection.

The existing negative mask-file polarity makes these shapes openings. They add no copper, paste, silkscreen, board outline, or drill geometry. Gold-finger snapshots show one continuous window across eight contacts and beyond their ends; numeric checks cover translated boards, both faces, every shape, reflected rotations, polygon closure, and unchanged output files on other layers.

The branch now includes current main and merged [Gerber #186](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/pull/186), retaining its separate stiffener layers, translated-board overlay helper, tests, and `0.0.110` package metadata. The development dependency now uses published `circuit-json@^0.0.510` for coverlay openings. Independent review found no interaction between the mask-only coverlay apertures and the separate mechanical stiffener layers.

Uses published `circuit-json@^0.0.510` from merged [schema #854](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/854); the schema preview is removed and its dependency gate is resolved. Public peers are unchanged. The TSX declaration is implemented in merged [Props #892](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/892) and [Core #4291](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4291). The end-to-end audit renders core TSX contact windows on both faces and verifies closed Gerber regions, original copper pads, no added paste, optional Y reflection, and unchanged other files.

Validation:

- Focused coverlay and stiffener regressions: 15 tests pass across 12 files with 255 assertions. Coverage includes translated geometry, both faces, rotated/reflected openings, stiffener grouping and ownership, polygon closure, and unchanged electrical layers.
- Full suite on Bun `1.3.1`, matching test CI: 186 tests pass across 92 files with 1,881 assertions and zero failures. TypeScript, build, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- All 124 existing Gerber SVG snapshots remain byte-for-byte unchanged, including the four coverlay snapshots previously rendered and visually inspected. The upstream stiffener SVG is byte-identical to current main.
- Full CI passes on source [`6244fd4`](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/commit/6244fd41fac12fbc99b06e359682f8f0f4eb236e): all five hosted checks are green, with no pending checks.

Addresses item 5 of [tscircuit #5277](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5277).

Release validation: installed npm `circuit-json@0.0.510`; all 186 tests (1,881 assertions), types, build, formatting, and diff checks pass. All 150 snapshot-file hashes are unchanged, and all five CI checks are green on `6244fd4`. No README changes.

title: Show datasheet footprints and copyable TSX with SSR indexing
description: Adds a Footprint section to datasheet pages, including a PCB SVG preview and a Copy TSX button for users to copy the complete stored component TSX with pin attributes.
body:
Datasheet pages now show a **Footprint** section with a `<chip footprint="..." />` usage example and a PCB SVG rendered on demand by `svg.tscircuit.com`. A **Copy TSX** button beside Download JSON copies the complete stored component TSX, including its pin attributes, and an expandable TSX section lets readers inspect it.

The server fetches the datasheet and includes the full TSX as escaped text in the initial HTML for indexing without JavaScript. That fetch has a five-second timeout and no retries; unavailable data leaves the page available for the client to fetch. Literal replacement characters in stored code are preserved when injecting SSR HTML.

The SVG preview submits a fixed standalone chip with a safely encoded footprint string. Missing metadata hides the relevant section or copy button. Preview loading is bounded to 20 seconds, with retry for failed or stalled requests. The preview and usage example stack on small screens. No dependency changes.

Validation:
- 36 focused and neighboring Bun tests pass, including complete SSR code preservation, safe escaping, missing TSX, API failures, and the five-second timeout.
- Five Playwright tests pass for desktop/mobile layout, preview failure/retry, timeout, missing metadata, and exact clipboard contents with pin attributes.
- Typecheck, touched-file formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Desktop and mobile screenshots reviewed.
- Live F1C100S preview was verified against the API and SVG service, including rendering at a 390px viewport.

The SVG service returns some compilation failures as HTTP 200 SVG images and has no CORS response header. Browser image events cannot distinguish those from successful SVGs; the preview handles network/decode failures and uses validated stored footprint metadata.

title: Add TSCIRCUIT_TOKEN environment variable authentication
description: Adds support for TSCIRCUIT_TOKEN environment variable authentication, allowing CI to authenticate without a saved session token.
body:

Use the same resolver for `auth print-token` and publishing. When using an environment token, fetch its account and publishing handle instead of relying on saved account metadata, allowing pushes with no saved session or handle.

title: Match schematic symbol circle stroke width
description: Sets the stroke width of reconstructed library-symbol circles to match the circuit-to-svg component-outline width, addressing discrepancies in rendering thickness for MOSFET body circles.
body:
## Motivation

Library-symbol circle primitives in Circuit JSON do not include a stroke width. During round-trip reconstruction, generated `schematiccircle` elements therefore fell back to the core `0.12` default, while circuit-to-svg renders component outlines at `0.02`. This made MOSFET body circles render six times thicker than the source schematic, which is visible in the LM5155EVM-FLY and LM251772EVM-PD comparisons.

## Summary

- set reconstructed library-symbol circles to the circuit-to-svg component-outline width
- keep the documented fallback beside the circle conversion because the Circuit JSON schema does not provide this property
- add focused runtime coverage and update every affected real TI EVM round-trip comparison

## Testing

- `bun test`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
