title: Reduce HD routing overhead with shared geometry and portfolio work
description: Reduces high-density routing overhead by sharing geometry and caching proven-free planar points, improving efficiency in routing calculations.
body:
High-density routing repeatedly queries the same obstacle broadphase, projects against fixed segment geometry, rebuilds fixed node topology for portfolio candidates, and rescans candidate work. This reuses that work while preserving neighbor order, strict clearance comparisons, candidate ownership, and search budgets.

- Share one planar broadphase query across a neighbor expansion, then apply the original per-neighbor bounds.
- Precompute segment geometry and cache proven-free planar points with exact coordinate/radius guards and obstacle-index invalidation.
- Share fixed topology within each portfolio attempt while explicitly copying mutable candidate and route snapshot data.
- Track candidate work incrementally, retaining the existing dynamic expansion budget and A13 accounting.

This isolates the HD group on current main after the repair03 update. The change contains five HD source files and four regression tests; dependency pins and DRC settings are unchanged.

Validation: **37 focused tests / 5,180 assertions pass**, including geometry boundaries, cache keys, topology ownership, snapshot independence, portfolio scheduling, grow/shrink behavior, and the dataset18 sample002 large-node expansion regression. TypeScript and the production build pass. Two independent code reviews found no correctness blockers.

Two official `/benchmark --dataset 18` comparisons measured the same main `3e8a0c7db9444aa596712649835563519d76d53d` and PR `9c1d5cd631d76d54e3e2e9648ba2b44efea13530`, sequentially on one 8-vCPU Blacksmith ARM runner per comparison:

| Comparison | P50 main → PR | P50 delta | Summed elapsed delta | HD routing delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [First run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2829#issuecomment-5966624100) | 85.385s → 86.745s | +1.59% | -1.33% | -7.18% |
| [Repeat](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2829#issuecomment-5966754882) | 87.556s → 84.458s | -3.54% | -4.79% | -8.89% |

Negative timing deltas are faster. HD routing and summed elapsed time improved in both comparisons; whole-pipeline P50 results were mixed, so these two runs do not establish a repeatable median speedup. The first comparison had lower HD routing time in all 16 cases and lower total elapsed time in 13; the repeat had lower HD routing time in 15 and lower total elapsed time in all 16.

Both comparisons retain **16/16 completion and 16/16 relaxed DRC passing**, with **zero DRC issues and timeouts**. Every exported non-timing routing metric, HD iteration count, via count, trace count, and lint count matches for all 16 samples. Individual portfolio counters are covered by the focused rescan-oracle tests; the official artifact does not export those counters.

All nine CI test shards, TypeScript, build, format, added-code, and deployment checks pass on the exact benchmarked head. The result comments link the workflows and raw report artifacts.

The default local Pipeline 9 returned a solved Muse e-paper result with **0.135411 mm** between different-net via copper lands, below the board's **0.15 mm** pad-edge rule. Keep drill clearance separate and retain the existing precision margin for coupled projection. Keep the indexed engine’s search heuristic separate: its single via copper gap applies to both same-net and different-net pairs, while the electrical pad rule applies to different nets. Add focused cases with distinct copper, trace and drill rules, including terminal and input preservation. No new repair stage, report-specific coordinates, post-routing correction, or DRC tolerance relaxation is added.

title: perf: reduce port ownership lookup and cache key overhead
description: Reduces overhead in port ownership lookup and cache key construction by indexing ownership once per solver and buffering typed serialization before hashing.
body:
Bugreport107 spends avoidable time repeatedly scanning ports for ownership and issuing small crypto updates while constructing intra-node cache keys. Index ownership once per uniform-distribution solver and buffer object-hash's typed serialization before hashing it.

The ownership index preserves first-match behavior for duplicate IDs and missing metadata. Cache keys retain typed numeric distinctions, including non-finite values; schema version 5 invalidates existing cache entries.

### Performance evidence

Local diagnostics on bugreport107-board-1726, Pipeline 9, default effort, Bun 1.3.14 on macOS arm64, based on a76f79a2:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Uniform port distribution | 3.146 s | 0.176 s |
| Cache-key construction across 2,762 captured nodes, median of seven alternating rounds after warmup | 171.1 ms | 48.1 ms |
| Complete routing, one fresh-process run per variant | 386.615 s | 387.576 s |

There is **no demonstrated end-to-end speedup** in this pair. Timing differences in unchanged repair and power-expansion stages exceeded the small savings. The isolated cache-key measurement excludes routing and candidate hyperparameter sweeps. Complete runs used the same installed dependencies without CPU sampling.

Both variants produced byte-for-byte identical JSON for 763 traces and identical step counts in every pipeline stage. Final quality counts were unchanged: 49 relaxed DRC errors and 67 with board clearance. Those errors also occur in the baseline; this does not satisfy the existing bugreport107 test's zero-error expectation.

### Validation

- Nine focused tests passed across eight files (49 assertions): existing cache-key and uniform-port regressions, plus new tests for buffered-key value distinctions and indexed ownership precedence.
- `bun run build` passed, including declarations.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Full bugreport107 before/after routing and both DRC evaluations completed; geometry was identical.

The larger follow-up opportunities remain regional repair's repeated net/obstacle setup, detailed-routing geometry work and independent-node scheduling, and per-step statistics allocation in power-trace expansion. They are outside this patch.

title: Enrich fetched part Circuit JSON with datasheet attributes
description: Imported chips need datasheet pin attributes in their Circuit JSON so downstream consumers can check electrical requirements. For example, the F1C100S analog supply requires 2.8V, and the imported regulator output must preserve its actual voltage variant.
body:
Imported chips need datasheet pin attributes in their Circuit JSON so downstream consumers can check electrical requirements. For example, the F1C100S analog supply requires 2.8V, and the imported regulator output must preserve its actual voltage variant.

```ts
const engine = new JlcPcbPartsEngine()
const circuitJson = await engine.fetchPartCircuitJson({
  supplierPartNumber: "C460327",
  includeDatasheetInformation: true,
})
```

The returned array contains canonical electrical attributes on existing source ports. Enrichment is opt-in, with constructor defaults and per-call overrides; no composition adapter or shared props interface change is needed.

- Keep the supplier method as orchestration: focused modules handle registry fetching/schema validation/caching, conversion to Circuit JSON, and footprint reconciliation.
- Validate API pin_attributes against the existing props schema and map all supported fields to canonical Circuit JSON. Physical numbers, BGA hints and shared signal labels are reconciled without replacing geometry, IDs, names or connectivity. Preserve false/zero and omitted existing fields; ambiguous matches stay unchanged.
- Use supplier-reported manufacturer identity, reject requested/imported mismatches, and require exact manufacturer search matches for enriched imports. This prevents attributes from a different regulator voltage variant from being applied.
- Enforce a five-second deadline across headers and the JSON body, including transports that ignore abort. Timeout errors explain that pin attributes may not be populated. A missing record preserves the imported circuit; HTTP, transport, schema and conversion failures reject.
- Coalesce concurrent requests, bound caches to 256 entries per fetch implementation, honor HTTP max-age/Age/no-cache/no-store with a 60-second maximum, clone returned records, and retry misses/failures. Registry requests bypass EasyEDA proxies and their credentials.
- Retain standalone metadata lookup and exported pure reconciliation for callers that already have Circuit JSON. Metadata includes available PDF URLs, footprinter strings and TSX source; stored TSX is never evaluated.

No production dependencies added. props and zod stay in devDependencies with validators bundled. The existing circuit-json devDependency uses published 0.0.509 for all canonical direction/GPIO/output-mode fields. Core aggregate warnings and voltage compatibility checks remain follow-ups.

Validation:
- 70 tests pass, including captured real supplier/API records for 140 F1C-board contacts, alternate LED numbering, BGA matching, schema round-trips, immutable geometry, wrong voltage variants, explicit overrides, cache retries, proxy isolation, and stalled-fetch/body deadlines.
- Type checking, formatting, build and declaration generation pass.
- Packed library runs direct part enrichment, opt-in, caching and reconciliation in Node without installed runtime dependencies.
- Read-only live verification passes for all nine board ICs/140 physical contacts against current API attributes. Current F1C pin33 has no structured attributes and remains explicitly missing. The old regulator's 1.8V output and 2.8V/2.5V rails remain verified. API Cache-Control and ETag/304 checks pass; Cloudflare DYNAMIC does not demonstrate an edge-cache hit.

title: Fix F1C AVCC connection rendered as inline label stubs
description: Fixes the rendering of the AVCC connection in the F1C schematic to ensure it is displayed as a single straight trace with an inline label instead of two inline terminal labels.
body:
The AVCC connection in [tscircuit/core#4334](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4334), `tests/drc/__snapshots__/source-pin-voltage-compatible-f1c-schematic.snap.svg`, renders as two inline terminal labels despite an unobstructed straight path between the regulator VOUT and F1C AVCC pins. This change produces one straight trace with one inline AVCC label.

The pins are 3.7 mm apart, beyond the input's 2.4 mm MSP distance limit. Inline conversion consumes their fallback labels before final trace recovery, and the simple recovery helper previously supported only perpendicular elbows. Recover straight connections between facing pins on inline-eligible two-pin named nets before inline conversion, using the existing obstacle, label, trace, ground, and section checks. Other named-net recovery retains its existing timing; explicit-wire recovery remains supported.

Commit order:
- `d6a15e5`: Exact solver input captured from core PR #4334 at `d84f47b7329e8fd1e3092124f604ffe109096559`, broken SVG snapshot, and failing straight-trace regression.
- `ab71ac6`: Fix, corrected snapshot, horizontal/vertical and fallback controls. Update the existing HDC3020 snapshot where the same bug hid a clear straight ALERT/GPIO wire behind terminal labels.

Running the built solver with the original core #4334 fixture emits exactly one straight schematic edge, one inline AVCC label, and no voltage DRC error.

title: Support configurable crosshatch pitch and copper width
description: Allows crosshatched pours to specify crosshatchPitch and crosshatchWidth in millimetres on both direct regions and Circuit JSON converter options, with validation and default settings.
body:
Allows crosshatched pours to specify `crosshatchPitch` and `crosshatchWidth` in millimetres on both direct regions and Circuit JSON converter options. Defaults preserve the existing 1mm pitch / 0.25mm width geometry; dimensions alone do not enable hatching.

Grid spacing, square opening size, edge rim, protection around connections and clearances, and fragment area/inset filters all follow the selected dimensions. Invalid enabled dimensions fail clearly, and a candidate-cell limit prevents extremely small pitches from allocating unbounded grids.

Validation: all 103 tests, typecheck, build and format check pass. Regression tests measure emitted opening areas, grid positions and clipped rims, check per-region converter forwarding and invalid input, and preserve the existing default snapshots.


Visual regression snapshot: identical 10 × 8mm boards at the same scale and grid origin, comparing default sizing, increased pitch, and increased copper width. The snapshot also shows clipped boundary openings and the width-dependent rim.

![Default and custom crosshatch size comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/1e670b4403e15c0d72afa52ca39d1e1ca7d2e64e/tests/__snapshots__/crosshatch-sizing-snapshot.snap.svg)

title: Clip crosshatch openings at pour edges and discard tiny remnants
description: Clips square openings at pour edges, retaining partial openings while discarding small fragments to ensure a clean copper pour.
body:
Crosshatch currently drops an entire square opening when it reaches the pour boundary, leaving uneven solid bands. Clip eligible squares against the inset copper region instead, retaining triangles, trapezoids and other partial openings behind a 0.25 mm solid rim. Board-edge clearance is applied before the rim; the `crosshatch` boolean API is unchanged.

Keep whole-cell exclusion around same-net pads/vias/traces, thermal reliefs, holes, keepouts and higher-priority pour clearances. Separating obstacle clearances from board-edge margins lets edge cells clip without carving around protected contacts or isolating their copper. Existing pour priority and solid-fill behavior remain unchanged.

Filter each connected opening fragment independently:
- Discard area below 0.0625 mm².
- Discard fragments that disappear under a 0.125 mm inward offset, including long thin slivers that pass the area test.

The filters derive from the fixed mesh width; they are not manufacturer-specific design rules. Fragment decomposition runs one grid cell at a time to avoid a WASM memory failure with thousands of disconnected openings.

Validation:
- Full solver suite: 100 tests pass, including rim/clearance, concave and slanted outline, small-area and sliver, edge-pad connectivity, and large-board regressions.
- TypeScript check, ESM/declaration build, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Updated rectangular SVG snapshot and added a labeled irregular-outline snapshot; visually inspected the result.
- Gerber smoke check: 112 BRep openings produce 112 clear regions plus the outer copper region.
- Local 100 × 100 mm benchmark: 9,940 openings in approximately 0.4 seconds. No timing threshold is asserted in CI.

Snapshot: [clipped outline](https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/blob/feat/clipped-crosshatch-openings/tests/__snapshots__/crosshatch-clipped-outline.snap.svg).

title: Support crosshatched copper pours with a boolean option
description: Adds crosshatch option for copper pours, allowing for a 45-degree mesh with specified dimensions, while preserving solid fill and existing copper connectivity.
body:
Adds `crosshatch?: boolean` to pour regions and Circuit JSON converter options. With `true`, the solver emits a 45-degree mesh with 0.25 mm copper width and 1 mm pitch, encoded as ordinary BRep inner rings. `false` or omission preserves solid fill.

Openings are removed only when wholly contained inside the cleared pour and separated from existing boundaries and same-net pads/vias/traces by 0.25 mm. This preserves thermal spokes, narrow necks and existing copper connectivity without adding bridges across clearances. Small regions may remain solid; this does not introduce a new floating-island policy. The grid is anchored at board (0, 0), and higher-priority regions reserve their hatch openings against lower-priority different-net pours.

The implementation uses batched polygon containment instead of a boolean operation per grid cell. No new Circuit JSON shape or renderer-specific pattern is required.

Companion API: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/897. Core forwarding: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4327 (draft pending dependency releases).

Validation:
- Full solver suite: 95 passing tests, including new geometry, thermal, clearance, priority, layer, shifted-grid and small-region regressions.
- TypeScript check, package build and changed-file formatting checks passed.
- Visually inspected the new SVG snapshot and a rendered Gerber export. The 10 mm fixture's 60 BRep holes produce 60 clear Gerber regions plus the outer copper region.
- Local benchmark: a 100 x 100 mm region with 9,660 holes solved in approximately 0.2 seconds (Apple Silicon; illustrative, not a CI timing assertion).

title: test: reproduce thumbnail corruption from triangles behind camera
description: Reproduces a rendering bug where a display extends behind the thumbnail camera, causing incorrect painting over the PCB, with a regression test that intentionally fails to highlight the issue.
body:
A large display extending behind the thumbnail camera incorrectly paints over the PCB. This regression uses a bright green PCB and a blue display physically beside it, reproducing the missing-board artifact without external models.

![Expected, broken actual render, and magenta pixel differences](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/poppygl/bb280c5f32a6f159d3c6f1dab33be78e80f47c86/tests/render/__snapshots__/near-plane-comparison.snap.png)

Each render is 512 × 512 pixels; the labeled comparison is 1536 × 648. The left panel is an independent reference with the display shortened analytically at the near plane. The middle panel is the actual renderer output. Magenta marks incorrect pixels in the right panel. Arrows label the PCB and visible display.

The actual-render and comparison snapshots intentionally record the broken output, so the stacked fix in #41 produces a visible image diff. Separate pixel assertions require the PCB to remain green and the visible display to remain blue, and compare the unannotated render against the reference. This PR intentionally fails that correctness check.

CI uploads the visual snapshots after every test run, including failures; the snapshot matcher also saves actual and diff PNGs when snapshots mismatch. Download the `visual-snapshots` artifact from the Bun Test run.

Validation: 32 existing tests pass, the regression fails; type checking and formatting pass.

title: fix: clip triangles before perspective division
description: Fixes the missing PCB when an attached display crosses behind the thumbnail camera by clipping triangles against the homogeneous near plane before perspective division.
body:
Fixes the missing PCB when an attached display crosses behind the thumbnail camera. Triangles are clipped against the homogeneous near plane (`z + w >= 0`) before perspective division, preserving their visible portions. Stacked on #40.

Before: the blue display incorrectly paints over the green PCB; magenta marks wrong pixels.

![Before clipping fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/poppygl/bb280c5f32a6f159d3c6f1dab33be78e80f47c86/tests/render/__snapshots__/near-plane-comparison.snap.png)

After: the PCB stays green, the visible display remains blue, and the difference panel is empty.

![After clipping fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/poppygl/451571a6045e216d3f57c19e19ce9426567de3e8/tests/render/__snapshots__/near-plane-comparison.snap.png)

Each render is 512 × 512 pixels, with labels and arrows; each comparison is 1536 × 648. The actual-render and comparison snapshots change in this PR, exposing the fix in GitHub's image diff. The expected image remains unchanged. The oracle is geometry shortened analytically at the near plane, independent of the clipping implementation.

Clipping preserves winding, reuses shared-edge intersections, and interpolates positions, normals, UVs, and colors before perspective-correct rasterization. Fully visible meshes retain their original geometry. Five additional labeled visual cases cover one/two vertices behind the eye, a vertex on the eye plane, a vertex between the eye and near plane, and fully hidden geometry, including texture/color/normal interpolation and model/view transforms.

Validation: all 38 tests pass; type checking and formatting pass. The original Muse GLB also renders the PCB correctly with its unchanged thumbnail camera. CI uploads `visual-snapshots`, including comparisons and any actual/diff PNGs from mismatches.

The published registry thumbnail still needs regeneration after the updated renderer reaches cloud build dependencies. Default camera framing of the complete assembly is a separate improvement.

body:
Global DRC repair repeatedly deduplicates/sorts neighboring item indexes and recomputes segment-contact distances while exploring candidates. This reduces that work while preserving candidate order and contact choices:

- Reuse generation-stamped bitsets to enumerate spatial candidates in ascending original-index order.
- Use a stable first-minimum contact scan, computing each distance once and preserving ties.
- Reject distant obstacles before connectivity/layer predicates.
- Allocate via-group visited sets lazily and remove redundant deduplication of disjoint ranges.

This main-targeting branch starts at `6f6e5dbfc1eb5616f2b81b4ace76884c85d572b5`. It preserves main's diameter parameter and observed unique layer order in `collectViaNodes`, including a `[3, 1, 2]` stack. It excludes unrelated fixes from the older autorouter-pinned branch. Benchmark additions change no production algorithms, thresholds, or settings.

The controlled full-repair replay compares exact historical **ccad3906→aee0ef2** worktrees with the same transitive dependencies and fresh native **ConnectivityMap 0.0.19** for both. Three sequential alternating timed runs per variant gave **26.3251→18.9977 s (27.8% lower median)**. All eight runs, including warmups, had identical routes, 16 iterations, repair statistics, and independent DRC output. Source/fixture checks, all samples, provenance, and reproduction steps are committed under `benchmarks/repair-isolation`.

The official repair-only consumer [autorouter #2827](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2827) measured **4.318% lower P50 (95.885→91.744 s)** and **3.146% lower total elapsed time**, with all **16 cases completing and passing relaxed DRC**, zero issues and timeouts. Both this official result and the controlled full-repair replay concern the original **ccad→aee pins**, not the current-main port. The benchmarked pinned branch stays in #154.

Run `bun run benchmark:spatial-index --out /tmp/repair-spatial-benchmark.json` to compare original Set/sort grid, production bitset grid, Flatbush and RBush over nine deterministic distributions, a labeled static Pipeline9 fixture, and four actual captured repair windows. Production-compatible mode indexes integer cell rectangles and checks every complete sorted output against a brute-force oracle. Physical-AABB mode is separately labeled because moving geometry prevents it from being an equivalent production replacement. Tree packages are development-only; construction/query costs, nine trials, ranges, checksums, and installed versions are recorded.

On this main port's two captured segment windows, bitset query medians fell **63.9%/62.2%**. Summed separate build/query medians across all four windows fell **25.3549→10.2059 ms (59.7%)**. Flatbush won small via windows and long-rectangle generated cases; bitsets lost on sparse scattered-ID queries at 16,384 items. These are index-workload measurements, not full dataset18 proof. All samples and interpretation are under `benchmarks/spatial-index`.

A benchmark-only same-aee full-repair backend comparison gave **17.5192 s bitsets vs 21.4458 s Flatbush (22.4% more tree-adapter time)** with identical outputs/statistics/independent DRC across all six runs. This limited experiment used two alternating measured runs per variant plus warmups and includes bounds-snapshot conversion/counters. RBush is measured in the index harness; no full-stage RBush timing was run.

Earlier single-pass diagnostics observed **39.716→30.176→24.435 s**: the combined bitset/obstacle/via-allocation group saved 9.540s, then stable first-minimum selection saved 5.741s. Those runs used the previous shared/indexed connectivity setup, had possible local contention, and are not the newer native-connectivity isolation. The grouped/marginal observations cannot establish independent causal shares for each change.

Local validation: **96 tests / 3,955 assertions passed**, full TypeScript checking including all three benchmark runners and USB fixture, and full repository format check. Independent fairness reviews verified ordered oracle parity, identical build boundaries, and clearly labeled construction estimates. The already-mocked portfolio incumbent regression now replays its genuine native CC1 constructor input, with capture provenance, while retaining every assertion and both live USB integration tests. No test timeout was changed. The complete suite also passes under CI's Bun 1.3.1.

body:
BGA discovery could compact a supplier footprint using the wrong pin order or the wrong missing-ball mask. On the 624-ball i.MX6, a high copper-overlap score previously allowed a center gap and aliases that conflicted with physical pin IDs.

Measure the populated grid for circular and square pads, preserve its missing-ball mask, and evaluate all four origins with the named row-major, column-major, and coordinate-only conventions from Footprinter 0.0.430. Estimate pitch across the full span to avoid accumulated supplier-coordinate rounding. Compare ball-coordinate hints as well as numeric IDs, requiring both to agree when both are supplied. Keep legacy row-label candidates available.

The independent C430888 / MCIMX6D6AVT08AD fixture now discovers:

```text
bga624_grid25x25_p0.8mm_pad0.4mm_missing(1)_blorigin_pinnumbering(columnmajor)
```

This upgrades an existing Footprinter dependency; it adds no dependencies. Refresh the two JST expectations affected by Footprinter's already released PH geometry change (the same differences reproduce on unchanged discovery code).

Validation:

- Full suite: 166 tests pass; typecheck, format check, and package build pass.
- Regression coverage includes asymmetric gaps, every origin, both numeric orders, coordinate-only IDs, skipped/extended row labels, legacy labels, conflicting coordinates, and unsupported numeric IDs.
- The independent supplier fixture checks all 624 numeric IDs, ball labels, and pad positions.
- Additional local import round-trip verification covers MCIMX6D6AVT08AD, MCIMX6U7CVM08AD, and MCIMX6U6AVM08AC: 1,872 contacts. The CLI's existing mapping/replacement helpers produce identity maps with unchanged pin labels and attributes; every rendered contact retains its canonical attributes. Maximum pad-center error is 0.000196 mm. Rendering uses an isolated local Core build containing merged PR4302, so this check does not claim a released CLI already includes these updates.

After this merges and publishes, the CLI can consume the new discovery release with Footprinter 0.0.430 or newer.

title: Honor declared copper clearance between different-net vias
description: Fixes copper clearance violations between different-net vias during power expansion in PCB design.
body:
Power expansion can move a via into a different net's copper clearance even when drill spacing passes. The full-board regression in tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2823 is clean before expansion, but afterward has four copper gaps of 0.130–0.141 mm against a declared 0.15 mm minimum. The spatial index currently uses its 0.10 mm trace rule for those via pairs.

Read `minPadEdgeToPadEdgeClearance` and apply it when prospective via copper is checked against other via copper. Expand the spatial query accordingly so larger pad rules cannot miss candidate vias. Trace rules remain independent, same-net copper remains exempt, and drill spacing still applies on all nets.

The focused regression fails before the change and passes afterward for both mutable and fixed trace vias, with checks for legal spacing, same-net copper, same-net drill spacing, and independent trace clearance.

Validation: all 48 tests pass (545 assertions), TypeScript and build pass. A [compatibility commit](https://github.com/tscircuit/power-trace-expander/commit/2ecd1cde8a72ef45d7d549a788de9b5379e39108) applies this same fix to the autorouter's existing pinned dependency commit, avoiding unrelated dependency changes during integration. That base passes all 86 tests (2,878 assertions), TypeScript and build; replaying the captured Linux CI pre-expansion geometry produces zero declared-rule DRC errors.

title: Type peripheral source plans for consumer TypeScript settings
description: Explicitly types the empty sourcePlans array as FanoutRoutePlan to resolve TypeScript errors TS2345 and TS2339 in downstream typechecks when strict null checks are enabled.
body:
Consumers that enable strict null checks but disable noImplicitAny infer the empty sourcePlans array as never[]. Because fanout-solver exports TypeScript source, this causes TS2345 and TS2339 in downstream typechecks and forced 3d-viewer to carry a Bun patch.

Explicitly type the array as FanoutRoutePlan[] and check the library with noImplicitAny disabled in the typecheck script. This changes only types.

Validation: reproduced both errors before the fix; all three typecheck configurations pass afterward; the existing peripheral source reservation test passes (264 assertions).

title: Preserve compact coupled routes during reachability checks
description: Preserves the established retry order for ordinary terminal searches and opts into early reachability retries only when negotiating fresh dogbone sites, ensuring that routing quality and physical pair-spacing limits are maintained without introducing new routing logic or quality thresholds.
body:
Ordinary bus routing changed candidate selection after the global reachability shortcut landed: core's existing AM3352 regression grew to 1,597 mm of copper and separated the DQS0 pair by 0.672 mm. Keep ordinary terminal searches' established retry order and opt into early reachability retries only when negotiating fresh dogbone sites. The optional component index is built lazily and remains counted against the 64 MiB cache cap.

The original core fixture now uses 1,494 mm of copper, with maximum detour 2.029 and maximum pair interior gap 0.138 mm. Add a regression using the existing raw-pad fixture and core's unchanged compactness and independent physical pair-spacing limits. No saved route geometry, chip-specific routing logic, or relaxed quality thresholds.

**CI limitation:** the final hosted Ubuntu benchmark is 6/8: inner-layer left/above exceed the 60-second cap on the slower runners. Tests, type checking, formatting, package validation, and preview checks pass. An earlier [standard Ubuntu run completed 8/8](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/37119869068) (10.8–57.3 seconds), but that timing is not consistent across hosted runners. The final [benchmark run](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/37120648732) remains red; the limit has not been relaxed.

The built package also routes the hardest inner-layer above sample under Node 26/V8 locally in 57.8 seconds, with 47/47 signals and native DRC, matching, and coupling checks passing.

The solver computes paired corridors, local signal dogbones, and single-layer carriers from the input geometry. It jointly negotiates newly generated dogbone sites and signal layers, then repairs the remaining bounded carrier/via conflict region. Supplied fanouts stay immutable; vias remain terminal dogbones only. This adds no chip-specific names, coordinates, saved signal routes, or weakened acceptance rules. Disconnected-grid checks and conservative score lower bounds avoid futile searches without changing candidate ordering or accepted geometry.

Shared tuning banks preserve pair spacing on either side of the centerline. Duplicate vertices can no longer conceal sharp curve handoffs; length tuning skips those candidates and continues searching. Regression tests cover multi-terminal reachability, rotated package sites, immutable copper, paired meanders, and conventional curve handoffs.

title: Route the AM3352 below-RAM sample on inner1 and inner2
description: Routes the AM3352 benchmark with RAM below the CPU, utilizing inner1 and inner2 layers for signal carriers, achieving a routing time of 27.817 seconds for 47 signals while maintaining power integrity and DRC compliance.
body:
The fifth AM3352 benchmark keeps RAM below the CPU and restricts every signal carrier to inner1 or inner2. It initially exceeded the 30-second routing budget. With this change it completes all 47 signals in **27.817 seconds**, using **24 inner1 / 23 inner2 carriers**, while preserving the 161 supplied VCC/GND dogbones.

Global `allowedLayers` intersects bus constraints during allocation and retries. The four-layer physical stack, top-pad joins, and through-via obstacles remain intact. Existing fanout handoffs on excluded layers fail rather than receiving another dogbone.

When a standalone differential pair shares a matched bus's carrier layer, route the independent byte buses first, the standalone pair second, and controls last. Each completed stage becomes fixed copper for the next stage. Three exact performance changes make the constrained case fit the budget: median partitioning instead of sorting each copper-index subtree, Floyd heap removal with unchanged tie ordering, and prepared chord projections during obstacle rasterization.

`./benchmark.sh` now runs only the five declared samples. The audit checks carrier availability, complete connectivity, immutable power copper, combined-copper DRC, total pad-to-pad length matching, and exterior pair coupling. Snapshot export validates all five before writing any routed artifact.

| Sample | Routing | Including validation | Signals | DRC |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Control | 12.004 s | 13.491 s | 47/47 | Pass |
| Right | 12.575 s | 16.133 s | 47/47 | Pass |
| Left | 17.381 s | 22.141 s | 47/47 | Pass |
| Above | 21.965 s | 25.918 s | 47/47 | Pass |
| Inner layers only | 27.817 s | 29.367 s | 47/47 | Pass |

Measured serially in fresh processes on macOS arm64 / Bun 1.3.2 with `./benchmark.sh --timeout-seconds 30 --require-all-solved`. Every case passes the native 0.635 mm byte skew and 0.127 mm pair skew limits, with zero separated pair length outside package fanouts. The inner-only case also has zero acute corners, illegal ordinary angles, or sharp meander corners. Timing depends on the machine; CI runs the existing 180-second benchmark budget. The inner-only case also passes on the standard Ubuntu CI runner in 55.868 s routing / 58.984 s including validation.

All five routed images were inspected. The original four PNGs are unchanged: [control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/solver/am3352-inner-layers/docs/routed-am3352-placements/control-solved.png), [right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/solver/am3352-inner-layers/docs/routed-am3352-placements/right-solved.png), [left](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/solver/am3352-inner-layers/docs/routed-am3352-placements/left-solved.png), [above](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/solver/am3352-inner-layers/docs/routed-am3352-placements/above-solved.png).

Resolve only actual entrance dependencies, using the full differential-channel width, to open longer central runs and test narrower banks. This reduces control bounds another **11.2%** and left bounds **26.5%** beyond current main. Right and above retain their previous bounds.

title: Persist natural bus length, spacing and impedance constraints
description: Persist natural bus and differential-pair routing constraints directly on source_bus: length bounds and targets, resolved length-matching references, centerline spacing, and flat nominalminmax impedance values. No vendor profiles or protocol defaults are introduced.
body:
Persist natural bus and differential-pair routing constraints directly on `source_bus`: length bounds and targets, resolved length-matching references, centerline spacing, and flat nominal/min/max impedance values. No vendor profiles or protocol defaults are introduced.

Bus/pair rule violations use the specific `pcb_bus_routing_constraint_error` discriminated by `routing_rule`, with structured bus/trace references and required rule-specific measurements. Checks that cannot be verified use a separate `pcb_bus_routing_constraint_warning` without measurement fields; missing geometry uses an empty PCB-trace reference array. body:
Put routing intent directly on `bus` and `differentialpair`. A bus names its associated pair with `lengthMatchTo`; its `maxLengthSkew` applies to the combined signals while the pair can retain its own tighter skew. Shared target lengths refer to existing signals/groups, without another grouping element.

```tsx
<bus
  name="DATA0"
  connections={[...dataSignals, maskSignal]}
  lengthMatchTo=".DQS0"
  maxLengthSkew="25mil"
  maxLength={{ reference: "longest_manhattan" }}
  pcbTraceSpacing="3w"
  pcbSpacingToOtherSignals="4w"
  targetImpedance="50±25ohm"
/>
```

Impedance input is scalar/XML-compatible: numeric ohms, a unit string, or an absolute tolerance string. `targetImpedance="50±25ohm"` normalizes to nominal 50 ohms and flat Min/Max bounds 25–75 ohms. Alternatively, declare `targetImpedanceMin="25ohm" targetImpedanceMax="75ohm"` without a nominal target. Differential pairs support the equivalent targetDifferentialImpedance/Min/Max props. Existing scalar targets keep their scalar output, object impedance ranges are rejected, and conflicting bounds/tolerance notations are rejected. `pcbEscapeSpacing` is removed for now.

Adds direct `minLength`, `maxLength`, `targetLength`, `lengthTolerance`, `pcbTraceSpacing` and `pcbSpacingToOtherSignals` props. Relative length expressions and width-relative spacing retain their geometry intent; no electrical defaults, protocol profile, new JSX element, expected-member-count field, check-only grouping API or generic constraint wrapper is introduced. Existing connections/pair polarity supply membership; existing pinAttributes remain available for pin-level electrical intent. The existing relative length object API remains unchanged in this update.

See docs/pcb-bus-routing.md for data/strobe and command/clock authoring examples, accepted inputs, normalized output, conflicts and migration.

Validation: all 610 local tests, type check and package build pass. All four documentation generators run. CI is green: tests, types, formatting and package preview build pass. Core/checks/Circuit JSON PRs #4346/#374/#862 still need adaptation to this author-facing API; this props PR does not claim runtime enforcement or hardware compliance.

title: fix: emit non-plated through-hole slots as pcb_cutout
description: Fixes the omission of non-plated through-hole slots in the generated TSX footprint by correctly emitting them as pcb_cutout polygons.
body:
## Summary

`C5378731` (SK6812MINI-EA) declares a 3.6 × 3.2 mm non-plated through-hole slot
for its light guide, but the generated TSX footprint contained only the 4
`<smtpad>` elements, the slot was silently dropped.

EasyEDA does not store this slot as a `HOLE` record. It stores it as a
`SOLIDREGION` path on the multi-layer layer with `fillStyle="npth"`, which
matched neither `isPcbSolidRegionCutout` (requires `"cutout"`) nor the
document-layer branch of the shape loop, so it fell through both.

## Change

- `isPcbSolidRegionNpth` + `handleNpthSlot` emit `fillStyle="npth"` regions
  as a `pcb_cutout` polygon.
- Extracted the M/L/A path walker from `handleFabricationNoteSolidRegion` into
  `expandEasyEdaPathData`, shared by both callers. Behaviour-preserving, and
  also needed for fidelity: the schema only recovers `M`/`L` commands, so the
  `A` commands carrying the corner fillets had to be expanded here or the
  corners would render chamfered.

`pcb_cutout` rather than `pcb_hole` because `pcb_hole` can only express
circle/rect/oval, and `circuit-to-svg` renders `"oval"` as a full ellipse,
which would have rounded away the fillets.

## Testing

`tests/convert-to-ts/C5378731-to-ts.test.ts` gains a numeric test asserting a
single `pcb_cutout` polygon with a 3.600 × 3.2005 mm bbox (source path spans
x 4036.0634→4050.2365, y 3017.8274→3030.4278 in 10-mil units) and more than 9
points, proving the arcs were expanded.

`bun test tests/convert-to-ts/C5378731-to-ts.test.ts` (2 pass, 0 fail.)

Existing SVG/3D/inline snapshots for this part were regenerated: the new cutout
participates in recentring, so every coordinate in that footprint shifts.

description: Add assembly.printedpart with jscad, model, modelUrl, or cadModel as alternative geometry sources, reusing existing assembly CAD resolution and transforms.
body:
Add `<assembly.printedpart>` with `jscad`, `model`, `modelUrl`, or `cadModel` as alternative geometry sources, reusing existing assembly CAD resolution and transforms.

JSCAD parts expose mounting faces through named reference rectangles inside their geometry. This supports a printed spacer between a motor and a board:

```tsx
<assembly.device>
  <assembly.motor name="MOTOR" model="nema17_backfaceholes" />
  <assembly.printedpart
    name="SPACER"
    jscad={<MotorSpacer />}
    mountedTo="MOTOR.backface"
    mountFace="motor"
  />
  <Rp2040MotorController mountedTo="SPACER.board" />
</assembly.device>
```

Core exports the headless `jscad` namespace, compiles JSX to operation JSON, and removes reference geometry before emission. Mesh generation remains in viewers/exporters. Mounting supports gaps, chains, and forward references; invalid or ambiguous attachments produce errors. A mounted board retains its PCB coordinates and fabrication plane.

Validation: 39 assembly tests pass, including model-source coverage and annotated snapshots of mounting rotations, shaft directions, and chained parts. TypeScript, build, and distribution smoke tests pass.

Uses published npm versions: `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.685`, `jscad-planner@^0.0.18`, `jscad-fiber@^0.0.88`, and `circuit-json@^0.0.515`. Assembly source records use `printedpart`, `motor`, or `subassembly` ftypes; modeled devices and screens use `subassembly`. CAD references retain their existing source ownership.

```tsx
<assembly.device>
  <assembly.motor name="NEMA17" standard="nema17" wireConnection="jst-ph-6" />

    mountedTo="NEMA17.backface"

    mountOrientation="top_layer_toward_mount_face"

</assembly.device>
```

Component anchors use finalized PCB centers relative to the mounting axis; edges use outward directions, defaulting to `rightedge`. Orientation selects the PCB layer facing the backface independently of the gap. Explicit incompatible shaft direction/orientation, missing or ambiguous anchors, and unavailable references produce named errors. Parsed props remain immutable. This stage supports one horizontal PCB per motor and references to that mounted motor.

body:
Add parameterized external spur gears and worm screws to the React and vanilla renderers, including `Footprinter3d` model-string routing, standalone JSCAD solids, and indexed mesh factories. Mechanical gear strings also work through the with-pads API without generating PCB copper.

Examples:

```ts
spurgear24_m1mm_w5mm_bore5mm_hubdiameter10mm_hublength3mm
wormgear_m1mm_d10mm_l20mm_starts2_left_bore3mm
```

Spur gears use sampled involute flanks, circular tooth tips/root valleys, optional through bores and integrated hubs. Worm screws sweep a trapezoidal axial rack profile, supporting one to eight starts and either hand. Both support phase and resolution controls, adapt root faceting to preserve thin bore/hub walls, and reject mesh allocations above one million vertices. The guide documents pitch conventions and approximation limits: spur root fillets/undercut and conjugate worm wheels are outside this initial implementation.

Depends on https://github.com/tscircuit/modelprinter/pull/11. The manifest and lockfile pin its published gear-enabled package preview; replace that preview with a released ModelPrinter version after the spec lands.

Validation: `bun test --timeout 10000` passes all 323 tests, and build, TypeScript and formatting pass. Geometry regressions cover manifold edges, outward winding, positive triangle areas/volume, independent involute and helical profile measurements, handedness, starts/lead, bores, near-root walls, allocation limits, large phases, and React/vanilla parity. Eight Cosmos variants and three four-view PNG snapshots cover the new models.

Spacing checks include partial copper and unrelated signals outside declared buses, use the larger local width for width multipliers, and exclude declared differential partners and same-net fragments. No reduced escape-spacing allowance is inferred. Violations use specific `pcb_bus_routing_constraint_error` elements; missing geometry and physical impedance analysis use separate `pcb_bus_routing_constraint_warning` elements, so an unverified rule cannot look like a pass.

Diagnostics are discriminated by `routing_rule`, with required rule-specific measurement names. Lengths and centerline spacing are mm, impedance is ohms; no `units` property is emitted. Spacing errors include the measured separation and offending PCB trace.

Validation: 14 focused geometry/constraint tests pass. Circuit JSON #862 is merged and this PR now uses published circuit-json 0.0.514. CI validates the complete suite and package build against that release. Core integration follows in #4346; these checks do not certify an electrical interface or replace physical stackup and signal-integrity analysis.

title: Support polygon solder paste in Gerber output
description: Adds support for polygon solder paste in Gerber output, fixing the unsupported shape error and enabling closed regions with concave outlines and inner openings.
body:
Polygon solder paste currently fails Gerber export with `Unsupported shape polygon`. Polygon apertures now produce closed regions on F_Paste or B_Paste, including concave outlines and inner openings.

Reuses the existing polygon region emitter and copper-pour/silkscreen cutout pattern: dark outer region, clear openings, then restored dark polarity. The shared emitter applies optional Y reflection. Region apertures are registered only for the matching paste layer, leaving copper, solder mask, outline, and drill output unchanged. Uses published circuit-json 0.0.513; no new runtime dependency or public API.

Inner contours cannot create holes merely by starting another contour inside the same region: [Ucamco's Gerber specification, section 4.10](https://www.ucamco.com/files/downloads/file_en/456/gerber-layer-format-specification-revision-2022-02_en.pdf) fills separate contours individually. This follows the repo's existing clear-polarity approach.

Validation: regression reproduces the unsupported-shape error without the fix. All five GitHub checks are green. Locally, all 187 tests pass, plus type checking, formatting, and build. The regression checks both layers, optional Y reflection, unchanged input and unrelated output files, restored polarity before a subsequent circular pad, and independent Gerber parsing without geometry warnings. The unchanged ICS-43434 import rendered through the merged core generator exports four polygon regions and five standard paste flashes while preserving all nine pads.

Follows merged [core #4344](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4344).

![Top polygon paste with inner opening](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/c139768b87e36a1092f44e318170469b3d98550f/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/polygon-paste-top.snap.svg)

title: Reduce port and Tiny Hypergraph routing overhead
description: Reduces routing overhead by optimizing port routing processes, including region scanning, workspace allocation, and statistics management, while maintaining existing routing policies and behaviors.
body:
Port routing repeatedly scans regions, allocates Tiny workspaces and copies unused statistics. Index lookups in source order, reuse solver/intersection workspaces and cached hop IDs, sparsify terminal endpoint sets, skip dominated scoring and materialize statistics when read. Routing policies, candidate costs/order and budgets retain their existing behavior.

Selected as one of three groups after six independent official dataset18 pairs against main `ef0ad74a0f389d4ad884f206453972157b1d3d77`. The [isolated result](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2834#issuecomment-5974302703) on exact head `fb6e3f62436d08f7bbc6ecb1ee70e251a42a6ac4` verifies P50 **87.715112 → 82.442135s (6.01% lower)** and summed runtime **10.78% lower**. Both revisions complete and pass relaxed DRC on 16/16 samples with zero issues/timeouts; all exported non-timing metrics, iterations, trace/via/lint counts and 360-second budgets match exactly. Checkout SHAs, ZIP digest and raw report bytes were independently verified.

The nine-file diff contains six port/Tiny source files, two regressions and only the Tiny dependency pin. [tiny-hypergraph #226](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/pull/226) targets dependency main. Consumer performance backport `4e2156904b1c3f2271dcc256021246faf811d641` retains its existing `31459ce` routing policies; main counterpart `693182319872579ff9449869890686c3f8616044` retains that branch’s policies. Inherited compact-hop incidence storage is excluded from this change’s attribution.

Validation: Seven focused tests / 80 assertions, TypeScript and ESM/DTS build pass. Exact installed source pins and the independent consumer/main mapping were audited. All 20 checks on this head are green.

The [combined three-group result](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2833#issuecomment-5974632478) on integration head `0d3cf151` proves **16.78% lower P50** and 16/16 unchanged quality. This focused PR is intended for independent review and merging; draft #2833 is the joint benchmark reference. These one-pair figures are approximate and cannot be added.

title: Fix combined CAD rotation order in exported GLBs
description: Fixes incorrect rotation of NEMA17 motor in exported GLBs when CAD X and Y rotations are combined, ensuring proper alignment of components in 3D space.
body:
The GLB exporter turns a NEMA17 the wrong way when CAD X and Y rotations are combined. In this rear-mounted RP2040 controller example, the old exporter leaves the PCB beside the motor and points the shaft toward the viewer. With the fix, the PCB aligns with the rear face, the shaft points away from the PCB, and the JST connector faces the viewer.

![NEMA17 and RP2040 controller before and after the rotation fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/b001b3c/tests/repro/__snapshots__/repro14-composed-cad-rotation.snap.png)

Both views use the same real models, CAD placement and camera. The PCB is from `imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller` 1.0.42, and the motor is modelprinter's `nema17_jstph6`. Compressed local GLBs keep the test independent of modelcdn and future releases. The left view is a frozen render from the unfixed exporter; the right view is rendered from the current code on every test run.

- [Repro commit](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/commit/140102c): readable Circuit JSON fixture, asset provenance, annotated before/after snapshot, actual shaft-tip/PCB-face measurements, point/normal probes, and CI uploads of visual diffs.
- [Fix commit](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/commit/368928e): only production rotation order and frame documentation. Apply circuit Z, then Y, then X, matching intrinsic `THREE.Euler(..., "XYZ")`; positions and normals use the same order.
- The final workflow commit provides package previews for downstream validation.

Run `bun test tests/repro/repro14-composed-cad-rotation.test.ts tests/unit/cad-rotation-composed.test.ts` at the repro and fix commits to see red/green behavior. The real-model PNG fails without the fix with a 13% diff against the existing 5% tolerance. The fixed geometry also puts the 24 mm shaft tip on the correct side and preserves the 6 mm PCB-to-rear-face gap. All 183 local tests pass. All CI checks are green, including the full suite, Playwright, TypeScript, formatting and preview publish. The real-model snapshot also passes on Linux.

title: Reduce routing allocations while preserving main search behavior
description: The independent consumer dataset18 result verifies 6.01 lower P50 runtime and 10.78 lower summed elapsed for the isolated port-tiny group against autorouter main ef0ad74. Both revisions complete and pass relaxed DRC on all 16 samples with zero issuestimeouts; all exported non-timing metrics and budgets match. Actual checkout SHAs and raw artifact bytes were independently verified. This measures the consumers historical performance backport and its integration; this main-targeted dependency PR retains its own baseline enginerouting behavior. The result does not establish an identical percentage for this dependency main branch. Repeated port-graph solves rebuild topology-sized workspaces, endpoint sets, and temporary intersection geometry. Reuse these allocations and index congested ports by boundary while preserving candidate costs, search order, and routing budgets. This ports the performance changes from 225 onto current main (0750fa4). Mains blocker-reachability fixes and benchmark dataset fallback remain intact. The routing-policy commits on 211 are excluded.
body:
The independent [consumer dataset18 result](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2834#issuecomment-5974302703) verifies **6.01% lower P50 runtime** and **10.78% lower summed elapsed** for the isolated port-tiny group against autorouter main `ef0ad74`. Both revisions complete and pass relaxed DRC on all 16 samples with zero issues/timeouts; all exported non-timing metrics and budgets match. Actual checkout SHAs and raw artifact bytes were independently verified.

This measures the consumer’s historical performance backport and its integration; this main-targeted dependency PR retains its own baseline engine/routing behavior. The result does not establish an identical percentage for this dependency main branch.

Repeated port-graph solves rebuild topology-sized workspaces, endpoint sets, and temporary intersection geometry. Reuse these allocations and index congested ports by boundary while preserving candidate costs, search order, and routing budgets.

This ports the performance changes from #225 onto current `main` (`0750fa4`). Main's blocker-reachability fixes and benchmark dataset fallback remain intact. The routing-policy commits on #211 are excluded.

Changes:
- Index boundary ports in source order and retain nearest-port selection.
- Cache candidate hop IDs, retain compact typed-array checks, share read-only analysis arrays, and allocate endpoint sets only for route terminals.
- Reuse intersection-count scratch storage, skip geometry for empty regions, and reject candidates already dominated by the existing cost lower bound.
- Keep candidate scoring on topology angles while preserving overridden geometry for inserting completed polygon segments. A regression covers separately supplied angle and boundary-coordinate arrays.
- Reuse one base-solver workspace between independent prepass routes. Reset reapplies initial assignments and rejects subclasses before mutation.

Validation against this main-based branch:
- GitHub CI passes all 143 tests across 61 files, including 1,160 assertions and the existing snapshot.
- TypeScript checking and the production Cosmos build pass.
- All eight committed historical SRJ18 port-graph inputs retain byte-identical serialized output, exact solve/failure flags, and exact iteration counts compared with current main. These inputs cover samples 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11.
- The PMP23595 reproduction retains the captured port-use counts and all 411 duplicated ports; reset regressions verify initial assignments and reject unsupported subclass resets.

Independent current-main consumer measurement: [tscircuit-autorouter #2834](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2834) isolates port indexes, kernel workspace reuse and lazy statistics, using the performance-only `4e2156904b1c3f2271dcc256021246faf811d641` backport on the existing `31459ce` dependency base. Its official result is linked above. This main-targeted PR is the corresponding integration on `0750fa4`, preserving that branch’s routing policies; the consumer deliberately retains its own baseline policies.

Inherited compact-hop incidence storage is already in the consumer baseline and is not credited to this change. Historical replay timings and the combined autorouter benchmark are diagnostic; they do not quantify this main branch’s independent speedup.

title: Fix landing-page autorouter loading and update dependencies

body:
Starting the landing-page autorouter currently resolves npm's latest version and downloads the solver through external CDNs. The primary CDN returned HTTP 500 during investigation, and routing has no visible running/completed state or solver-failure message.

Bundle a pinned, tested Pipeline7 solver into the web worker so routing starts without npm/CDN requests. Show routing progress, completion, and failed-solver errors. Validation:
- Production build and TypeScript check pass.
- All 5 tests pass, including a new worker regression that routes the actual landing fixture with runtime fetch disabled and checks serializable snapshots and routed traces.
- Chromium against the production build routes the default board into 94 traces with external requests blocked and no page errors.
- A deliberately out-of-bounds connection displays the solver's error on the page.

The solver adds approximately 2.6 MB to the minified worker chunk, loaded when routing starts. Its transitive graphics-debug package declares a React 18 peer; the application uses React 19, and the production worker and browser checks pass.

title: Reduce DRC setup, connectivity and via-site query overhead
description: Reduces overhead in DRC setup and connectivity checks by optimizing route evaluations and caching mechanisms, leading to improved performance in autorouting processes.
body:
The independent [consumer dataset18 result](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2836#issuecomment-5974351175) verifies **6.31% lower P50 runtime** and **3.08% lower summed elapsed** for the isolated repair group against autorouter main `ef0ad74`. Both revisions complete and pass relaxed DRC on all 16 samples with zero issues/timeouts; all exported non-timing metrics and budgets match. Actual checkout SHAs and raw artifact bytes were independently verified.

This measures the consumer’s historical performance backport and its integration; this main-targeted dependency PR retains its own baseline engine/routing behavior. The result does not establish an identical percentage for this dependency main branch.

Global repair repeatedly prepares DRC context, compares the same nets and recollects every route's vias during movement attempts. This change removes that work while preserving candidate ordering, geometry, scoring, ownership IDs and DRC rules.

- Add an explicit routes-only evaluator mode for callbacks that construct their own exact DRC context. Default and dynamically changed evaluator modes retain their existing inputs.
- Reuse ordered route/obstacle net decisions only within one synchronous force call, with bounded caches. Later calls observe input mutations.
- Resolve a live via site using the existing collector on the target route and routes with the same root connection. Restore original route indices and ordering, retaining the original point-overlap and radial epsilon checks. Each lookup observes current geometry and roots.

The consumer backport is `5ec441040f04f40715051af23987bd6dde72c6c8`; this main-targeted PR is `ca0bbf133ca9ec8c8af48e12eba614261423ea57`. Each version retains its own collector's existing layer semantics.

Validation: the complete historical suite passes 110 tests / 28,834 assertions; the main-branch suite passes 104 tests / 18,676 assertions. Typechecks pass, including the upstream USB fixture. The ordered via-site oracle covers 160 generated cases, epsilon boundaries, aliases, sparse inputs, stale descriptors, live geometry/root edits and layer metadata. Independent review found no semantic issue.

Captured native repair comparisons use three alternating measured pairs and one warmup per variant. Root-scoped via collection alone reduces the historical median **15.596 → 11.896 seconds (23.73%)** and the upstream median **18.153 → 12.775 seconds (29.63%)**. All eight runs per version retain exact routes, iterations, stats and intermediate DRC snapshots. The versions are compared with their own baselines; these are isolated stage measurements, not official dataset18 results.

The checked-in `scripts/benchmark-repair-isolation.ts` and `benchmarks/repair-isolation/srj18-pipeline9-sample004.json.gz` reproduce the comparison with `--baseline` and `--optimized` module paths, revision guards, `--rounds 3 --warmups 1`, and `--connectivity-module` pointing to the consumer's native ConnectivityMap implementation. The fixture's original capture revision was not recorded. The runner rehydrates the canonical map fields; its fixture omits an unused legacy serialized alias.

Independent current-main consumer measurement: [tscircuit-autorouter #2836](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2836) contains only the repair dependency update and two explicit routes-only evaluator opt-ins. Its official result is linked above; it establishes the whole-dataset repair-group effect separately from the combined result below.

The autorouter consumes the historical backport in [PR #2833](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2833). The [official dataset18 benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2833#issuecomment-5973527033) on final consumer head `dc45cd7` proves P50 **85.981675 → 69.012793 seconds (19.735% less runtime)**. Both revisions complete and pass relaxed DRC on all 16 cases with zero issues/timeouts; all exported non-timing metrics and budgets match exactly. This is the combined consumer change, not an isolated repair contribution.

## Validation

title: Add helical gear schemas, dimensions, and model strings
description: Adds helical gear model strings and exported schemastypesdimension helpers for the companion renderer, reusing spur validation and introducing new properties for helical gears.
body:
Adds `helicalgear` model strings and exported schemas/types/dimension helpers for the companion renderer in https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/403. It reuses spur validation and transverse module/pressure-angle conventions, adds helix angle and handedness, and exposes normal dimensions plus signed twist.

Zero helix preserves spur dimensions. The gear specification documents parallel helical/spur pairing and the pitch/lead convention for a simplified worm-wheel layout, without claiming a hobbed or conjugate worm wheel.

Validation: `bun test` (15 passing), `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `bun run build`; CI and package preview also pass. Tests cover aliases/units/defaults, strict validation, both hands, zero helix, and worm pitch/lead relationships. Geometry and visual tests remain in jscad-electronics.

title: Add ModelPrinter specs for spur gears and worm screws
description: Add renderer-independent spur gear and worm gear model strings, strict parameter schemas, and dimension helpers for gear geometry specification through the existing API.
body:
Add renderer-independent `spurgear` and `wormgear` model strings, strict parameter schemas, and dimension helpers so callers can specify gear geometry through the existing `mp.string(...).json()` API.

For example, `spurgear24_m1mm_w5mm_bore5mm` specifies a 24-tooth involute spur gear, while `wormgear_m1mm_d10mm_l20mm_starts2_left` specifies a two-start left-hand worm screw. Parameters include pressure angle, tooth thinning/backlash, radial clearance, through bores, phase, optional spur hubs, and mesh resolution. Unknown tokens, duplicate aliases, malformed numbers, and invalid tooth/root dimensions fail validation.

`docs/gears.md` defines the pitch conventions and formulas. Spur module is transverse; worm module and pressure angle are axial. Worm screws use a simplified swept axial rack profile; conjugate worm wheels and manufacturing tooth-root details are outside this initial contract. Geometry and visual snapshots are implemented separately in jscad-electronics.

Companion renderer PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/402.

title: Add NEMA wire termination specs and named reference points

body:

Validation: 8 tests pass; typecheck, formatting and build pass. Tests cover custom body lengths, diagonal and negative wire angles, hidden references, string parsing, and conflicting or invalid parameters.

body:
Completed AM3352 routes now undergo bounded envelope compaction. Across all nine declared samples, total signal envelope area falls **7.72%**, from **7,317.67 to 6,752.55 mm²**. Individual improvements range from 0.15% to 18.43%; the unweighted mean is 6.86%.

The compactor preserves matched copper lengths, segment directions, tuning-bank shapes, differential pairs, endpoints, vias and fixed fanouts. Proposals must reduce the envelope and pass the existing geometry, clearance, skew and coupling validators before replacing the accepted route. Cancellation or an unsuccessful proposal retains the accepted routing.

The [measurement report](docs/envelope-compaction/README.md) includes per-sample area, full pad-to-pad bus/pair skew, runtime and reviewed completed snapshots. Compaction adds a median 10.07 seconds per sample (5.22–35.85 seconds); all nine finish within the existing 180-second routing budget.

Validation:
- Strict nine-sample benchmark: 9/9 solved; 47/47 signals each; zero native DRC errors; all bus/pair skew and coupling checks pass; inputs and all 161 fixed power dogbones unchanged.
- Completed snapshots independently revalidated by the standard exporter and visually inspected for every declared AM3352 sample and all four legacy DDR placements.
- TypeScript, formatting and isolated Node/browser/TypeScript package checks pass.
- Full suite: 298 tests across 109 files, 536,065 assertions, zero failures. New cases cover compaction, rotations/reflections, immutable copper, curve preservation and cancellation.

title: fix: preserve accepted routes when envelope optimization is interrupted
description: Preserves accepted routing results during interruptions in the envelope optimization process, ensuring that incomplete optimizations do not overwrite valid outputs.
body:
Once the pipeline finishes routing, matching, package coupling and escape attachment, it keeps a private accepted copy before entering optional envelope optimization. `tryFinalAcceptance()` restores that copy on iteration exhaustion or an explicit stop. Optimizer exceptions also preserve it. A mutable, incomplete optimization candidate cannot replace the accepted output, and unfinished routing still fails.

This introduces the safe optimization lifecycle; the default hook does no geometry work. The separate envelope PR supplies the optimizer. Stacked on #31 for nine-case benchmark coverage.

Validation: **287 tests pass**, including real-route explicit-stop and iteration-budget tests, native DRC/skew checks after restoration, optimizer failure and unfinished-route rejection. Typecheck, formatting, package build and isolated consumers pass. **9/9 benchmark samples pass**, 47/47 signals each with native DRC, configured skew, coupling and unchanged fixed power; all copper metrics match the preceding benchmark. Complete-CA runtime: **103.937 s** (113.002 s in the preceding run; normal machine/load variation).

[Per-case measurements and all nine inspected routed snapshots](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/4009d9181a9a3b35a4ee09bfe8d4c97b24ddc618/docs/optimization-final-acceptance.md). Full DDR absolute-length compliance remains a separate board requirement.

description: Adding the complete 24-signal addresscontrolclock timing bus to the existing powered AM3352 inner-layers fixture exhausts v0.0.15s 800,000-iteration budget. The unchanged fixture routes all 47 signals in 36.658 s; adding only that bus fails in route_shared_layers after 114.394 s.
body:
Adding the complete 24-signal address/control/clock timing bus to the existing powered AM3352 `inner-layers` fixture exhausts v0.0.15's 800,000-iteration budget. The unchanged fixture routes all 47 signals in 36.658 s; adding only that bus fails in `route_shared_layers` after 114.394 s.

## Visual reproduction

![Exact reproduction input: two timing buses versus three; airwires are not routed copper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/9a636335139f15cf7995a13e632371f61604bba5/docs/am3352-ca-input.svg)

Requested input diagnostic: the cyan lines show the additional CA/clock bus. Pads, endpoints and fixed power escapes are identical. These straight signal lines are **airwires**, not a successful route. The three-bus case has no completed routed output. Regenerate with `bun scripts/snapshot-am3352-ca-input.ts`.

For comparison, the successfully validated two-bus baseline is:

![Completed two-bus baseline on inner1 and inner2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/9a636335139f15cf7995a13e632371f61604bba5/docs/routed-am3352-placements/inner-layers-solved.png)

**Configuration clarification:** upstream is a valid partial router benchmark, but it is incomplete as a DDR compliance test: it omits CA-to-clock group matching and absolute-length limits. The SBC's three timing groups are more complete; its current copper still fails timing. Neither is a verified compliant DDR board. Matching CK to CK# alone does not match address/control timing to the clock. The SBC's 0.635 mm CA/clock bound is a conservative single-load application of TI's topology-specific rules; see the [detailed constraint comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/9a636335139f15cf7995a13e632371f61604bba5/docs/am3352-complete-ca-reproduction.md#which-configuration-is-correct).

The diagnostic exporter was typechecked and visually inspected. Five fixture/snapshot-guard tests passed (24 assertions). Routing code, constraint values, and the previously measured benchmark results are unchanged.


This adds a standalone reproduction and fixture-contract tests. Pads, signal identities, both byte buses, all three differential pairs, layer restrictions, and 161 immutable FanoutSolver power dogbones remain identical. The new bus requests 0.635 mm skew on inner1/inner2. The runner checks native copper/connectivity, pair coupling, and all three pad-to-pad bus skews; it exits nonzero for a failure, timeout, or invalid completed route. Production routing code is unchanged.

```sh
bun scripts/repro-am3352-ca-bus.ts --timeout-seconds 120 --output /tmp/am3352-ca-repro.json
```

Validation:
- Reproduction: baseline passes; added CA bus fails at 800,000 iterations (exit 1). Independently reproduced at the same iteration limit.
- `./benchmark.sh --timeout-seconds 120 --require-all-solved`: **8/8 pass**, 47/47 signals each, native DRC and existing matching pass, fixed power copper preserved.
- Per-bus total copper skew: BYTE0/BYTE1 = **0.635/0.635 mm in every sample**; all three pair skews ≤0.127 mm. Solver runtimes 18.949–83.875 s. [Full per-sample measurements and reproduction details](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/repro/am3352-complete-ca-bus/docs/am3352-complete-ca-reproduction.md).
- Default 60 s benchmark: 6/8 here; the two timeouts were not counted as passes.
- Typecheck and seven focused fixture/output/snapshot tests pass (33 assertions).

The original benchmark does not constrain CA/clock group skew or TI absolute lengths. This reproduction is not full DDR electrical signoff. Our SBC trials also omitted fixed power escapes: removing only those escapes from the original inner-layer fixture independently times out at 120 s, so those trials were not an equivalent benchmark comparison.

All eight existing successful routed images were individually inspected. These show the original two-bus baseline. The explicitly requested input diagnostic above is separately labeled; it is not counted as a routed artifact:

body:
Length matching no longer forces an entire bus onto one carrier layer. A 24-signal address/clock matching group previously overfilled its preferred layer and failed; the pipeline now allocates its members across allowed layers while matching their total copper lengths globally. Differential partners still share a carrier layer, and existing fanouts remain immutable.

Small buses retain co-location as an initial routing preference when the stack and handoffs permit it; retries may split them. Explicit `allowedLayers` remain hard constraints. Multilayer groups use the general routing/matching path rather than the specialized same-layer bus path. No new public props or board-specific routing logic are introduced.

Independent-lane tuning also rejects new returns into its own terminal via land, preventing a copper shortcut found by native self-short checks. The existing coupled-pair correction path is preserved. Snapshot export retains route data rather than all completed search caches.

### Routed review image

![47/47 routed, matching buses across inner1/inner2/bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/fix/multilayer-matching-groups/docs/routed-am3352-multilayer/core-multilayer-solved.png)

[Measurement report and snapshot guide](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/fix/multilayer-matching-groups/docs/routed-am3352-multilayer/README.md) · [Eight powered placement snapshots](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/fix/multilayer-matching-groups/docs/routed-am3352-placements/README.md)

The expanded core input routes 47/47 signals in 16.424s locally, using inner1=15, inner2=22, bottom=10. Native copper DRC, bus/pair length matching and pair-coupling measurements pass. Byte skew is ≤0.635mm, address/clock skew ≤2.54mm and pair skew ≤0.127mm, measured over total copper.

**Remaining core quality limitation:** this expanded result totals 1,767.185mm of planar copper, above core's existing 1,550mm compactness ceiling; max/mean detour is 2.063/1.739 versus the 2.05/1.55 ceilings. This PR fixes the routing failure; it does not relax that ceiling or claim that the full core integration test or electrical DDR signoff passes.

### Validation

- 280 tests pass, including immutable mixed-layer fanout handoffs, global matching, pair layer identity, the actual expanded core input, native wire/via copper DRC, and independent-lane via clearance.
- Type checking, formatting, build, and isolated Node/browser/TypeScript package consumers pass.

The eight powered placement cases use their existing FanoutSolver combined-copper DRC validator. The expanded core input additionally runs published `@tscircuit/checks` self-short and overlap checks with materialized via lands. These validation scopes are distinct; the existing paired terminal correction path is not broadened here.

Final isolated benchmark: **8/8**, all 47/47 connected, fixed power preserved, existing combined-copper DRC and total-copper matching passed. Route times: control 12.178s, right 11.878s, left 16.165s, above 24.613s, inner-layers 22.548s, inner-layers-right 28.706s, inner-layers-left 39.298s, inner-layers-above 50.063s.

### CI status

All **280 tests** pass on standard Ubuntu, including the expanded core/native copper DRC regression. Formatting, type checking, package consumers, and preview build also pass.

The 60s Ubuntu benchmark remains red: inner-layers-left and inner-layers-above timed out. This workflow already fails on `main` ([baseline run](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/37147207215)): inner-layers-left took 57.922s and inner-layers-above timed out. No timeout or quality gate is relaxed. The local final run passes all eight placements in 11.878–50.063s; its validated images are unchanged from the existing gallery. Keeping the PR draft for routing review while the shared benchmark performance limitation remains.

body:
Stacked on #28; base is `repro/am3352-complete-ca-bus`.

Adding the complete 24-signal CA/clock timing bus previously exhausted 800,000 iterations. This change completes all **47 signals on inner1/inner2** in **117.507 s / 72,455 iterations**, with all three timing groups and all three differential pairs independently validated. Native copper DRC, connectivity, exterior coupling, input immutability and all 161 fixed power dogbones pass.
