The shared-layer search now continues ordinary-lane negotiation before committing a nearly complete assignment to via-site repair. Folded tuning gets a bounded allowance per lane, retains completed ordinary corrections, and considers larger deficits first. Multi-bus matching can explore wider interior banks; single-bus matching keeps its established width choices. No fixture-specific routes, moved terminals or relaxed geometry/timing constraints are used.

| Complete-CA check | Measured result |
| --- | --- |
| BYTE0 / BYTE1 / CA-clock skew | 0.635 / 0.635 / 0.635 mm (within existing floating-point epsilon) |
| DQS0 / DQS1 / CK pair skew | 0.020663 / 0.127000 / 0.072830 mm |
| Native combined DRC | Pass: 208 traces, 53,383 segments, 255 vias |
| Complete connectivity / exterior coupling / immutable power | Pass |

**This fixes the reproduction, not full SBC DDR compliance.** CA/clock lengths are 74.970–75.605 mm, exceeding the SBC's 63.5 mm absolute ceiling. Absolute limits and board electrical validation remain outstanding; existing SBC copper is preserved.

Validation:
- **282 tests pass**, including two physical-pocket regressions that fail with the original tuner and a guard preventing unfinished outputs from reaching the image exporter.
- Typecheck, formatting, package build and isolated Node/browser/TypeScript consumers pass.
- `./benchmark.sh --timeout-seconds 120 --require-all-solved`: **8/8 pass**, each 47/47 connected, native DRC and configured matching/coupling pass; runtimes **23.439–82.101 s**. BYTE0/BYTE1 skews are 0.635/0.635 mm in every case; all pair skews ≤0.127 mm.
- Fresh complete-CA and all eight original placement snapshots passed export guards and were individually inspected. [Per-case runtimes, skews, all eight snapshots and full JSON reports](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/d260c5b4e3d0949acd9a2b1c0eb2f9763743fc89/docs/routed-am3352-complete-ca/README.md).
- CI now requires the complete-CA reproduction. The original placement deadline increases from 60 to 120 s because the unmodified parent already times out on slower runners; complete-CA gets 180 s. No acceptance check is removed.

Reproduce: `bun scripts/repro-am3352-ca-bus.ts --timeout-seconds 180`. Export the validated image with `bun scripts/snapshot-am3352-ca-routed.ts`.

title: Let pver record published versions on main
description: Allows the pver tool to record published versions directly on the main branch using the GITHUB_TOKEN, eliminating the need for a separate bot-token version PR and auto-merge steps, while ensuring versioning remains serialized and accurate for future releases.
body:
The solver publishes successfully, then fails to record its version because the bot token cannot push the version PR (403). The stale manifest eventually prevents subsequent releases.

Let `pver release` push its existing version commit to main using the repository-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: write`. Remove the separate bot-token version PR and auto-merge steps. Token-originated pushes do not trigger another release workflow; publication remains serialized. Record already-published 0.0.13 as the baseline so the next release starts at the correct version. Main has no branch protection or rules preventing this push.

Validation: actionlint passes. Inspected published pver 0.0.43: its default release includes push-main, commits the manifest before tagging/publication, rebases on remote main, and performs a normal push after publication. Verified 0.0.13 is available from jscdn and contains the merged routing fix. No package publication or production workflow execution was performed for this PR.

Core consumes the published package in https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4345. Matching plop template changes: https://github.com/tscircuit/plop/pull/32.

Allocate tuning-bank space according to buspair demand, use dense curves in the narrower banks, and slide unconstrained control segments inward after matching. body:
Two-layer bus routing reserved equally wide tuning lanes for control signals that did not need matching, pushing the outer traces far from the chips. Allocate tuning-bank space according to bus/pair demand, use dense curves in the narrower banks, and slide unconstrained control segments inward after matching.

Across the four powered AM3352 placements, the combined signal bounding-box area falls **29.4%** (4,981.89 → 3,516.38 mm²), with every placement improving:

| RAM position | Before → after | Reduction | Routing time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Below | 474.66 → 468.31 mm² | 1.3% | 23.01s |
| Right | 908.32 → 880.43 mm² | 3.1% | 27.80s |
| Left | 1,381.39 → 983.29 mm² | 28.8% | 37.72s |
| Above | 2,217.52 → 1,184.36 mm² | 46.6% | 48.48s |

Both mechanisms use geometry and existing constraints; there are no board names, pad mappings, coordinates, or saved routes in the implementation. Pairs retain joint tuning and coupling. The control pass excludes buses, pairs, curves and fixed copper; it preserves endpoints and directions and rejects length increases, expanded bounds, collisions and self-touching. Existing wider banks remain fallbacks.

Validation:

- Local `./benchmark.sh --require-all-solved`: all 8 powered placements complete, with 47/47 signals and native combined DRC, pad-to-pad byte/pair matching, pair coupling, self-clearance, and angle checks passing. All 161 fixed VCC/GND dogbones remain unchanged; restricted carriers use only inner1/inner2.
- Rotation/reflection tests cover compact banks and control compaction with fixed obstacles.
- 277 tests pass; typecheck, format check and isolated Node/browser/TypeScript package validation pass.
- Refreshed routed snapshots pass the all-sample validation gate and were visually inspected. The report includes full signal bounds, middle-region envelopes and clearance-aware unoccupied area.

See `docs/routed-am3352-placements/README.md` for the eight-sample results and routed images, and `two-layer-envelope-comparison.json` for the comparison against the merged #21 baseline.

CI: tests, typecheck, formatting, package validation and previews pass. The Ubuntu benchmark times out on the two-layer left/above placements. This also occurs on the base commit before these changes ([main benchmark log](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/37141990731)); the PR does not increase the 60-second limit. Local routing times above are measured on macOS arm64 with Bun 1.3.2.

title: Fix stale release version baseline to unblock publishing
description: Updates the version in package.json from 0.0.1 to 0.0.12 to reflect the latest published version and unblock the publishing process.
body:
The publication after #23 failed before publishing: the manifest still declares 0.0.1, while tags already exist through v0.0.12. `pver` only skips ten occupied versions and stops at v0.0.12.

Record the latest successfully published version, 0.0.12, in package.json. On merge, the publisher can select 0.0.13 and release the already-merged routing fix for core PR https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4345. No runtime changes or tag deletion.

Verified the publish failure log and existing v0.0.12 tag. The merged routing fix already passed typecheck, package validation, and formatting; this change only corrects release metadata. Earlier publishing succeeded but the subsequent bot version-recording PR failed with 403, leaving this stale baseline.

title: Sync model URLs and automate daily library updates
description: Synchronizes model URLs with explicit parameter inputs and automates daily updates for model libraries, ensuring that the application reflects the latest changes and maintains user configurations accurately.
body:
Parameter edits previously left the address bar pointing at the original configuration. Keep the URL synchronized with explicit parameter inputs, model selection, applied strings, and resets so refreshes and copied links restore the same model. This includes JSON-only placement and footprint overrides, and uses replaceState to avoid adding a history entry for every edit.

Add a daily npm update workflow at 10:23 UTC, plus manual dispatch. It updates Footprinter, ModelPrinter, and jscad-electronics together with their lockfile and published source commits, regenerates catalogs, and runs build/unit/browser checks before pushing a commit to main. Vercel's existing Git integration deploys that commit; unchanged releases do nothing and failed checks prevent publication.

The live update trial found that ModelPrinter 0.0.8 adds helicalgear, which the previous catalog could not load. Include the current ModelPrinter/jscad-electronics updates and the helical gear schema, controls, string serialization, and preview adapter so those releases work. Catalog assertions now follow installed versions instead of fixed version/count literals.

Validation:
- 170 unit tests, including update planning and helical gear generation/string round-trips.
- All 13 browser tests pass against the production build, including refresh, directly shared addresses, resets, history length, JSON-only settings, footprint overrides, and helical gear edits.
- Live npm update followed by an unchanged-version run.
- Production build, TypeScript, and actionlint.

title: Add GLB and STEP downloads to model pages
description: Adds a Download dropdown beside Share on every model and footprint configuration page, with GLB and STEP options that export the current preview geometry. Downloads wait for valid, up-to-date geometry and support keyboard navigation, mobile layouts, progress, cancellation on edits, and error feedback.
body:
Adds a Download dropdown beside Share on every model and footprint configuration page, with GLB and STEP options that export the current preview geometry. Downloads wait for valid, up-to-date geometry and support keyboard navigation, mobile layouts, progress, cancellation on edits, and error feedback.

GLB preserves colors and converts Z-up millimeters to Y-up meters. STEP exports colored, faceted AP214 geometry in millimeters in a separate worker; it does not reconstruct analytic curves or a parametric CAD history. Exporters exclude the viewer's grid and lighting.

Validation:
- 165 unit tests, including independent OpenCascade STEP imports checking dimensions, placement, colors, and actual gear/motor models.
- Detailed default bolt and worm models export within the download time budget.
- Browser tests cover real GLB/STEP downloads, GLB dimensions after edits, invalid parameters, keyboard controls, and mobile footprint downloads.
- TypeScript and production build.

body:
Create a searchable workbench for configuring ModelPrinter and Footprinter functions with live previews. The catalog includes all six current ModelPrinter functions (including spur gears and multi-start worm screws) and all 104 Footprinter functions.

- Generate parameter controls from the model schemas and checked-in Footprinter schema metadata; recompute dependent defaults when presets change.
- Render real geometry in a cancellable worker with interactive Three.js views and precise footprint SVG previews. Invalid inputs retain the last valid preview.
- Provide editable DSL, TypeScript/JSX exports, parameter JSON, and configuration share links. Use exact typed overrides when the footprint string grammar cannot express an option.
- Add responsive mobile panels, catalog regeneration tooling, CI, setup documentation, and Vercel build configuration.

Validation: 145 unit tests cover catalog coverage, schema inputs, serialization, presets, and actual generated geometry. Seven browser tests cover live gear changes, footprint pads, boolean overrides, DSL imports, NEMA presets, invalid-input recovery, sharing, and mobile controls. Typecheck and production build pass.

Repository provisioned through tscircuit/create-repo#80. Connecting a hosting project and assigning models.tscircuit.com remains a deployment step.
